# ================================================================================

R-131 · ONE ZOD SCHEMA PER BOUNDARY, DEFINED IN `src/lib/validation.ts` OR ITS MODULE
MUST: Every route, tRPC procedure, job payload, webhook body, bot command
argument, WS/SSE message, and provider response has a schema. Handlers receive
parsed data only.
VERIFY: A test posts malformed bodies to every endpoint and asserts a 4xx with a
stable error code, never a 500.

R-132 · STRICT SCHEMAS: UNKNOWN KEYS REJECTED
MUST: Use `.strict()` on inbound schemas so unexpected fields are rejected, not
silently dropped — except where a provider explicitly may add fields, where the
schema is `.passthrough()` and the extra data is never used.
PREVENTS: Mass-assignment and hidden parameter injection.

R-133 · SOLANA ADDRESSES ARE VALIDATED STRUCTURALLY AND SEMANTICALLY
MUST: Validate base58, length, and that it parses to a valid 32-byte public key;
for mints, verify the account exists, is owned by a supported token program, and
matches the expected type before use.
NEVER: Accept an address because it "looks like" one.
VERIFY: Tests reject: wrong length, invalid base58 chars, curve-invalid keys,
a system account passed as a mint, and a token account passed as a mint.

R-134 · ENUMS AND MODES ARE ALLOWLISTS
MUST: Sides, tiers, networks, statuses, order types, and flags are validated
against explicit enums. Unknown value ⇒ reject.

R-135 · SIZE LIMITS ON EVERYTHING
MUST: Bound request body size, array lengths, string lengths, page sizes, batch
sizes, webhook payload size, and file uploads. Every unbounded input is a DoS.
VERIFY: A test sends an oversized payload and asserts rejection before parsing
cost is incurred.

R-136 · NO REGEX ON UNTRUSTED INPUT WITHOUT ReDoS REVIEW
MUST: Avoid nested quantifiers and catastrophic backtracking; prefer parsers or
bounded character-class checks; length-limit before matching.

R-137 · NO RAW SQL WITH INTERPOLATION
MUST: Use Drizzle's query builder or parameterized `sql` templates. Never build
SQL by string concatenation, ever, including in scripts and migrations tooling.
VERIFY: `grep -rnE "sql\.raw|\\\$\{.*\}.*(SELECT|INSERT|UPDATE|DELETE)" src/`
returns zero results.

R-138 · NO USER INPUT IN FILE PATHS, SHELL COMMANDS, OR URLS
MUST: Never pass user-controlled data to `fs` paths, `exec`, `spawn`, or a URL
that the server will fetch. Where a fetch target is configurable, use an
allowlist (`ALLOWED_NETWORK_HOSTS`) and reject private/link-local addresses.
PREVENTS: Path traversal, command injection, and SSRF into cloud metadata.

R-139 · SANITIZE ON OUTPUT, ENCODE PER CONTEXT
MUST: Escape for the destination — HTML, Telegram markdown/HTML, log JSON, CSV
(prevent formula injection), and shell. Token names and symbols are hostile input
and are always escaped and length-limited before display.
PREVENTS: XSS and chat-formatting attacks delivered through token metadata.

R-140 · NORMALIZE BEFORE COMPARING
MUST: Normalize case, Unicode (NFC), and whitespace before comparing identifiers
such as emails and usernames; compare addresses byte-wise after decoding, never
by case-insensitive string equality.

R-141 · REJECT AMBIGUOUS OR DUPLICATE PARAMETERS
MUST: Duplicate query params, conflicting body fields, or an amount specified in
two units ⇒ reject with a stable error code. Never pick one silently.

R-142 · VALIDATE PROVIDER RESPONSES AS HOSTILE
MUST: Apply R-084 to Jupiter, Helius, PumpPortal, RugCheck, DexScreener, Birdeye,
Moralis, Telegram, and RPC responses. A provider compromise or bug must not
become a fund loss.
DO: Additionally sanity-check semantic invariants: output mint equals the
requested mint, route amounts are within tolerance of the quote, account keys
include the expected signer, no unexpected instruction targets a token account.

R-143 · NEVER EXECUTE PROVIDER-SUPPLIED INSTRUCTIONS BLINDLY
MUST: Before signing any transaction assembled from provider data, decode and
assert: fee payer is the expected wallet, no instruction transfers SOL or tokens
to an address outside the expected set, no `setAuthority`/`closeAccount`/
`approve` on user accounts unless explicitly intended, program IDs are on the
allowlist, and ALT accounts resolve to expected keys.
VERIFY: A test feeds a tampered swap response containing a drain instruction and
asserts the signer refuses.
PREVENTS: The highest-severity supply-chain attack against this design.

R-144 · IDS ARE OPAQUE AND UNGUESSABLE WHERE THEY GRANT ACCESS
MUST: Use UUIDv4/ULID (or the schema's defined type) for user-facing resource
IDs; never sequential integers in URLs for objects that carry authorization.

R-145 · NULL, UNDEFINED, AND EMPTY ARE DISTINCT AND HANDLED
MUST: Define, for every optional field, what missing means; never treat `0`,
`''`, or `false` as absent; never use `||` for defaulting on numeric or boolean
values (use `??` with an explicit branch).

# ================================================================================
# CHAPTER 13 — ERRORS AND FAILURE SEMANTICS
# ================================================================================

R-146 · STABLE ERROR CODES ONLY, ACROSS EVERY BOUNDARY
MUST: Clients (web, bot, API consumers) receive `{ code: 'ERR_DOMAIN_NNN',
message: <generic>, correlationId }`. Nothing else. Codes are registered in one
table (`src/lib/errors.ts`), never renumbered, never reused.
VERIFY: A test asserts no response body contains a stack trace, file path, table
name, hostname, IP, SQL fragment, or provider raw error.

R-147 · ERROR MESSAGES OBEY §1.7.5 ABSOLUTELY
MUST NOT: Emit to a user or an external system any message containing file
paths, hostnames, IPs, table/column names, stack traces, or the strings
"decrypt", "unwrap", "kek", "dek", "privateKey" (case-insensitive).
VERIFY: A CI test greps rendered error catalogs and a runtime test hits every
error branch, asserting the forbidden-pattern list never matches.

R-148 · DISTINGUISH THE FIVE FAILURE CLASSES
MUST: Classify every failure as: user error (4xx, do not retry), authorization
(4xx, log security event), validation (4xx), transient dependency (retryable with
backoff), or internal invariant violation (5xx, alert, never auto-retry a money
path). Behavior differs per class and is explicit in code.
PREVENTS: Retrying a non-idempotent failure and double-spending.

R-149 · NEVER RETRY A MONEY OPERATION WITHOUT AN IDEMPOTENCY GUARANTEE
MUST: Retry only when the operation is idempotent (R-012) or when you can prove
the prior attempt had no effect (e.g. the transaction was never submitted).
DO: For submitted transactions, resolve by querying the chain for the signature
before any resubmission decision.
PREVENTS: The double-buy that costs a user twice.

R-150 · ERRORS CARRY CORRELATION IDS AND CONTEXT — INTERNALLY ONLY
MUST: Internal error objects carry correlationId, userId, phase, operation, and
the provider's raw error under `diagnostic`, logged structurally; the external
surface carries only code + correlationId.

R-151 · NO ERROR IS DISCARDED
MUST: Every caught error is either handled with a defined recovery, converted to
a typed failure and returned, or logged and rethrown. Never both swallowed and
unlogged.

R-152 · INVARIANT VIOLATIONS HALT THE OPERATION AND ALERT
MUST: If an internal invariant fails (balance mismatch, unexpected state
transition, missing lot, signature for an unknown intent), stop that operation,
persist the evidence, raise a security/incident event, and alert. Do not attempt
to repair automatically.

R-153 · PARTIAL FAILURE IS AN EXPLICIT STATE
MUST: Every multi-step money operation defines and persists its intermediate
states (e.g. `signing`, `sent`, `confirmed`) so that a crash leaves a resolvable
record, and defines a resolver that reconciles unknown states against the chain.
NEVER: Leave a trade in a state that means "we do not know" without a resolver.

R-154 · TIMEOUTS ARE NOT FAILURES OF INTENT
MUST: A timeout on submission means unknown, not failed. Never mark a trade
failed on timeout; move to `unknown`/`resolving`, then determine ground truth
from the chain by signature.
PREVENTS: Telling a user their trade failed while it lands, then re-executing.

R-155 · USER-FACING FAILURE MESSAGES ARE ACTIONABLE AND HONEST
MUST: Map each code to a short, plain-language message that tells the user what
happened and what they can do, without internal detail and without false
certainty ("Trade may still be confirming — we'll update you" when unknown).
# ================================================================================
# CHAPTER 14 — LOGGING, OBSERVABILITY, AND AUDIT
# ================================================================================

R-156 · ONE LOGGER, STRUCTURED JSON, NO EXCEPTIONS
MUST: All logging goes through `src/lib/logger.ts` (Winston, JSON). No
`console.log`, `console.error`, `process.stdout.write`, or `print` anywhere in
committed code outside a declared CLI script.
VERIFY: `grep -rn "console\." src/ app/` returns zero results (lint rule
`no-console` enabled, error level).

R-157 · MANDATORY LOG FIELDS
MUST: Every log line includes: `ts` (ISO-8601 UTC), `level`, `event` (stable
snake_case name), `correlationId`, `env`, `network`, and `service`. Money events
add `userId`, `walletId`, `intentId`, `mint`, `amountBaseUnits`, `side`.
PREVENTS: Logs that cannot answer "what happened to this user's trade".

R-158 · NEVER LOG SECRETS, KEY MATERIAL, OR FULL PII
MUST NOT: Log private keys, seeds, KEK/DEK, tokens, cookies, auth headers,
webhook secrets, full emails, or raw Telegram init data. Redact by allowlist:
log only fields you explicitly chose to log.
DO: Use a serializer that drops unknown fields rather than one that redacts known
ones. Hash identifiers where correlation is needed without exposure.
VERIFY: A test passes an object containing every secret field name to the logger
and asserts none appear in the output; CI greps log samples for secret patterns.

R-159 · LOG EVERY SECURITY EVENT TO THE DATABASE
MUST: Failed auth, session revoke, ownership violation, rate-limit trip, invalid
webhook signature, flag denial, breaker trip, kill-switch change, admin action,
key operation, and anomalous amount are written to `auditLogs` /
`securityEvents` via `src/lib/security-logger.ts`, in addition to file logs.
VERIFY: Each event type has a test asserting the row is written with the right
type and without secrets.

R-160 · AUDIT LOGS ARE APPEND-ONLY AND TAMPER-EVIDENT
MUST: No application code path updates or deletes audit rows; the DB role used by
the app has no UPDATE/DELETE on those tables; where this document specifies hash
chaining, each row includes the previous row's hash and a verifier exists.
VERIFY: A test attempts an update/delete as the app role and asserts permission
denied; the chain verifier runs in CI against a seeded fixture.

R-161 · CORRELATION IDS PROPAGATE END TO END
MUST: Generate at entry (HTTP, webhook, bot update, cron), pass through job
payloads, signer requests, provider calls (as a header where supported), and
include in every log and every user-facing error.
VERIFY: A test traces one trade and asserts a single correlationId appears in
every stage's log line.

R-162 · LOG LEVELS HAVE MEANINGS AND ARE ENFORCED
MUST: `error` = action required or money affected; `warn` = degraded or
suspicious but handled; `info` = state transitions and money events; `debug` =
developer detail, disabled in production by `LOG_LEVEL`.
NEVER: Log at `error` for expected user mistakes (alert fatigue), or at `debug`
for a security event.

R-163 · NO UNBOUNDED LOG VOLUME
MUST: Rate-limit or sample high-frequency logs (websocket messages, price ticks,
polling), cap per-line size, and rotate/ship logs with a retention policy. Disk
full is an outage; log spam is a cost incident.
VERIFY: Rotation configured and tested; a load test shows bounded log growth.

R-164 · METRICS FOR EVERY CRITICAL PATH
MUST: Emit counters and histograms for: trades by state, signer requests and
rejections, provider latency and error rate per provider, queue depth and job
duration, rate-limit trips, breaker state, kill-switch state, RPC failures,
websocket reconnects, and end-to-end trade latency percentiles.
VERIFY: The P3.6 latency budgets (copy < 500ms p99, standard < 2s p99) are
measured from real data, not asserted.

R-165 · ALERTS ARE ACTIONABLE, ROUTED, AND TESTED
MUST: Every alert names the runbook that resolves it, has a threshold justified
by data, and has been fired at least once in a test to prove delivery.
NEVER: Add an alert with no runbook, or a runbook with no alert for a critical
failure.

R-166 · SILENCE IS NOT HEALTH (DEAD MAN'S RULE, D-055)
MUST: Every worker, subscription, and scheduled job emits a heartbeat; absence of
a heartbeat beyond a threshold alerts. The system must detect "the copy trader
stopped receiving webhooks" without a user reporting it.

R-167 · HEALTH CHECKS TELL THE TRUTH
MUST: `/api/health` reports real dependency state (DB, Redis, RPC, signer,
queue) with timeouts, and returns non-200 when a dependency required for trading
is unavailable. Never a static 200.
NEVER: Include secrets, versions of internal components, or detailed internal
topology in a public health response.

R-168 · KEEP AN IMMUTABLE RECORD OF EVERY MONEY EVENT
MUST: For each trade: intent, quote (with source and timestamp), built
transaction hash/summary, signature, submission attempts, confirmation status,
final on-chain result, fees paid, and resulting position/lot changes are all
persisted. Reconstruction must be possible without external services.

# ================================================================================
# CHAPTER 15 — SECRETS, KEY MATERIAL, AND CUSTODY
# The strictest chapter. A violation here is not a bug; it is a breach.
# ================================================================================

R-169 · SECRETS EXIST ONLY IN ENVIRONMENT OR SECRET STORAGE
MUST: Every value in D-014 is read from `process.env` (validated at boot, R-494)
or a secret manager. Never in source, tests, fixtures, seeds, comments, docs,
commit messages, issue text, screenshots, or chat.
VERIFY: §1.7.2 CI check (no string literal ≥ 32 chars outside the allowlist) plus
a secret scanner (gitleaks/trufflehog equivalent) on every commit and in CI.

R-170 · PRIVATE KEYS ARE NEVER PLAINTEXT AT REST
MUST: Wallet private keys are encrypted with a DEK; the DEK is wrapped by the KEK
(`MASTER_KEK` / KMS / Vault per this document); the KEK never touches the
database and never appears in application logs.
NEVER: Store a keypair JSON, mnemonic, or raw secret key in any table, file,
backup, or cache in plaintext.
VERIFY: A test inserts a wallet and asserts the stored bytes are not a valid
decodable keypair without the DEK; a DB dump is grepped for base58 patterns.

R-171 · THE APPLICATION NEVER HOLDS DECRYPTED KEY MATERIAL
MUST: Per CTL-100, decryption and signing happen inside the remote signer
boundary (D-045). The application sends a signing request and receives a signed
transaction or a rejection.
NEVER: Return key bytes across the boundary "for convenience", cache a decrypted
key, place it on a global, put it in a closure that outlives the request, or pass
it to a logger, serializer, error, or metric.
VERIFY: A code-level check asserts no export from the signer module returns a key
type; a test asserts the signer API surface exposes only sign/reject.

R-172 · KEY MATERIAL IS ZEROIZED AND SHORT-LIVED
MUST: Decrypted key material exists for the minimum time needed to sign, is held
in a buffer that is overwritten after use where the runtime allows, and is never
placed in a string (strings are immutable and unclearable).
DO: Disable core dumps for the signer process; do not attach a debugger to it in
production; exclude it from heap snapshots and APM object capture.

R-173 · THE SIGNER ENFORCES POLICY INDEPENDENTLY
MUST: The signer re-validates, on its own, every constraint that protects funds:
session validity and non-revocation, kill switch and flags, per-trade and daily
caps, allowlisted program IDs, expected fee payer, destination checks, slippage
bounds, and transaction shape (R-143). It must not trust the caller's assertion
that checks were done.
VERIFY: A test calls the signer directly with a revoked session and with a drain
instruction; both are rejected and logged.
PREVENTS: A compromised application host forcing bad trades (RISK-002).

R-174 · SIGNING IS RATE-LIMITED, LOGGED, AND ATTRIBUTED
MUST: Every signing request records who, what, why, correlationId, the resulting
signature or rejection reason, and counts against per-user and global limits.
Unattributable signing requests are refused.

R-175 · KEK/DEK LIFECYCLE IS IMPLEMENTED, NOT ASSUMED
MUST: Implement generation, wrapping, unwrapping, rotation, and revocation per
this document's key tables (`keyEncryptionKeys`, `keyStatusEnum`:
active|rotated|compromised), including re-wrapping on rotation and a documented,
tested procedure for the compromised path.
VERIFY: A rotation test proves old-ciphertext readability after rotation and that
a key marked compromised can no longer be used.

R-176 · CRYPTO PRIMITIVES ARE THE SPECIFIED ONES
MUST: Argon2id for passwords (DEF-004), AEAD (AES-256-GCM or specified
equivalent) with unique nonces for encryption, `crypto.randomBytes`/WebCrypto for
randomness, and constant-time comparison for secrets and MACs.
NEVER: `Math.random()` for anything security-relevant; ECB mode; a reused
IV/nonce; a homemade construction; a comparison with `===` on a token or MAC.
VERIFY: Tests assert nonce uniqueness across many encryptions and that timing
comparison helpers are used for all secret equality checks.

R-177 · SECRET ROTATION IS SUPPORTED FROM DAY ONE
MUST: Every secret can be rotated without a code change and without downtime
where P0.15 requires it: dual-read during rotation, versioned key IDs, documented
procedure, and a rehearsal recorded in VERIFICATION.md.

R-178 · NO SECRET CROSSES A PROCESS BOUNDARY IT DOES NOT NEED
MUST: Workers, the bot, the web app, and the signer receive only the secrets
their role requires. There is no single env file with everything shared by all
processes in production.

R-179 · NEVER ACCEPT KEY MATERIAL FROM A USER OVER AN INSECURE CHANNEL
MUST NOT: Ask for, accept, or process a private key or seed phrase via Telegram,
chat, email, a URL, a query parameter, or an unencrypted form field. If a user
sends one, do not store it, redact it from logs, warn them it is compromised, and
log a security event.

R-180 · WALLET RECOVERY MATERIAL IS TREATED AS KEY MATERIAL
MUST: Recovery exports (P2.6) are generated on demand, encrypted for the user,
never persisted in plaintext, rate-limited, audited, require re-authentication,
and are excluded from backups and logs.

R-181 · BACKUPS OF KEY MATERIAL ARE ENCRYPTED AND SEPARATELY KEYED
MUST: Database backups containing encrypted keys are themselves encrypted, with
the backup key stored separately from the KEK, and restore is tested (CHAPTER 42)
without ever exposing plaintext keys.

R-182 · NO SECRETS IN CLIENT-SIDE CODE OR PUBLIC CONFIG
MUST: Only `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` values reach the browser, and no `NEXT_PUBLIC_*`
variable may contain a secret. Review every one at every release.
VERIFY: A build-time check fails if a `NEXT_PUBLIC_` value matches a secret
pattern or if a server-only var appears in the client bundle.
PREVENTS: Publishing an RPC/API key to every visitor.

R-183 · NO SECRETS IN URLS, EVER
MUST NOT: Put tokens, keys, or session identifiers in query strings, path
segments, redirects, or webhook URLs beyond an unguessable path segment that is
treated as a secret and never logged.
PREVENTS: Leakage through logs, referrers, and browser history.

R-184 · THIRD-PARTY CODE NEVER RUNS IN THE SIGNER'S PROCESS
MUST: The signer has the minimum dependency set, no analytics, no APM agent that
captures arguments, no dynamic plugin loading, and no network access beyond what
signing requires.

R-185 · ASSUME COMPROMISE: LIMIT WHAT ONE KEY CAN DO
MUST: Per-wallet spending caps, session scoping, allowlisted programs, and
treasury separation (hot/cold, multisig, timelock per P2.7/P5.9) exist so that a
single compromised component cannot drain everything.

R-186 · SECURITY HOLDS ARE ENFORCED AT THE SIGNER
MUST: `userSecurityHolds` and revocations take effect at the signer within the
documented time bound, not merely in the UI or API layer.
VERIFY: A test places a hold mid-flight and asserts the next signature is refused.

R-187 · KEY OPERATIONS REQUIRE FRESH AUTHENTICATION
MUST: Wallet export, key rotation, session-limit increases, withdrawal address
changes, and admin key actions require re-authentication and, where specified,
multi-signature or a timelock.

R-188 · SECRETS ARE VALIDATED FOR STRENGTH AT BOOT
MUST: Refuse to start if a secret is missing, empty, a known default, shorter
than its minimum (e.g. `SESSION_SECRET_MIN_LENGTH`), or equal to an example
value from documentation.
VERIFY: Boot-time config validation test covers each case.

R-189 · COMPROMISE RESPONSE IS PRE-WRITTEN
MUST: `docs/runbooks/key-compromise.md` exists before mainnet and specifies:
kill switch engagement, key marking, rotation, user notification, funds
migration, evidence preservation, and post-incident review — with owners and
time bounds.

R-190 · NEVER DEMONSTRATE A SECURITY CONTROL BY DISABLING IT IN PRODUCTION
MUST: Prove controls in test or staging with fixtures. Never toggle a production
control to "show" that it works.
# ================================================================================
# CHAPTER 16 — AUTHENTICATION
# ================================================================================

R-191 · ONE AUTH SYSTEM, AS SPECIFIED
MUST: Better Auth with the Drizzle adapter, mapped to the `users` table per PART
II §1, plus Telegram Mini App `initData` verification. No second auth path, no
hand-rolled JWT, no "temporary" bypass, no debug login.
NEVER: Add an API key, header, or query parameter that authenticates a user
outside this system.

R-192 · PASSWORDS: ARGON2ID, PER DEF-004
MUST: Argon2id with the documented parameters, unique salt per password, never
truncated, never logged, never compared with `===`.
VERIFY: Inspect a stored hash to confirm the `$argon2id$` prefix and parameters;
a test asserts the same password yields different hashes.

R-193 · TELEGRAM initData IS CRYPTOGRAPHICALLY VERIFIED, ALWAYS
MUST: Verify the HMAC over the data-check-string with the bot token per
Telegram's specification, in constant time, and reject if `auth_date` is older
than the documented freshness window.
NEVER: Trust `user.id` from initData without a valid signature; never accept
initData from a query string on a GET that could be logged or replayed.
VERIFY: Tests reject: tampered field, wrong hash, replayed old `auth_date`,
missing hash, and an initData signed by a different bot token.

R-194 · WEBHOOK AUTHENTICITY IS MANDATORY (DEF-001)
MUST: Verify `X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token` against `TELEGRAM_BOT_SECRET` in
constant time on every update; verify Helius webhook authentication per its
documented mechanism; reject unauthenticated calls with 401 and a security event,
before parsing the body.
NEVER: Process an update because it "looks like" Telegram's shape.

R-195 · SESSIONS ARE SERVER-SIDE, REVOCABLE, AND SHORT
MUST: Auth sessions are stored in the database (`session` table), validated on
every request against the store (not only a signed cookie), have an absolute and
an idle expiry, and are immediately invalidated on logout, password change, or
revocation.
VERIFY: A test revokes a session and asserts the very next request fails.

R-196 · COOKIES ARE HARDENED
MUST: `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Lax` or `Strict` as specified, `Path=/`,
host-only, with a `__Host-` prefix where applicable, and a short max-age.
NEVER: Store any token in `localStorage` or `sessionStorage`.

R-197 · SESSION FIXATION AND ROTATION
MUST: Issue a new session identifier on every privilege change: login, tier
upgrade, password change, 2FA change, admin elevation. Never reuse the
pre-authentication identifier.

R-198 · CSRF PROTECTION ON EVERY STATE-CHANGING REQUEST
MUST: `src/middleware/csrf.ts` protects all non-GET routes reachable by a
browser; token mismatch ⇒ 403 + security event. Verify origin/referer as a second
signal. Exempt only endpoints authenticated by a non-cookie mechanism, explicitly
listed.
VERIFY: A test posts without a token and asserts 403.

R-199 · AUTH ENDPOINTS ARE RATE-LIMITED, FAIL-CLOSED
MUST: Registration, login, password reset, email verification, initData exchange,
and session refresh are rate limited per IP and per account, backed by Redis, and
deny when Redis is unavailable (R-014).
VERIFY: A test exceeds the threshold and asserts denial; a second test kills
Redis and asserts denial rather than allowance.

R-200 · NO USER ENUMERATION, NO TIMING ORACLE
MUST: Identical responses and comparable timing for "unknown account" and "wrong
password"; generic messages; the same rate limit for both.

R-201 · EMAIL VERIFICATION AND RESET TOKENS ARE SINGLE-USE, SHORT-LIVED, HASHED
MUST: Store only a hash of the token, expire within the documented window,
invalidate on use, invalidate all outstanding tokens on password change, and
never include the token in a log or a redirect that is logged.

R-202 · TELEGRAM IDENTITY BINDING IS EXPLICIT AND ONE-WAY-SAFE
MUST: Linking a Telegram account to an existing user requires an authenticated
action from the existing account; a Telegram ID may map to exactly one user; a
re-bind requires re-authentication and is audit-logged.
PREVENTS: Account takeover by binding an attacker's Telegram to a victim.

R-203 · ADMIN ACCESS IS SEPARATE, EXPLICIT, AND MINIMAL
MUST: Admin capability is a server-side property checked on every admin route,
never inferred from a Telegram chat ID alone unless combined with a second
factor, and every admin action is audit-logged with the actor. Where P5.9
requires multi-signature, a single admin can never execute alone.

R-204 · NO AUTHENTICATION LOGIC IN THE CLIENT
MUST: The browser and the bot render based on server-provided state; every
decision is re-made server-side on each request. Hiding a control is not access
control.

# ================================================================================
# CHAPTER 17 — AUTHORIZATION, OWNERSHIP, AND TENANCY
# ================================================================================

R-205 · EVERY QUERY IS SCOPED TO THE AUTHENTICATED USER
MUST: Every read and write of user-owned data (wallets, sessions, trades,
positions, lots, settings, copy targets, notifications) includes the owner
predicate in the query itself, not as a post-fetch check.
NEVER: `findById(id)` then compare owner in application code as the only control.
VERIFY: A test authenticates as user A and requests every user-scoped resource ID
belonging to user B; all return not-found/forbidden with a security event.
PREVENTS: IDOR — the most common web vulnerability, and here it means another
user's wallet.

R-206 · AUTHORIZATION IS CHECKED AT EVERY LAYER THAT CAN ACT
MUST: API route, tRPC procedure, service function, job handler, and signer each
independently verify authorization for the action they perform. A job that trades
must re-verify the session and ownership at execution time.
PREVENTS: A queued job executing after the user's authority was revoked.

R-207 · TIER AND LIMIT ENFORCEMENT IS SERVER-SIDE AND RE-EVALUATED
MUST: Tier (`tierEnum`) limits, trust tier restrictions (D-068), per-session
caps, and per-day caps are enforced on the server at the moment of action, from
the database, not from a client claim or a cached value older than its TTL.

R-208 · ALLOWLISTS, NOT DENYLISTS, FOR AUTHORIZATION
MUST: Permitted actions, programs, mints, hosts, origins, commands, and admin
operations are enumerated; anything absent is denied.
PREVENTS: A new capability defaulting to allowed.

R-209 · REVOCATION IS THE FASTEST PATH IN THE SYSTEM (SES-07)
MUST: Session revocation and the panic button take precedence over all other
work: they are never queued behind trading jobs, they propagate to workers and
the signer within the documented bound, they are durable, and they are effective
even if the app process is restarted mid-flight.
VERIFY: A test issues a revoke during an in-flight trade and asserts no signature
is produced afterward, measured against the documented time bound.

R-210 · REVOKED, EXPIRED, PAUSED, AND HELD STATES ALL DENY
MUST: Any trading session not in `active`, any user with a security hold, any
disabled flag, any engaged kill switch, or any tripped breaker denies the action
— checked together in one authorization function used by every caller.
NEVER: Implement these checks separately in each call site; one function, one
source of truth, tested exhaustively.

R-211 · ADMIN ACTIONS CANNOT TOUCH USER KEYS
MUST: No admin capability exists that exports, decrypts, or signs with a user's
key. Admin can halt, flag, and inspect metadata only.

R-212 · CROSS-USER AGGREGATES ARE EXPLICITLY AUTHORIZED
MUST: Analytics or leaderboard features expose only data the document authorizes,
aggregated and anonymized, never per-user balances or addresses without consent.

R-213 · CAPABILITY CHECKS ARE POSITIVE, NOT NEGATIVE
MUST: `if (canTrade(user, ctx)) { ... } else deny()` with `canTrade` returning
false on any error. Never `if (!isBanned) allow`.

R-214 · DELEGATED ACTIONS CARRY THE ORIGINAL PRINCIPAL
MUST: Copy trades, scheduled jobs, and bot-initiated actions record and enforce
the originating user's authority, never a service identity with broader rights.

R-215 · NO PRIVILEGE ESCALATION THROUGH DATA
MUST: A user can never set their own `tier`, flags, limits, admin status,
referral credit, or `isPaper` field through any input path. Those fields are
never accepted from a request body; they are set by server logic only.
VERIFY: A test posts each privileged field and asserts it is ignored and a
security event is recorded.

# ================================================================================
# CHAPTER 18 — RATE LIMITING, ABUSE, AND RESOURCE PROTECTION
# ================================================================================

R-216 · RATE LIMITING IS REDIS-BACKED AND FAIL-CLOSED
MUST: `src/lib/rate-limiter.ts` is the only limiter; it uses Redis; when Redis is
unreachable it denies. Limits exist per IP, per user, per session, per endpoint
class, and globally.
VERIFY: Tests for threshold behavior, for reset behavior, and for the Redis-down
denial path.

R-217 · MONEY ENDPOINTS HAVE STRICTER LIMITS THAN READ ENDPOINTS
MUST: Quote, intent creation, signing, withdrawal, payment verification, and
copy-target changes have their own low limits, plus a per-user velocity check on
notional value, not only request count.

R-218 · GLOBAL BACKPRESSURE BEFORE COLLAPSE
MUST: Define maximum concurrent trades, queue depth, websocket connections, SSE
streams, and provider concurrency. When exceeded: shed load with a clear error,
never queue unboundedly, never let memory grow without limit.
VERIFY: A load test proves bounded memory and a clean rejection path.

R-219 · PROVIDER RATE LIMITS ARE RESPECTED PROACTIVELY
MUST: Client-side limiters per provider (Helius, Jupiter, PumpPortal, RugCheck,
Birdeye, Moralis, DexScreener, Telegram) sized below the documented limits, with
429 handling, `Retry-After` respect, and a circuit breaker on sustained failure.
PREVENTS: Bans (PumpPortal explicitly bans), credit exhaustion, and cascading
failure at the worst possible moment.

R-220 · RETRY WITH EXPONENTIAL BACKOFF AND FULL JITTER, ALWAYS BOUNDED
MUST: Every retry uses exponential backoff with jitter, a max attempt count, and
a total deadline. No fixed-interval retry loops. No infinite retries.
PREVENTS: Retry storms that turn a blip into an outage and a cost incident.

R-221 · ONE USER CANNOT CONSUME THE SYSTEM
MUST: Per-user quotas on jobs, subscriptions, copy targets, notifications, and
concurrent trades. Fair-share scheduling where a shared worker pool exists.

R-222 · TELEGRAM SEND RATES ARE COALESCED AND LIMITED
MUST: Implement message coalescing (P7.2) and per-chat/global send limits with
backoff on 429; never send one message per event in a burst.

R-223 · WEBHOOK INTAKE IS BOUNDED AND FAST
MUST: Webhook handlers verify, bound, persist, and enqueue — then return quickly.
No trading logic, no provider calls, and no long work inside the HTTP handler.
VERIFY: A test asserts handler latency stays under the documented bound under a
burst, and that duplicates are deduplicated by event ID.

R-224 · ANTI-AUTOMATION ON HIGH-VALUE ACTIONS
MUST: Withdrawals, limit increases, wallet exports, and admin actions require
re-authentication, and are limited by count per period, with alerting on
anomalies.

R-225 · DETECT AND STOP RUNAWAY LOOPS AUTOMATICALLY
MUST: A per-user and global counter of trades per minute, signer calls per
minute, and RPC calls per minute trips a breaker at a documented threshold and
alerts. A bug that trades in a loop must be stopped by the system, not by a human
noticing.
PREVENTS: The worst realistic loss scenario — an automation defect trading
thousands of times before anyone wakes up.
# ================================================================================
# CHAPTER 19 — DATABASE AND SCHEMA
# ================================================================================

R-226 · THE DOCUMENT'S SCHEMA IS CANONICAL
MUST: Implement `src/db/schema.ts` exactly as specified: table names (`users`,
`session`, `account`, `verification`, `wallets`, `tradingSessions`, `trades`,
`tradeIntents`, `positions`, `taxLots`, `tokenMetadata`, `copyTargets`,
`webhookEvents`, `notifications`, `referrals`, `userSettings`, `auditLogs`,
`rateLimits`, `keyEncryptionKeys`, `circuitBreakerState`, `userSecurityHolds`,
`feature_flags`), enums (`tier`, `trade_side`, `trade_status`, `session_status`,
`wallet_type`, `key_status`, `notification_type`), columns, relations, and indexes.
NEVER: Rename, add, or drop a table or column without an approved deviation and
the §1.7.3 propagation checklist.

R-227 · EVERY FOREIGN KEY IS DECLARED WITH EXPLICIT DELETE BEHAVIOR
MUST: State `onDelete` for every reference. Never rely on the default. Money and
audit rows are never cascade-deleted; user deletion anonymizes rather than
destroys financial history where retention requires it.

R-228 · UNIQUENESS IS ENFORCED BY THE DATABASE
MUST: Every business uniqueness rule (idempotency keys, telegram ID, email,
referral code, one active session per scope, one lot per acquisition event,
webhook event ID) has a UNIQUE constraint or unique index. Application checks are
not sufficient under concurrency.
VERIFY: A concurrency test inserts duplicates in parallel and asserts exactly one
succeeds and the other fails with a handled constraint error.

R-229 · CHECK CONSTRAINTS FOR DOMAIN INVARIANTS
MUST: Non-negative amounts, valid enum states, `expires_at > created_at`, bps
within 0..10_000, and similar invariants are enforced in the database where
expressible.
PREVENTS: A code bug writing impossible data that later crashes accounting.

R-230 · NOT NULL BY DEFAULT
MUST: Columns are `NOT NULL` unless absence is a meaningful, documented state.
Nullable money columns are prohibited.

R-231 · INDEXES MATCH THE ACTUAL QUERY PATHS
MUST: Every query in the codebase is covered by an index appropriate to its
predicate and ordering; every index in the schema is justified by a query.
VERIFY: `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` on the top queries shows no sequential scan on large
tables; the results are recorded in VERIFICATION.md.

R-232 · NO N+1 QUERIES ON ANY PATH THAT SERVES A REQUEST OR A TRADE
MUST: Batch with joins or `IN` queries; measure query counts per request in tests
for the hot endpoints.

R-233 · TRANSACTIONS WRAP EVERY MULTI-ROW INVARIANT
MUST: Any operation that must be all-or-nothing (intent + idempotency key, trade
+ position + lot, payment + tier upgrade, referral credit) runs in one database
transaction with an appropriate isolation level, and its failure path is tested.
NEVER: Perform a network call inside a database transaction.

R-234 · CONCURRENCY CONTROL IS EXPLICIT
MUST: Choose and document, per operation: optimistic (version column + retry) or
pessimistic (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`) locking. Wallet balance-affecting operations
serialize per wallet. Lock ordering is consistent to avoid deadlocks, and deadlock
errors are retried a bounded number of times.
VERIFY: A concurrent test on one wallet asserts no overdraft and no deadlock loop.

R-235 · NO LONG-RUNNING TRANSACTIONS
MUST: Keep transactions short; never hold one across an external call, a user
interaction, or a queue wait. Set `statement_timeout` and
`idle_in_transaction_session_timeout` at the connection level.
PREVENTS: Connection pool exhaustion and cascading stalls.

R-236 · CONNECTION POOLS ARE SIZED, MONITORED, AND BOUNDED
MUST: Configure pool size deliberately per process type (API, workers, bot),
alert on saturation and wait time, and never create a client per request.

R-237 · READS THAT DECIDE MONEY USE THE PRIMARY AND THE RIGHT ISOLATION
MUST: Never make a spend decision from a stale replica read or from a cache. Read
the authoritative row, in the same transaction as the write where required.

R-238 · SOFT DELETE OR HARD DELETE — DECIDED, DOCUMENTED, CONSISTENT
MUST: Follow the schema's model. Where soft delete is used, every query filters
deleted rows and a test proves it. Where hard delete is used, dependent rows are
handled explicitly.

R-239 · JSONB COLUMNS ARE SCHEMA-VALIDATED IN CODE
MUST: Any JSONB payload is parsed with Zod on read and validated on write;
never `as` cast. Document the shape next to the column.

R-240 · SEED DATA IS DETERMINISTIC AND NON-PRODUCTION-DESTRUCTIVE
MUST: `src/db/seed.ts` is idempotent, inserts only the documented metadata (SOL,
USDC, USDT), never overwrites user data, and refuses to run in production unless
explicitly forced with a recorded reason.

R-241 · DATABASE ROLES FOLLOW LEAST PRIVILEGE
MUST: The application role cannot DROP, cannot ALTER, cannot read the migration
role's objects it does not need, and has no UPDATE/DELETE on audit tables.
Migrations run under a separate role.

R-242 · NO ORM ESCAPE HATCHES ON MONEY TABLES WITHOUT REVIEW
MUST: Raw SQL touching money or audit tables requires the §1.7.7 reviewer block
and a test.

# ================================================================================
# CHAPTER 20 — MIGRATIONS
# ================================================================================

R-243 · MIGRATIONS ARE GENERATED FROM THE SCHEMA, REVIEWED, THEN APPLIED
MUST: `drizzle-kit generate` from the actual schema; read the generated SQL line
by line before applying; never hand-edit generated SQL except with a recorded
reason and a re-verification.

R-244 · EVERY MIGRATION HAS A TESTED DOWN PATH (§1.7.4)
MUST: Write and test the rollback before applying the forward migration. A
migration without a proven rollback is not applied.
VERIFY: On a scratch database: up → assert → down → assert original state → up.

R-245 · MIGRATIONS ARE FORWARD-COMPATIBLE WITH RUNNING CODE
MUST: Use expand/contract: add nullable column → backfill → start writing → start
reading → make non-null → remove old. Never deploy a migration that breaks the
currently running version.
PREVENTS: Downtime and 500s during every deploy.

R-246 · DESTRUCTIVE MIGRATIONS REQUIRE EXPLICIT HUMAN APPROVAL
MUST: Any `DROP`, `ALTER ... TYPE` that can lose data, `NOT NULL` addition
without a default, or column rename is a HARD STOP for approval, with a backup
taken and verified immediately before.

R-247 · BACKFILLS ARE BATCHED, RESUMABLE, AND THROTTLED
MUST: Never a single `UPDATE` over a large table in production. Batch by primary
key ranges, checkpoint progress, throttle, and be safe to re-run.

R-248 · MIGRATIONS RUN EXACTLY ONCE, IN ORDER, WITH A LOCK
MUST: Use the migration tool's ledger and an advisory lock so concurrent deploys
cannot double-apply. Verify the applied list matches the repository on boot.

R-249 · MIGRATIONS ARE TESTED ON A FRESH DATABASE AND ON A COPY OF REALISTIC DATA
MUST: `drizzle-kit migrate` on empty PostgreSQL 16 must succeed (a P0.2 gate),
and, once data exists, migrations are rehearsed against a restored backup.

R-250 · NEVER MIGRATE AND DEPLOY BLINDLY TOGETHER
MUST: Migration and application deploy are separate, ordered, observable steps
with a verification between them, per the blue-green process (P0.11).

# ================================================================================
# CHAPTER 21 — CACHING (REDIS AND IN-PROCESS)
# ================================================================================

R-251 · NEVER CACHE AUTHORIZATION DECISIONS BEYOND THEIR SAFE TTL
MUST: Session validity, revocation state, holds, flags, and kill-switch state are
either read fresh or cached with a TTL short enough to satisfy the documented
revocation bound, plus an explicit invalidation on change.
VERIFY: The revocation test (R-209) passes with caching enabled.

R-252 · NEVER CACHE KEY MATERIAL OR DECRYPTED SECRETS
MUST NOT: Put anything from D-015 in Redis, in memory beyond a signing
operation, or in any cache layer.

R-253 · EVERY CACHE ENTRY HAS A TTL AND A NAMESPACE
MUST: Keys are namespaced (`osiris:<env>:<network>:<domain>:<id>`), TTLs are
explicit constants, and no key is written without one.
PREVENTS: Cross-environment and cross-network cache poisoning.

R-254 · CACHE FAILURES DEGRADE, THEY DO NOT ELEVATE
MUST: A cache miss or Redis outage results in a slower correct answer or a
denial — never a permissive answer, never stale money data presented as fresh.

R-255 · WRITE-THROUGH OR INVALIDATE — NEVER HOPE
MUST: Every mutation invalidates or updates every cache entry derived from it.
List the affected keys in the task record for any new cached read.

R-256 · NO CACHING OF QUOTES BEYOND THEIR TTL, NO CACHING OF BALANCES FOR SPEND
MUST: Quote caching honours `JUPITER_QUOTE_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS`; balances used for
a spend decision are never served from cache (R-114/R-237).

R-257 · REDIS IS TREATED AS EPHEMERAL
MUST: No state whose loss changes money or authorization lives only in Redis.
Rate-limit counters may live there (fail closed on loss); sessions, trades, and
flags do not.

# ================================================================================
# CHAPTER 22 — QUEUES, JOBS, AND WORKERS (pg-boss)
# ================================================================================

R-258 · TYPED JOB DEFINITIONS ONLY
MUST: Define every job through `src/jobs/define-job.ts` with a Zod payload
schema, an explicit name constant, retry policy, timeout, and priority. No
untyped `send('name', anyObject)`.
VERIFY: A test asserts an invalid payload is rejected at enqueue time.

R-259 · EVERY HANDLER ASSUMES AT-LEAST-ONCE DELIVERY (D-046)
MUST: Handlers are idempotent (R-012), tolerate duplicates and out-of-order
arrival, and record their effect keyed by the idempotency key before performing
external actions.
VERIFY: A test delivers the same job twice concurrently and asserts one effect.

R-260 · JOB PAYLOADS CARRY IDS, NOT SNAPSHOTS OF MUTABLE STATE
MUST: Pass identifiers and the idempotency key; re-read authoritative state
(session validity, limits, balances, flags) inside the handler at execution time.
PREVENTS: Executing on authorization that was true when enqueued and false now.

R-261 · JOB PAYLOADS CONTAIN NO SECRETS AND NO KEY MATERIAL
MUST: Never enqueue tokens, private keys, decrypted values, or full PII. Payloads
are persisted in the database and visible to operators.

R-262 · RETRIES ARE BOUNDED, BACKED OFF, AND POISON-AWARE
MUST: Max attempts, exponential backoff with jitter, and a dead-letter path
(D-047) with alerting. Money jobs are never retried without the R-149 guarantee.

R-263 · JOB TIMEOUTS AND VISIBILITY ARE SHORTER THAN THE BUSINESS DEADLINE
MUST: Configure expiration so a stuck job cannot hold a trade past its useful
life, and so a crashed worker's job is re-delivered predictably — into an
idempotent handler.

R-264 · WORKERS SHUT DOWN GRACEFULLY AND NEVER ABANDON A SIGNED TRANSACTION
MUST: On SIGTERM: stop accepting new jobs, finish or safely checkpoint in-flight
work, persist state, release locks, then exit within the documented window. A
worker killed mid-trade must leave a resolvable record (R-153).
VERIFY: A test kills a worker between sign and confirm and asserts the resolver
determines ground truth from the chain.

R-265 · ONE JOB, ONE RESPONSIBILITY, WITH EXPLICIT STATE TRANSITIONS
MUST: The trade pipeline stages (quote → build → sign → send → confirm) are
separate, each persisting its state transition, each restartable.

R-266 · QUEUE DEPTH AND AGE ARE MONITORED WITH ALERTS
MUST: Alert on depth, oldest-job age, failure rate, and dead-letter growth.
A silently growing queue is an outage in progress.

R-267 · NO UNBOUNDED FAN-OUT
MUST: Enqueueing from a handler is bounded and cycle-free. Never allow a job to
enqueue itself unconditionally.

R-268 · BOUNDED CONCURRENCY EVERYWHERE
MUST: Worker concurrency, provider concurrency, and any `Promise.all` over a
dynamic list use an explicit concurrency limit. Never `Promise.all` over an
unbounded array of network calls.

R-269 · SCHEDULING IS DURABLE, NOT IN-PROCESS
MUST: Recurring work uses the durable scheduler (pg-boss/cron in the deployment),
never `setInterval` in a web process that may be replaced at any time.

R-270 · JOBS RESPECT THE KILL SWITCH AND FLAGS AT EXECUTION TIME
MUST: Every trading job re-checks `trading_enabled`, `signer_enabled`, the
relevant feature flag, breaker state, and session validity as its first action,
and exits cleanly (recording why) if any denies.
# ================================================================================
# CHAPTER 23 — EXTERNAL PROVIDERS AND API CLIENTS
# Applies to: Helius (RPC + Sender + webhooks), Jupiter v6, PumpPortal, RugCheck,
# DexScreener, Birdeye, Moralis, Telegram, Cloudflare, Oracle Cloud, and any
# other named external system.
# ================================================================================

R-271 · ALL NETWORK ACCESS GOES THROUGH A TYPED CLIENT MODULE
MUST: Exactly one client module per provider (`src/lib/helius.ts`,
`src/lib/jupiter.ts`, `src/lib/pumpportal.ts`, etc.). No `fetch` to an external
host anywhere else in the codebase.
VERIFY: `grep -rn "fetch(\|axios\|got(" src/ app/` shows calls only inside client
modules and their tests.
PREVENTS: Unmonitored, unlimited, unvalidated calls scattered through the system.

R-272 · CLIENTS EXPOSE DOMAIN OPERATIONS, NOT RAW HTTP
MUST: `getQuote(params): Result<Quote>` — not `post('/quote', body)`. The client
owns URL construction, headers, auth, timeout, retry, validation, and error
mapping.

R-273 · EVERY CALL HAS A TIMEOUT AND AN ABORT PATH
MUST: Explicit timeout constant per operation, AbortController wired, and a
typed timeout error distinct from a failure response.

R-274 · RETRY ONLY WHAT IS SAFE TO RETRY
MUST: Retry idempotent reads on transient errors with backoff and jitter. Never
auto-retry a submission or any state-changing provider call without the R-149
guarantee.

R-275 · VALIDATE EVERY RESPONSE (R-084) AND ITS SEMANTICS (R-142)
MUST: Schema-parse the body, then assert domain invariants before use.
PREVENTS: Trading on a malformed or hostile response.

R-276 · MAP PROVIDER ERRORS INTO THE INTERNAL TAXONOMY
MUST: Translate provider status codes and error bodies into the five failure
classes (R-148) and stable codes (R-146). Never leak the provider's raw text
outward.

R-277 · ONE CIRCUIT BREAKER PER PROVIDER
MUST: Track failure rate and latency; open the breaker on sustained failure;
half-open with a probe; record state transitions; expose breaker state in metrics
and health.

R-278 · FALLBACK ORDER IS EXPLICIT, DEGRADED MODE IS DEFINED
MUST: Per P0.14, define for each dependency: primary, fallbacks (e.g. dRPC,
GetBlock as configured), what capability is lost, and what is disabled entirely.
Degraded mode reduces capability, never security (D-074).
NEVER: Silently switch to a provider that has different guarantees for a money
decision without recording it on the trade record.

R-279 · NO PROVIDER IS AN AUTHORIZATION SOURCE
MUST: Never let a provider's response decide whether a user may act. Providers
supply data; OSIRIS decides.

R-280 · API KEYS ARE PER-ENVIRONMENT, SERVER-SIDE, ROTATABLE
MUST: Distinct keys per environment, never in client bundles, never in URLs that
get logged, rotatable without redeploy, revoked immediately on suspicion.

R-281 · PAGINATION AND LIMITS ARE HANDLED COMPLETELY
MUST: Follow cursors to completion with a bound, or state explicitly that only
the first page is used and why. Never assume a single page contains everything.

R-282 · CLIENT-SIDE RATE LIMITING BELOW THE PROVIDER'S LIMIT (R-219)
MUST: Configure per-provider limiters from the documented limits with headroom;
respect `Retry-After`; never burst on reconnect.

R-283 · WEBSOCKET CLIENTS RECONNECT SAFELY
MUST: Exponential backoff with jitter and a cap; re-subscribe to exactly the
previous subscription set; deduplicate messages across reconnects; never
reconnect in a tight loop; honour documented ban conditions (PumpPortal bans
abusive reconnects).
VERIFY: A test simulates 20 disconnects and asserts backoff growth, resubscribe
correctness, and zero duplicate processing.

R-284 · SUBSCRIPTIONS HAVE HEARTBEATS AND STALENESS DETECTION
MUST: Ping/pong or message-age monitoring; a stream with no data past its
threshold is declared stale, alerts, and triggers a controlled reconnect —
and any feature depending on it fails closed meanwhile.

R-285 · PIN THE PROVIDER CONTRACT VERSION
MUST: Use the documented API version/base URL (e.g. Jupiter v6) explicitly; do
not follow "latest"; record the version in the client and in logs.

R-286 · DETECT CONTRACT DRIFT LOUDLY
MUST: When response validation fails repeatedly, treat it as a provider contract
change: open the breaker, alert with the diff, disable the dependent feature, and
require human review. Never "loosen the schema" to make it pass.
PREVENTS: RISK-005 (Jupiter API changes) becoming a silent money bug.

R-287 · SEND PROVIDERS THE MINIMUM DATA
MUST: Never transmit user identifiers, emails, or secrets to a data provider.
Send only what the call requires.

R-288 · CACHE ONLY WHAT THE CONTRACT ALLOWS, WITH THE DOCUMENTED TTL
MUST: Honour the documented cache TTLs (`JUPITER_QUOTE_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS`,
`CACHE_DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS`, token metadata cache) and never cache a value used
for settlement past its freshness bound.

R-289 · COUNT AND CAP PROVIDER USAGE
MUST: Meter calls and credits per provider per hour/day, alert before free-tier
limits, and hard-stop non-essential usage when a cap is neared (RISK-004,
P0.17).

R-290 · NON-PRODUCTION USES NON-PRODUCTION ENDPOINTS
MUST: Devnet/test endpoints and test API keys in local/test/staging. A test must
never reach a mainnet endpoint or spend real credits.
VERIFY: A test-environment guard throws if a mainnet URL is configured.

R-291 · EVERY PROVIDER HAS AN OUTAGE RUNBOOK
MUST: `docs/runbooks/provider-<name>.md`: detection, blast radius, degraded
behavior, fallback steps, user messaging, recovery, and verification.

R-292 · RECORD EVERY EXTERNAL VERIFICATION
MUST: When you verify a live provider contract, limit, price, or behavior,
record in VERIFICATION.md: provider, date (UTC), exact endpoint or doc URL, what
was confirmed, the impact, and whether it contradicts this document.
NEVER: Change the document to match reality; record the discrepancy instead
(R-016, §13).

R-293 · NO UNDOCUMENTED OR SCRAPED ENDPOINTS
MUST NOT: Use an endpoint the provider does not document, scrape a UI, or rely on
an internal API, without explicit approval recorded in DECISIONS.md.
PREVENTS: Silent breakage and terms-of-service violations that get keys banned.

R-294 · OUTBOUND URLS COME FROM CONFIG, NEVER FROM USER OR CHAIN DATA
MUST: Every outbound host is from the validated config allowlist
(`ALLOWED_NETWORK_HOSTS`). Never fetch a URL found in token metadata, a webhook
payload, or a user field.
PREVENTS: SSRF into cloud metadata and internal services.

R-295 · INBOUND PROVIDER WEBHOOKS ARE AUTHENTICATED, BOUNDED, IDEMPOTENT
MUST: Verify authenticity (R-194), bound size (R-135), deduplicate by provider
event ID with a UNIQUE constraint in `webhookEvents`, persist raw payload for
replay, then enqueue. Return 2xx only after durable persistence.
VERIFY: Replaying the same webhook twice produces exactly one downstream effect.

# ================================================================================
# CHAPTER 24 — SOLANA EXECUTION CORRECTNESS
# ================================================================================

R-296 · COMMITMENT LEVELS ARE EXPLICIT ON EVERY RPC CALL
MUST: Pass commitment explicitly (D-029); never rely on the client default;
record which level produced each decision.

R-297 · `processed` IS NEVER SUFFICIENT FOR A MONEY DECISION
MUST NOT: Credit, debit, mark confirmed, update a position, or notify success on
`processed`.

R-298 · `finalized` IS REQUIRED BEFORE IRREVERSIBLE CREDIT
MUST: Payment verification (PAY-01), tier upgrades, referral payouts, and
treasury movements require `finalized` plus the documented checks (recipient,
amount, mint, memo/reference, and that the signature has not been credited before).
VERIFY: A test credits once for a repeated verification request (idempotent) and
rejects a `confirmed`-only transaction.

R-299 · TRANSACTIONS ARE VERSIONED AND ALTS ARE HANDLED AS SPECIFIED
MUST: Build versioned transactions with the address lookup tables Jupiter
returns, resolving and validating every ALT account per PART II. Never drop ALTs
to "simplify"; never assume legacy transactions will fit.

R-300 · SIMULATE BEFORE SENDING
MUST: Simulate every transaction (P1.5b) before signing/sending where the
document requires it; derive the CU limit from the simulation plus documented
headroom; abort on simulation failure with the decoded program error mapped to a
stable code.
NEVER: Send a transaction whose simulation failed because "it might still work".

R-301 · COMPUTE BUDGET IS SET EXPLICITLY AND BOUNDED
MUST: Always set compute unit limit and price instructions explicitly, from the
estimate and the caps (R-318). Never rely on defaults.

R-302 · FEE PAYER, SIGNERS, AND ACCOUNT ROLES ARE ASSERTED BEFORE SIGNING
MUST: Assert the fee payer is the expected wallet, the required signer set is
exactly as expected, and no account is marked writable that should not be.

R-303 · PROGRAM ID ALLOWLIST ON EVERY INSTRUCTION
MUST: Every instruction's program ID must be on the allowlist for that operation
(token program, token-2022, ATA program, system, compute budget, the routed DEX
programs, Jupiter). Anything else ⇒ refuse to sign, log a security event.
PREVENTS: A tampered route inserting a `setAuthority` or drain instruction.

R-304 · DESTINATION AND AUTHORITY CHECKS BEFORE SIGNING (R-143)
MUST: Assert no instruction assigns authority, closes an account, approves a
delegate, or transfers to an address outside the expected set for this operation.

R-305 · ATA EXISTENCE AND CREATION ARE EXPLICIT AND ACCOUNTED
MUST: Check whether the ATA exists; include creation only when needed; account
for its rent in the cost and the reserve (R-111); cap ATAs created per trade;
prefer idempotent ATA creation instructions.

R-306 · WSOL IS WRAPPED AND UNWRAPPED SYMMETRICALLY
MUST: Every wrap has a matching close/unwrap path, including on the failure path,
so SOL is never stranded in a temporary WSOL account.
VERIFY: A test asserts post-trade balances reconcile, including failed trades.

R-307 · RENT-EXEMPT MINIMUMS ARE RESPECTED
MUST: Never leave an account below rent-exemption; never spend the SOL reserve;
compute rent from live parameters.

R-308 · TOKEN PROGRAM SELECTION IS DETERMINED BY THE MINT, NOT ASSUMED
MUST: Detect whether a mint is SPL Token or Token-2022 by its owner program and
use the correct program and account layouts throughout.

R-309 · TRANSACTION SIZE IS CHECKED BEFORE SEND
MUST: Verify the serialized transaction fits within limits; if it does not,
reduce the route/instructions deterministically or fail — never truncate blindly.

R-310 · FETCH THE BLOCKHASH AS LATE AS POSSIBLE
MUST: Obtain the recent blockhash immediately before signing, from the same RPC
family used for submission, and record it with the attempt.

R-311 · BLOCKHASH EXPIRY IS TRACKED AND ENFORCED
MUST: Track `lastValidBlockHeight`; stop waiting once the height passes; declare
the attempt expired, resolve its true status by signature, and only then decide
whether to build a new attempt. A new blockhash means a new signature, a new
attempt record, and a fresh run of every pre-sign check.
NEVER: Re-sign with a new blockhash inside a retry loop without re-validating
session, limits, flags, quote freshness, and balance.
PREVENTS: A "retry" silently executing a trade the user is no longer authorized
to make, or executing twice.

R-312 · THE SIGNATURE IS THE IDENTITY OF AN ATTEMPT
MUST: Persist every attempt with its signature before submission; resolve status
by signature; never conflate two attempts of one intent.

R-313 · SUBMISSION USES THE SPECIFIED PATH AND ITS REQUIREMENTS
MUST: Use Helius Sender per its documented contract (endpoint, headers, minimum
tip, rate limits) where the document specifies it; do not silently fall back to a
generic `sendTransaction` with different economics — record any fallback on the
trade and in the log.

R-314 · MULTI-PATH SUBMISSION SENDS THE SAME SIGNED TRANSACTION
MUST: When submitting via multiple paths (P1.4f), send the identical signed
transaction bytes to every path. Never sign a second transaction to "try again"
in parallel.
PREVENTS: Two landings, two fills, double spend.

R-315 · CONFIRMATION IS POLLED WITH BOUNDS AND RESOLVED TO GROUND TRUTH
MUST: Poll `getSignatureStatuses` (and/or the documented mechanism) with backoff
until confirmed, expired, or deadline; treat `null` as unknown, not failed; on
deadline, move to the resolving state (R-153/R-154) and determine the outcome
from the chain before any user-facing verdict or retry.

R-316 · DROPPED TRANSACTIONS ARE HANDLED EXPLICITLY
MUST: Define, implement, and test the dropped-transaction path: detect expiry
without landing, verify non-existence by signature, then permit exactly one
rebuild under the full pre-sign check set, with a bounded attempt count.

R-317 · SLOT-AWARE EXECUTION WHERE SPECIFIED
MUST: Implement P1.5e as documented — use slot progression rather than wall-clock
assumptions for validity, staleness, and scheduling decisions.

R-318 · PRIORITY FEES AND TIPS ARE CAPPED, DYNAMIC, AND ATTRIBUTED
MUST: Compute fees per the dynamic engine (P1.4d/P5.7) within hard minimum and
maximum bounds from constants; never exceed the documented percentage of trade
value; record the fee and tip paid on the trade record; alert on sustained
maximum usage.
PREVENTS: Fee runaway during congestion quietly consuming user funds.

R-319 · JITO BUNDLES FOLLOW THEIR DOCUMENTED CONSTRAINTS
MUST: Implement P1.4b exactly — bundle composition, tip account and minimum,
submission endpoint, and status polling. A bundle that cannot be verified as
landed is treated as unknown, not successful.

R-320 · MEV PROTECTION IS APPLIED WHERE SPECIFIED
MUST: Implement P1.4c (MEV protect / DontFront semantics) as documented for the
paths that require it, and record whether protection was active on each trade.

R-321 · CONGESTION IS A DEFINED DEGRADED MODE
MUST: Detect elevated failure/expiry rates and enter a documented degraded mode:
raise minimums, reduce concurrency, widen deadlines, or halt new trades — with
user-visible status. Never respond to congestion by removing checks.

R-322 · DEVNET AND MAINNET ARE PHYSICALLY SEPARATED
MUST: Separate RPC URLs, separate wallets, separate database rows tagged by
network, separate webhooks, and a boot-time assertion that the configured network
matches the environment's expectation.
VERIFY: A test asserts the app refuses to start with `production` +
`devnet` mismatch, and vice versa.

R-323 · RPC FAILOVER NEVER SPLITS A DECISION
MUST: Use one RPC for the lifetime of a confirmation decision; if it fails, restart
the resolution against another provider and reconcile explicitly — never merge
partial answers from two providers into one verdict.

R-324 · STATUS REGRESSION IS HANDLED
MUST: If a previously confirmed signature later reports an error or disappears,
treat it as an incident: freeze the affected position updates, alert, reconcile
from the chain, and never silently overwrite financial records.

R-325 · NEVER SIGN ANYTHING YOU DID NOT BUILD OR FULLY DECODE
MUST: The signer signs only transactions it can decode and validate instruction
by instruction. An opaque blob is refused.
# ================================================================================
# CHAPTER 25 — TRADE PIPELINE AND EXECUTION SAFETY
# ================================================================================

R-326 · ONE PIPELINE, ONE STATE MACHINE, PERSISTED
MUST: Every trade follows the documented states (`pending`, `quoted`,
`building_tx`, `signing`, `sending`, `sent`, `confirmed`, `failed`, `revoked`)
with every transition persisted, timestamped, and attributed. No shortcuts, no
in-memory-only states.
VERIFY: A test drives every legal transition and asserts every illegal transition
is rejected.

R-327 · INTENT BEFORE ACTION
MUST: Persist a `tradeIntents` row with the idempotency key, user, session,
mints, amount, side, limits, and correlationId BEFORE quoting, building, or
signing. The intent is the authorization record.
PREVENTS: Untraceable signatures with no corresponding user request.

R-328 · PRE-SIGN CHECK SET IS A SINGLE FUNCTION, RUN EVERY TIME
MUST: One function performs, in order: flags and kill switch, session active and
not revoked, user holds, tier and session limits, breaker state, quote freshness,
slippage bounds, balance and reserve, token safety verdict, transaction decode and
allowlist checks, fee caps. It runs immediately before every signature — including
on retries and rebuilds.
NEVER: Duplicate a subset of these checks somewhere else and call it sufficient.
VERIFY: A test removes each check in turn and asserts a corresponding attack
succeeds — proving each check is load-bearing (negative-control testing).

R-329 · THE USER'S PARAMETERS ARE NEVER SILENTLY WIDENED
MUST: Slippage, amount, and route constraints may only be narrowed by the system,
never widened. If execution requires wider tolerance, it fails and informs the
user.
PREVENTS: The classic "retry with more slippage" pattern that hands value to MEV.

R-330 · A QUOTE IS BOUND TO ITS INTENT
MUST: Store the quote (route, in/out amounts, price impact, source, timestamp)
with the intent, and assert the built transaction matches the quote within
documented tolerance before signing.

R-331 · PRICE IMPACT AND SANITY BOUNDS ARE ENFORCED
MUST: Reject quotes exceeding documented price-impact limits, quotes with an
output of zero, quotes whose implied price deviates beyond a bound from an
independent reference, and routes through programs not on the allowlist.

R-332 · EXECUTION IS SERIALIZED PER WALLET
MUST: Only one in-flight signing/submission per wallet at a time, enforced by a
lock with a timeout, so concurrent trades cannot double-spend the same balance.
VERIFY: A concurrency test asserts serialization and no overdraft.

R-333 · REVOCATION AND KILL SWITCH INTERRUPT THE PIPELINE AT EVERY STAGE
MUST: Each stage checks halt conditions on entry and before any external effect;
work is abandoned safely with a recorded reason; a signed-but-unsent transaction
is discarded, never stored for later use.
VERIFY: Tests inject a halt at each of the nine states and assert correct
behavior at each.

R-334 · NEVER STORE A SIGNED TRANSACTION FOR LATER USE
MUST: A signature is produced only when it is about to be submitted. Signed
artifacts are never queued, cached, or persisted for reuse.
PREVENTS: A stale, still-valid signed transaction being replayed after
authorization ends.

R-335 · THE TRADE RECORD IS THE SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH FOR OUTCOME
MUST: Position, lot, PNL, notification, and UI updates derive from the confirmed
trade record — never from an optimistic assumption at submission time.

R-336 · USER-VISIBLE STATUS NEVER OVERSTATES CERTAINTY
MUST: "Submitted" ≠ "Confirmed" ≠ "Filled". Show the true state, including
"unknown, resolving", with the signature so the user can verify independently.

R-337 · FAILED TRADES ARE FULLY CLEANED UP
MUST: On failure, release locks, unwind temporary accounts where safe, reconcile
balances, record the reason with a stable code, and leave no partial position or
lot rows.

R-338 · MANUAL AND AUTOMATED TRADES SHARE THE SAME SAFETY PATH
MUST: Copy trades, bot commands, dashboard trades, and API trades converge on the
same intent → checks → signer path. No path may bypass any check.
VERIFY: A test asserts each entry point calls the same pre-sign function.

R-339 · SELLS ARE VALIDATED AGAINST ACTUAL HOLDINGS
MUST: Verify the on-chain token balance before a sell; never sell more than held;
handle dust and rounding by capping at the actual balance; never let a rounding
error produce a failed transaction that costs fees repeatedly.

R-340 · EVERY TRADE RECORDS ITS FULL ECONOMICS
MUST: Persist input/output amounts (base units), price, slippage set and realized,
priority fee, tip, network fee, ATA rent, platform fee, and route — for
accounting, tax lots, and dispute resolution.

# ================================================================================
# CHAPTER 26 — TOKEN SAFETY (SAF-05, HONEYPOTS, RUGS)
# ================================================================================

R-341 · NO BUY WITHOUT A SAFETY VERDICT
MUST: Every buy requires a completed safety evaluation for that mint, within its
freshness window, with a recorded verdict and reasons. No verdict ⇒ no trade.

R-342 · TOKEN-2022 EXTENSIONS ARE PARSED, NOT ASSUMED
MUST: Implement SAF-05 exactly: parse the mint's extension set; evaluate transfer
fee, transfer hook, permanent delegate, non-transferable, default account state,
mint close authority, confidential transfer, and any other documented extension.
NEVER: Treat an unrecognized extension as harmless. Unknown ⇒ reject (fail closed).
VERIFY: Fixture tests for each extension type, including a mint with multiple
extensions and one with an unknown extension type.

R-343 · AUTHORITIES ARE CHECKED, INCLUDING PROGRAM UPGRADE AUTHORITY
MUST: Check mint authority, freeze authority, and — per the document's
ProgramData procedure — the token program's upgrade authority. Retained
dangerous authorities are a documented risk factor with a defined policy.

R-344 · HONEYPOT AND LIQUIDITY CHECKS ARE MANDATORY (P1.6b)
MUST: Evaluate sellability, liquidity depth and lock status, holder
concentration, and the documented heuristics before buying. Insufficient data ⇒
reject, never "assume fine".

R-345 · SAFETY VERDICTS ARE CACHED WITH SHORT TTL AND INVALIDATED ON CHANGE
MUST: A mint's verdict expires; authorities and extensions can change; re-verify
before each buy beyond the TTL, and on any observed change.

R-346 · THIRD-PARTY SAFETY SCORES ARE INPUTS, NOT DECISIONS
MUST: RugCheck and similar feed the verdict; the on-chain checks are
authoritative. A provider outage means the on-chain checks decide; if those
cannot run, fail closed.

R-347 · TOKEN METADATA IS HOSTILE INPUT
MUST: Escape and length-limit names, symbols, and URIs before display or logging;
never render HTML from metadata; never fetch a metadata URI server-side (R-294);
never use a symbol as an identifier — the mint address is the identity.

R-348 · A FAILED SELL ATTEMPT ON A TOKEN RAISES ITS RISK STATE
MUST: Repeated sell failures for a mint mark it as suspected-honeypot, alert the
user, and block further buys of that mint pending review.

# ================================================================================
# CHAPTER 27 — COPY TRADING AND WEBHOOK AUTOMATION
# ================================================================================

R-349 · COPY TRADING IS OFF UNLESS EXPLICITLY ENABLED PER USER
MUST: `copy_trading_enabled` flag AND a per-user opt-in AND an active trading
session AND per-target limits — all required, all checked at execution time.

R-350 · TARGETS ARE VALIDATED AND BOUNDED
MUST: Validate target addresses; cap the number of targets per user by tier; cap
the per-target and aggregate exposure; allow instant disable per target.

R-351 · COPY SIZING IS EXPLICIT, CAPPED, AND NEVER PROPORTIONAL BY ACCIDENT
MUST: Implement the documented sizing model (fixed amount and/or percentage) with
absolute per-trade and per-day caps, and a minimum size below which the copy is
skipped rather than executed as dust.
PREVENTS: A whale's 500 SOL trade being mirrored into a user's entire balance.

R-352 · DECODE, DO NOT GUESS, THE TARGET'S TRADE
MUST: Use the documented decoders for the supported programs (Phase 1: Raydium
AMM v4, PumpSwap, Jupiter inner instructions) with exact discriminators and
account layouts. If the program is unsupported or decoding is ambiguous, skip the
event and record why.
NEVER: Infer the traded mint from balance deltas alone unless the document
specifies that method.

R-353 · STALE SIGNALS ARE DISCARDED
MUST: Enforce the documented delay tolerance; a signal older than the bound is
dropped with a recorded reason. Late copies are worse than no copies.

R-354 · DEDUPLICATE EVERY SIGNAL
MUST: Deduplicate by transaction signature and by target-event ID before
enqueuing, with a unique constraint, tolerating webhook re-delivery and
WebSocket reconnect overlap (D-046).
VERIFY: Replayed webhook + reconnect overlap produce exactly one copy trade.

R-355 · COPY TRADES OBEY EVERY MANUAL-TRADE CONTROL
MUST: Token safety, slippage bounds, fee caps, breaker, kill switch, tier limits,
balance reserve, and the pre-sign check set apply identically (R-338).

R-356 · SELF-COPY AND LOOPS ARE IMPOSSIBLE
MUST: Refuse to copy a target that is an OSIRIS-managed wallet, refuse targets
that would create a cycle, and detect oscillating buy/sell loops on the same mint
within a window.
PREVENTS: A feedback loop that trades until the balance is gone.

R-357 · WEBHOOK ENDPOINTS ARE UNGUESSABLE, AUTHENTICATED, AND ROTATABLE
MUST: Secret path segment plus signature/secret verification; the URL is treated
as a secret; rotation is supported and documented.

R-358 · WEBHOOK PROCESSING IS ASYNCHRONOUS AND BOUNDED (R-223)
MUST: Persist then enqueue; process in workers; cap per-target and global copy
concurrency; shed load explicitly under burst rather than queuing indefinitely.

R-359 · MISSED EVENTS ARE DETECTED, NOT ASSUMED ABSENT
MUST: Monitor expected event cadence per target and alert on silence (R-166);
provide a documented backfill/reconciliation path that is idempotent.

R-360 · COPY TRADE ATTRIBUTION IS RECORDED
MUST: Every copy trade records the target, the source signature, the decode
result, the sizing decision, and the latency at each stage — for audit and for
the P3.6 budget.

R-361 · A TARGET'S BEHAVIOR CANNOT ESCALATE PRIVILEGE
MUST: Nothing in a target's transaction (memos, token names, instruction data)
may influence OSIRIS control flow beyond the decoded, validated trade parameters
(R-019).

R-362 · COPY TRADING HALTS ON ANOMALY
MUST: Auto-disable a target (and alert) on: repeated decode failures, repeated
execution failures, safety rejections, unusual size, or breaker trips — rather
than continuing to burn fees.
# ================================================================================
# CHAPTER 28 — REAL-TIME TRANSPORT (WEBSOCKET CONTROL + SSE DATA)
# ================================================================================

R-363 · THE DOCUMENTED ARCHITECTURE IS BINDING: WS FOR CONTROL, SSE FOR DATA
MUST: Implement exactly the split specified in PART II §11. Do not introduce
Socket.io, a different framework, or a second transport.

R-364 · CONNECTIONS ARE AUTHENTICATED AT HANDSHAKE AND RE-AUTHORIZED CONTINUOUSLY
MUST: Authenticate on connect using the server-side session; re-check
authorization for every subscription and periodically for long-lived streams;
close immediately on revocation, expiry, or hold.
NEVER: Authenticate via a token in the query string that lands in logs (R-183).

R-365 · SUBSCRIPTIONS ARE SCOPED TO THE OWNER
MUST: A connection may subscribe only to its own user's channels. Channel names
include the user ID and are validated server-side against the session.
VERIFY: A test subscribes to another user's channel and asserts rejection plus a
security event.

R-366 · SERVER PUSHES ONLY WHAT THE USER MAY SEE
MUST: Filter every broadcast per recipient; never fan out a payload containing
another user's data with client-side filtering.

R-367 · CONNECTIONS ARE BOUNDED AND BACKPRESSURED
MUST: Cap connections per user and globally; bound per-connection send buffers;
drop or coalesce on slow consumers; never let an unread stream grow memory
without limit (D-048).
VERIFY: A load test with slow consumers shows bounded memory and clean
disconnects.

R-368 · HEARTBEATS AND IDLE TIMEOUTS ARE MANDATORY
MUST: Ping/keepalive on both transports, idle timeout, and server-side cleanup of
dead connections. Track connection count as a metric.

R-369 · MESSAGES ARE VERSIONED, TYPED, AND VALIDATED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS
MUST: A discriminated union of message types with Zod validation on receive; an
explicit protocol version; unknown types rejected and logged, not ignored.

R-370 · REAL-TIME IS A CONVENIENCE, NEVER AN AUTHORITY
MUST: Control actions received over WebSocket are re-validated exactly like HTTP
requests; the database remains the source of truth; a missed message must never
cause an incorrect financial state.

R-371 · CLIENTS RECONNECT WITH BACKOFF AND RESUME CORRECTLY
MUST: Client reconnect uses backoff with jitter; on resume, the client refetches
authoritative state rather than assuming continuity; server assigns event IDs so
gaps are detectable.

R-372 · REVOCATION AND KILL SWITCH PROPAGATE IN REAL TIME
MUST: Session revocation, holds, and kill-switch engagement immediately close or
notify affected connections within the documented bound (R-209), and the UI
reflects the halt without a refresh.

# ================================================================================
# CHAPTER 29 — TELEGRAM BOT
# ================================================================================

R-373 · WEBHOOK MODE, grammY, AS SPECIFIED — WITH SECRET VERIFICATION (DEF-001)
MUST: Implement webhook mode per PART II §16; verify the secret token on every
update (R-194); reject and log anything unverified before parsing.

R-374 · EVERY UPDATE IS PROCESSED IDEMPOTENTLY
MUST: Deduplicate by `update_id`; Telegram re-delivers on non-2xx. Return 2xx
after durable persistence; do the work asynchronously.
VERIFY: A replayed update produces exactly one effect.

R-375 · CHAT IDENTITY IS NOT AUTHORIZATION
MUST: A Telegram chat ID alone never authorizes a money action. Resolve to an
OSIRIS user with a verified binding (R-202), then apply the full authorization
set and the trust-tier restrictions (D-068).

R-376 · TRUST TIERS ARE ENFORCED SERVER-SIDE
MUST: Actions restricted to the web dashboard are rejected from Telegram at the
service layer, not merely absent from the keyboard.
VERIFY: A test invokes a restricted command directly and asserts rejection.

R-377 · DESTRUCTIVE AND MONEY COMMANDS REQUIRE EXPLICIT CONFIRMATION
MUST: Trades, revocations, withdrawals, and setting changes use a confirmation
step bound to a nonce with a short expiry, tied to the specific parameters, and
single-use.
PREVENTS: Fat-finger and callback-replay execution.

R-378 · CALLBACK DATA IS UNTRUSTED AND BOUND
MUST: Callback payloads are signed or reference a server-side record; never
encode amounts, mints, or user IDs in callback data that the server trusts;
validate that the callback's user matches the record's owner.

R-379 · NEVER ACCEPT OR DISPLAY SECRETS IN CHAT (R-179)
MUST: The bot never asks for keys or seeds, never echoes them, and warns and logs
if one is sent. It never shows full addresses in a way that invites social
engineering without the user's own verification path.

R-380 · MESSAGES ARE COALESCED AND RATE-LIMITED (R-222)
MUST: Implement P7.2 coalescing; respect Telegram limits; back off on 429; drop
or summarize rather than flooding.

R-381 · ALL DYNAMIC CONTENT IS ESCAPED FOR THE PARSE MODE
MUST: Escape user- and chain-supplied text (token names, symbols, memos) for the
chosen parse mode; length-limit; never interpolate raw metadata into markdown.

R-382 · COMMANDS ARE AN EXPLICIT ALLOWLIST WITH TYPED ARGUMENTS
MUST: Register exactly the documented commands (`/start`, `/help`, `/session`,
`/revoke`, `/pnl`, and phase-added ones); parse arguments with a schema; unknown
commands respond with help, never with a stack trace.

R-383 · THE PANIC PATH IS ALWAYS AVAILABLE AND ALWAYS FIRST
MUST: `/revoke` (and the panic flow) works even when trading is degraded, the
queue is backed up, or the breaker is open — it is never rate-limited into
uselessness for the owning user and never queued behind trading work (R-209).

R-384 · NOTIFICATIONS TELL THE TRUTH AND ARE NOT A SUBSTITUTE FOR STATE
MUST: Notifications reflect persisted state; a failed send never changes system
state; retries are bounded and deduplicated so a user is never told twice that
one trade filled.

# ================================================================================
# CHAPTER 30 — FRONTEND AND NEXT.JS
# ================================================================================

R-385 · THE CLIENT IS UNTRUSTED, ALWAYS
MUST: Every rule in CHAPTER 17 is enforced server-side regardless of the UI.
Hiding, disabling, or omitting a control is presentation, never protection.

R-386 · NO SECRETS, NO PRIVILEGED LOGIC IN THE BUNDLE (R-182)
MUST: Audit every `NEXT_PUBLIC_*`; keep provider keys, RPC keys with write scope,
and any signing capability out of the browser entirely.

R-387 · NO DANGEROUS RENDERING
MUST NOT: Use `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, `eval`, `new Function`, or inject
unescaped chain data anywhere. Render all external strings as text.
VERIFY: `grep -rn "dangerouslySetInnerHTML\|eval(\|new Function" app/ src/`
returns zero results.

R-388 · SECURITY HEADERS AND CSP ARE PRESENT AND TESTED
MUST: Content-Security-Policy (no `unsafe-inline` for scripts), HSTS,
X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors,
Permissions-Policy — configured in Caddy and/or middleware as documented.
VERIFY: An automated header test runs against staging and fails the build on a
missing or weakened header.

R-389 · CORS AND ORIGIN POLICY ARE EXPLICIT ALLOWLISTS
MUST: Only the documented origins; never `*` with credentials; validate `Origin`
on state-changing requests (R-198).

R-390 · NO BROWSER STORAGE OF SENSITIVE STATE
MUST NOT: Persist tokens, keys, balances used for decisions, or PII in
localStorage/sessionStorage/IndexedDB. Session state lives in HttpOnly cookies
and server state.

R-391 · MONEY UI IS PESSIMISTIC, NOT OPTIMISTIC
MUST: Never show a trade as done before the server confirms; show the true state
machine; disable the submit control while an intent is in flight and key it by
the idempotency key so a double-click cannot create two intents.
VERIFY: A test double-submits and asserts one intent.

R-392 · AMOUNT INPUTS ARE PRECISION-SAFE
MUST: Parse decimal strings (R-104), enforce the mint's decimals, display
