### PumpSwap Buy Instruction Layout

```typescript
// Buy instruction data layout
// [discriminator: 8 bytes][baseAmountIn: 8 bytes][quoteAmountIn: 8 bytes][minAmountOut: 8 bytes]
// Total: 32 bytes

const BuyLayout = struct([
  u8("discriminator"), // Actually 8 bytes, use blob(8) in practice
  u64("baseAmountIn"),
  u64("quoteAmountIn"),
  u64("minAmountOut"),
]);

// For buy: baseAmountIn = 0, quoteAmountIn = SOL amount, minAmountOut = minimum tokens
// For sell: baseAmountIn = token amount, quoteAmountIn = 0, minAmountOut = minimum SOL
```



### PumpSwap Account Structure (Buy/Sell)

```typescript
interface PumpSwapPoolData {
  baseMint: PublicKey;           // Token mint
  quoteMint: PublicKey;          // SOL (usually WSOL)
  lpMint: PublicKey;             // LP token mint
  poolBaseTokenAccount: PublicKey;  // Pool's token ATA
  poolQuoteTokenAccount: PublicKey; // Pool's SOL ATA
  coinCreator: PublicKey;        // Token creator
  dataLen: number;               // Account data length (< 300 means creator fees apply)
}

// Buy instruction accounts (indexes):
// 0: pool (mut)
// 1: user (signer, mut)
// 2: global_config
// 3: base_mint
// 4: quote_mint
// 5: user_base_ata (mut)
// 6: user_quote_ata (mut)
// 7: pool_base_token_account (mut)
// 8: pool_quote_token_account (mut)
// 9: protocol_fee_recipient (mut)
// 10: token_program
// 11: creator_vault_ata (mut) — only if pool.dataLen < 300
// 12: creator_vault_authority
// 13: pump_fees_program
// 14: fee_config_pda
```



### PumpSwap Pool Data Decoding

```typescript
import { struct, u64, publicKey, u8, u16, bool } from "@solana/buffer-layout";

const PumpSwapPoolLayout = struct([
  u8("discriminant"),          // Pool discriminator
  publicKey("coinCreator"),     // Token creator
  publicKey("baseMint"),        // Base token mint
  publicKey("quoteMint"),       // Quote token mint (SOL/WSOL)
  publicKey("lpMint"),          // LP token mint
  u64("poolBaseAmount"),        // Base token reserves
  u64("poolQuoteAmount"),       // Quote token reserves (SOL)
  u64("protocolFeeBasisPoints"), // Protocol fee (e.g., 100 = 1%)
  u64("lpFeeBasisPoints"),      // LP fee
  publicKey("poolBaseTokenAccount"),  // Pool base ATA
  publicKey("poolQuoteTokenAccount"), // Pool quote ATA
  // ... additional fields vary by version
]);

async function fetchPoolData(
  connection: Connection,
  poolAddress: PublicKey
): Promise<PumpSwapPoolData> {
  const account = await connection.getAccountInfo(poolAddress);
  if (!account) throw new Error("Pool not found");

  const data = PumpSwapPoolLayout.decode(account.data);

  return {
    baseMint: data.baseMint,
    quoteMint: data.quoteMint,
    lpMint: data.lpMint,
    poolBaseTokenAccount: data.poolBaseTokenAccount,
    poolQuoteTokenAccount: data.poolQuoteTokenAccount,
    coinCreator: data.coinCreator,
    dataLen: account.data.length,
  };
}
```



### Complete PumpSwap Swap Function

```typescript
const PUMP_AMM_PROGRAM_ID = new PublicKey("pAMMBay6oceH9fJKBRHGP5D4bD4sWpmSwMn52FMfXEA");
const PUMP_FEES_PROGRAM_ID = new PublicKey("pfeeUxB6jkeY1Hxd7CsFCAjcbHA9rWtchMGdZ6VojVZ");
const GLOBAL_CONFIG = new PublicKey("GTh9Z1qH9gH1h7g5g5g5g5g5g5g5g5g5g5g5g5g5g5g5g"); // ACTION REQUIRED: Get actual global config

async function executePumpSwap(
  connection: Connection,
  payer: Keypair,
  pool: PublicKey,
  amountIn: bigint,
  minAmountOut: bigint,
  isBuy: boolean
): Promise<string> {
  const poolData = await fetchPoolData(connection, pool);

  const userBaseAta = getAssociatedTokenAddressSync(poolData.baseMint, payer.publicKey);
  const userQuoteAta = getAssociatedTokenAddressSync(poolData.quoteMint, payer.publicKey);

  // Build instruction data
  const data = Buffer.alloc(32);
  const discriminator = isBuy
    ? Buffer.from([0x66, 0x06, 0x3d, 0x12, 0x01, 0xda, 0xeb, 0xea])
    : Buffer.from([0x33, 0xe6, 0x85, 0xa4, 0x01, 0x7f, 0x83, 0xad]);

  discriminator.copy(data, 0);
  data.writeBigUInt64LE(isBuy ? 0n : amountIn, 8);      // baseAmountIn
  data.writeBigUInt64LE(isBuy ? amountIn : 0n, 16);     // quoteAmountIn
  data.writeBigUInt64LE(minAmountOut, 24);              // minAmountOut

  const keys: AccountMeta[] = [
    { pubkey: pool, isSigner: false, isWritable: true },
    { pubkey: payer.publicKey, isSigner: true, isWritable: true },
    { pubkey: GLOBAL_CONFIG, isSigner: false, isWritable: false },
    { pubkey: poolData.baseMint, isSigner: false, isWritable: false },
    { pubkey: poolData.quoteMint, isSigner: false, isWritable: false },
    { pubkey: userBaseAta, isSigner: false, isWritable: true },
    { pubkey: userQuoteAta, isSigner: false, isWritable: true },
    { pubkey: poolData.poolBaseTokenAccount, isSigner: false, isWritable: true },
    { pubkey: poolData.poolQuoteTokenAccount, isSigner: false, isWritable: true },
    { pubkey: PROTOCOL_FEE_RECIPIENT, isSigner: false, isWritable: true },
    { pubkey: TOKEN_PROGRAM_ID, isSigner: false, isWritable: false },
  ];

  // Add creator fee accounts if pool is "legacy" (dataLen < 300)
  if (poolData.dataLen < 300) {
    const [creatorVaultAuthority] = PublicKey.findProgramAddressSync(
      [Buffer.from("creator_vault_authority"), poolData.coinCreator.toBuffer()],
      PUMP_AMM_PROGRAM_ID
    );
    const creatorVaultAta = getAssociatedTokenAddressSync(
      poolData.quoteMint,
      creatorVaultAuthority,
      true // allowOwnerOffCurve
    );
    const [feeConfigPDA] = PublicKey.findProgramAddressSync(
      [Buffer.from("fee_config")],
      PUMP_FEES_PROGRAM_ID
    );

    keys.push(
      { pubkey: creatorVaultAta, isSigner: false, isWritable: true },
      { pubkey: creatorVaultAuthority, isSigner: false, isWritable: false },
      { pubkey: PUMP_FEES_PROGRAM_ID, isSigner: false, isWritable: false },
      { pubkey: feeConfigPDA, isSigner: false, isWritable: false }
    );
  }

  const instruction = new TransactionInstruction({
    programId: PUMP_AMM_PROGRAM_ID,
    keys,
    data,
  });

  // Check if account extension needed (for larger pools)
  const poolInfo = await connection.getAccountInfo(pool);
  let tx: Transaction;
  if (poolInfo && poolInfo.data.length < 300) {
    const extendIx = new TransactionInstruction({
      programId: PUMP_AMM_PROGRAM_ID,
      keys: [{ pubkey: pool, isSigner: false, isWritable: true }],
      data: Buffer.from([0x00]), // extend account discriminator
    });
    tx = new Transaction().add(extendIx, instruction);
  } else {
    tx = new Transaction().add(instruction);
  }

  tx.feePayer = payer.publicKey;
  tx.recentBlockhash = (await connection.getLatestBlockhash()).blockhash;
  tx.sign(payer);

  return await connection.sendRawTransaction(tx.serialize(), {
    skipPreflight: true,
    maxRetries: 3,
  });
}
```



### PumpSwap Migration Detection

A Pump.fun → PumpSwap migration happens in a single transaction containing:
1. Pump.fun `migrate` instruction (on `6EF8rrecthR5Dkzon8Nwu78hRvfCKubJ14M5uBEwF6P`)
2. PumpSwap `create_pool` instruction (on `pAMMBay6oceH9fJKBRHGP5D4bD4sWpmSwMn52FMfXEA`)

```typescript
async function detectMigration(
  tx: ParsedTransactionWithMeta
): Promise<{ mint: string; poolAddress: string; solAmount: number } | null> {
  const instructions = tx.transaction.message.instructions;

  // Look for Pump.fun migrate instruction
  const migrateIx = instructions.find(
    (ix) => ix.programId.toBase58() === "6EF8rrecthR5Dkzon8Nwu78hRvfCKubJ14M5uBEwF6P"
  );

  // Look for PumpSwap create_pool instruction
  const createPoolIx = instructions.find(
    (ix) => ix.programId.toBase58() === "pAMMBay6oceH9fJKBRHGP5D4bD4sWpmSwMn52FMfXEA"
  );

  if (!migrateIx || !createPoolIx) return null;

  // Extract mint from migrate instruction accounts (typically index 1)
  const mint = migrateIx.accounts[1]?.toBase58();

  // Extract pool address from create_pool instruction accounts (typically index 0)
  const poolAddress = createPoolIx.accounts[0]?.toBase58();

  // Extract SOL amount from token balance changes
  const preBalances = tx.meta?.preBalances || [];
  const postBalances = tx.meta?.postBalances || [];
  const accountKeys = tx.transaction.message.staticAccountKeys;

  let solAmount = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < accountKeys.length; i++) {
    const delta = (postBalances[i] || 0) - (preBalances[i] || 0);
    if (delta < 0 && accountKeys[i].toBase58() === migrateIx.accounts[2]?.toBase58()) {
      solAmount = Math.abs(delta) / 1e9;
    }
  }

  return { mint, poolAddress, solAmount };
}
```



### PumpSwap for Copy Trading (Phase 1 Approach)

For Phase 1 copy trading, use the **PumpPortal WebSocket** for PumpSwap trade detection instead of on-chain decoding. The WebSocket provides:
- Real-time buy/sell events with token mint, amounts, and prices
- Migration events when tokens graduate from Pump.fun
- No need to decode instruction layouts in real-time

On-chain PumpSwap decoding (as documented above) is for:
- Historical backfill
- Post-trade verification
- Advanced analytics (Phase 6+)

ADDENDUM C: LOSS CIRCUIT BREAKER — COMPLETE STATE MACHINE
================================================================================

The spec mentions DIF-08 (loss circuit breaker) but doesn't document the state machine. Here is the complete design.



### Circuit Breaker State Machine

```
[MONITORING] --loss threshold exceeded--> [TRIPPED]
   ^                                          |
   |                                          |--60s cooldown + typed confirmation--> [OVERRIDDEN]
   |                                          |                                          |
   |<-----------------reset after window-------------------|--------------------------|
   |                                                                             |
   |<---------------------------------manual reset--------------------------------|
```



### States

| State | Description | Entry Condition |
|-------|-------------|-----------------|
| `MONITORING` | Normal operation, tracking PNL | Default state |
| `TRIPPED` | Trading halted, user notified | Rolling PNL < -threshold |
| `OVERRIDDEN` | User manually overrode (60s + typed confirmation) | User confirms override |



### Configuration

```typescript
interface CircuitBreakerConfig {
  // Rolling window for PNL calculation
  windowDurationMinutes: number; // Default: 60 (1 hour)

  // Loss threshold to trigger circuit breaker
  lossThresholdSol: number;      // Default: 0.5 SOL
  lossThresholdUsd: number;      // Default: 100 USD

  // Consecutive loss threshold (alternative trigger)
  maxConsecutiveLosses: number;  // Default: 3

  // Cooldown before override is allowed
  overrideCooldownSeconds: number; // Default: 60

  // Override requires typed confirmation
  overrideConfirmationText: string; // Default: "I understand the risks"
}
```



### Rolling PNL Computation

```typescript
interface CircuitBreakerState {
  userId: string;
  windowStartAt: Date;
  windowPnlSol: Decimal;
  isTripped: boolean;
  trippedAt: Date | null;
  overrideUntil: Date | null;
  consecutiveLosses: number;
}

async function updateCircuitBreaker(
  userId: string,
  tradePnlSol: Decimal,
  config: CircuitBreakerConfig
): Promise<{ isTripped: boolean; reason: string }> {
  const now = new Date();

  // Get or create state
  let state = await db.query.circuitBreakerState.findFirst({
    where: eq(circuitBreakerState.userId, userId),
  });

  if (!state) {
    state = await db.insert(circuitBreakerState).values({
      userId,
      windowStartAt: now,
      windowPnlSol: "0",
      isTripped: false,
      consecutiveLosses: 0,
    }).returning().then(r => r[0]);
  }

  // Check if window has expired
  const windowEnd = new Date(state.windowStartAt.getTime() + config.windowDurationMinutes * 60 * 1000);
  if (now > windowEnd) {
    // Reset window
    await db.update(circuitBreakerState)
      .set({
        windowStartAt: now,
        windowPnlSol: tradePnlSol.toString(),
        isTripped: false,
        trippedAt: null,
        consecutiveLosses: tradePnlSol.lessThan(0) ? 1 : 0,
      })
      .where(eq(circuitBreakerState.userId, userId));
    return { isTripped: false, reason: "Window reset" };
  }

  // Update rolling PNL
  const newPnl = new Decimal(state.windowPnlSol.toString()).add(tradePnlSol);
  const newConsecutiveLosses = tradePnlSol.lessThan(0)
    ? state.consecutiveLosses + 1
    : 0;

  // Check thresholds
  const pnlThresholdExceeded = newPnl.lessThan(-config.lossThresholdSol);
  const consecutiveThresholdExceeded = newConsecutiveLosses >= config.maxConsecutiveLosses;

  if (pnlThresholdExceeded || consecutiveThresholdExceeded) {
    await db.update(circuitBreakerState)
      .set({
        windowPnlSol: newPnl.toString(),
        isTripped: true,
        trippedAt: now,
        consecutiveLosses: newConsecutiveLosses,
      })
      .where(eq(circuitBreakerState.userId, userId));

    // Notify user
    await sendNotification(userId, {
      type: "system",
      title: "🛑 Circuit Breaker Tripped",
      body: `Trading halted. Loss: ${newPnl.abs().toFixed(4)} SOL in last ${config.windowDurationMinutes}min. ` +
            `Override available in ${config.overrideCooldownSeconds}s with typed confirmation.`,
    });

    return {
      isTripped: true,
      reason: pnlThresholdExceeded
        ? `Rolling PNL loss exceeded: ${newPnl.toFixed(4)} SOL`
        : `Consecutive losses exceeded: ${newConsecutiveLosses}`,
    };
  }

  // Update state (not tripped)
  await db.update(circuitBreakerState)
    .set({
      windowPnlSol: newPnl.toString(),
      consecutiveLosses: newConsecutiveLosses,
    })
    .where(eq(circuitBreakerState.userId, userId));

  return { isTripped: false, reason: "Within thresholds" };
}
```



### Override Flow (60s + Typed Confirmation)

```typescript
async function requestCircuitBreakerOverride(
  userId: string,
  confirmationText: string,
  config: CircuitBreakerConfig
): Promise<{ success: boolean; error?: string }> {
  const state = await db.query.circuitBreakerState.findFirst({
    where: eq(circuitBreakerState.userId, userId),
  });

  if (!state || !state.isTripped) {
    return { success: false, error: "Circuit breaker is not tripped" };
  }

  // Check cooldown
  const trippedAt = state.trippedAt;
  if (!trippedAt) {
    return { success: false, error: "Invalid state: tripped but no timestamp" };
  }

  const cooldownEnd = new Date(trippedAt.getTime() + config.overrideCooldownSeconds * 1000);
  const now = new Date();

  if (now < cooldownEnd) {
    const remainingSeconds = Math.ceil((cooldownEnd.getTime() - now.getTime()) / 1000);
    return {
      success: false,
      error: `Cooldown active. ${remainingSeconds}s remaining before override is allowed.`,
    };
  }

  // Verify typed confirmation
  if (confirmationText !== config.overrideConfirmationText) {
    return {
      success: false,
      error: `Confirmation text mismatch. Required: "${config.overrideConfirmationText}"`,
    };
  }

  // Apply override
  const overrideDuration = 60 * 60 * 1000; // 1 hour override
  await db.update(circuitBreakerState)
    .set({
      isTripped: false,
      overrideUntil: new Date(now.getTime() + overrideDuration),
      windowStartAt: now, // Reset window
      windowPnlSol: "0",
      consecutiveLosses: 0,
    })
    .where(eq(circuitBreakerState.userId, userId));

  // Log for audit
  await db.insert(auditLogs).values({
    userId,
    action: "CIRCUIT_BREAKER_OVERRIDE",
    details: { previousTrippedAt: trippedAt, overrideAt: now },
  });

  return { success: true };
}
```



### Integration with Trade Pipeline

Every trade job checks the circuit breaker before execution:

```typescript
async function executeTrade(job: PgBoss.Job<TradeJobData>) {
  // Check circuit breaker
  const cbState = await db.query.circuitBreakerState.findFirst({
    where: eq(circuitBreakerState.userId, job.data.userId),
  });

  if (cbState?.isTripped) {
    // Check if override is active
    const now = new Date();
    if (!cbState.overrideUntil || now > cbState.overrideUntil) {
      throw new Error("CIRCUIT_BREAKER_TRIPPED: Trading halted due to loss threshold");
    }
  }

  // ... proceed with trade
}
```

ADDENDUM G: SOLANA VERIFIABLE BUILDS — COMPLETE REFERENCE
================================================================================

Verified builds ensure that the executable program deployed to Solana's network matches the source code in the repository. The verification process compares the hash of the onchain program with the hash of the locally built program from source code.



### Solana Verify CLI Installation

```bash
# Install Docker first (required for deterministic builds)
# https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/

# Install Cargo/Rust
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh

# Install Solana Verify CLI
cargo install solana-verify

# Pin to specific version if needed:
cargo install solana-verify --version $VERSION

# Or install from specific commit:
cargo install solana-verify --git https://github.com/Ellipsis-Labs/solana-verifiable-build --rev 13a1db2
```



### Verifying a Program from Repository

```bash
# Basic verification
solana-verify verify-from-repo -um --program-id <PROGRAM_ID> https://github.com/<ORG>/<REPO>

# With specific commit hash
solana-verify verify-from-repo -um --program-id <PROGRAM_ID> https://github.com/<ORG>/<REPO> --commit-hash <COMMIT_HASH>

# With library name (for repos with multiple programs)
solana-verify verify-from-repo -um --program-id <PROGRAM_ID> https://github.com/<ORG>/<REPO> --library-name <PROGRAM_LIB_NAME>

# For Anchor programs, add --bpf flag
solana-verify verify-from-repo -um --program-id <PROGRAM_ID> https://github.com/<ORG>/<REPO> --library-name <NAME> --bpf

# With mount path (for programs in subfolders)
solana-verify verify-from-repo -um --program-id <PROGRAM_ID> https://github.com/<ORG>/<REPO> --mount-path <PATH_TO_PROGRAM_FOLDER>
```



### Verifying from Docker Image

```bash
# Verify against pre-built Docker image (faster, no rebuild)
solana-verify verify-from-image   -e <PATH_TO_EXECUTABLE_IN_CONTAINER>   -i <DOCKER_IMAGE>   -p <PROGRAM_ID>

# Example:
solana-verify verify-from-image   -e examples/hello_world/target/deploy/hello_world.so   -i ellipsislabs/hello_world_verifiable_build:latest   -p 2ZrriTQSVekoj414Ynysd48jyn4AX6ZF4TTJRqHfbJfn
```



### Getting Program Hash

```bash
# Get on-chain program hash
solana-verify get-program-hash <PROGRAM_ID>

# Get executable hash from local file
solana-verify get-executable-hash <PATH_TO_SO_FILE>
```



### Submitting Verification to OtterSec API

```bash
# Step 1: Verify from repo (uploads PDA onchain)
solana-verify verify-from-repo -um --program-id <PROGRAM_ID> https://github.com/<ORG>/<REPO>

# Step 2: Submit remote verification job
solana-verify remote submit-job --program-id <PROGRAM_ID> --uploader <UPGRADE_AUTHORITY_ADDRESS>

# Step 3: Check job status
solana-verify remote get-job --job-id <JOB_ID>
```

### Verification Status Check

```typescript
// Check if a program is verified
async function isProgramVerified(programId: string): Promise<boolean> {
  try {
    const response = await fetch(`https://verify.osec.io/status/${programId}`);
    const data = await response.json();
    return data.verified === true;
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

// Alternative: Check Solana Explorer or SolanaFM
```

### For Multisig-Controlled Programs (e.g., Squads)

```bash
# Returns base58 transaction to import into Squads transaction builder
```



### Trust Model

The verification system is designed to be trustless:
- **On-Chain PDA**: Verification metadata lives onchain, not controlled by any central authority
- **Upgrade Authority Proof**: Only the program's upgrade authority can create/update the PDA
- **Independent Verification**: Anyone can verify by reading the PDA and running `solana-verify` locally
- **Continuous Re-verification**: The API automatically re-verifies all programs every 24 hours

**Limitations**:
- Verification confirms source matches deployment — NOT that the code is secure
- Verified ≠ audited, or safe
- Always review code before interacting with programs
- The verify program itself (deployed by OtterSec) is not yet frozen and can be upgraded



### Integration with SAF-05

For Token-2022 safety checks, verification status should be checked for:
1. The Token-2022 program itself (`TokenzQdBNbLqP5VEhdkAS6EPFLC1PHnBqCXEpPxuEb`) — Verified by Solana Foundation
2. Any transfer hook programs referenced by tokens
3. Any metadata pointer programs
4. The PumpSwap AMM program

Unverified programs with upgrade authority carry higher risk.

### WebSocket Client Implementation

```typescript
import WebSocket from "ws";

class HeliusWebSocketClient {
  private ws: WebSocket | null = null;
  private apiKey: string;
  private subscriptions = new Map<number, string>();
  private nextId = 1;
  private reconnectDelay = 1000;
  private maxReconnectDelay = 30000;
  private pendingRequests = new Map<number, { resolve: Function; reject: Function }>();

  constructor(apiKey: string) {
    this.apiKey = apiKey;
  }

  connect(): Promise<void> {
    return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
      this.ws = new WebSocket(`wss://mainnet.helius-rpc.com/?api-key=${this.apiKey}`);

      this.ws.on("open", () => {
        console.log("[Helius WS] Connected");
        this.reconnectDelay = 1000;
        resolve();
      });

      this.ws.on("message", (data) => {
        const message = JSON.parse(data.toString());
        this.handleMessage(message);
      });

      this.ws.on("close", () => {
        console.log("[Helius WS] Disconnected, reconnecting...");
        setTimeout(() => this.connect(), this.reconnectDelay);
        this.reconnectDelay = Math.min(this.reconnectDelay * 2, this.maxReconnectDelay);
      });

      this.ws.on("error", (err) => {
        console.error("[Helius WS] Error:", err);
        reject(err);
      });
    });
  }

  private handleMessage(message: any) {
    // Handle subscription responses
    if (message.id !== undefined && this.pendingRequests.has(message.id)) {
      const { resolve, reject } = this.pendingRequests.get(message.id)!;
      this.pendingRequests.delete(message.id);
      if (message.error) {
        reject(message.error);
      } else {
        resolve(message.result);
      }
      return;
    }

    // Handle notifications
    if (message.method) {
      const subscriptionId = message.params?.subscription;
      const handler = this.subscriptions.get(subscriptionId);
      if (handler) {
        // Route to appropriate handler
        this.emit(handler, message.params.result);
      }
    }
  }

  async subscribe(method: string, params: any[]): Promise<number> {
    const id = this.nextId++;
    return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
      this.pendingRequests.set(id, { resolve, reject });
      this.ws?.send(JSON.stringify({
        jsonrpc: "2.0",
        id,
        method,
        params,
      }));
    });
  }

  async unsubscribe(subscriptionId: number, method: string): Promise<void> {
    const id = this.nextId++;
    return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
      this.pendingRequests.set(id, { resolve, reject });
      this.ws?.send(JSON.stringify({
        jsonrpc: "2.0",
        id,
        method,
        params: [subscriptionId],
      }));
    });
  }

  private emit(event: string, data: any) {
    // Implement event emission
  }

  disconnect() {
    this.ws?.close();
  }
}
```

```typescript
// Subscribe to transactions involving target wallets
async function setupCopyTradingWebhooks(
  client: HeliusWebSocketClient,
  targetWallets: string[]
): Promise<number> {
  const subscriptionId = await client.subscribe("transactionSubscribe", [
    {
      vote: false,
      failed: false,
      accountInclude: targetWallets, // Up to 50,000 wallets
      accountExclude: [],
      accountRequired: [],
    },
    {
      commitment: "confirmed",
      encoding: "jsonParsed",
      transactionDetails: "full",
      showRewards: false,
      maxSupportedTransactionVersion: 0,
    },
  ]);

  return subscriptionId;
}
```

================================================================================
ADDENDUM K: LOAD BALANCING, CACHING & PERFORMANCE ARCHITECTURE
================================================================================

User asked: "Is there any way to add load balancing and caching and should we? Because I want it to be as fast as possible, so I don't want the servers to be overbearing and stuff with the database."

Short answer: YES. You absolutely need both. For a trading bot where milliseconds matter, load balancing and caching are not optional — they are the difference between landing a trade and watching it fail. Here's the complete architecture.

---



## PART 1: SOLANA RPC CONNECTION POOL & LOAD BALANCING



### Why Multiple RPC Endpoints?

A single RPC endpoint is a single point of failure. During network congestion, NFT mints, or airdrops, shared endpoints can spike to 1000+ ms latency or drop requests entirely. cite🛠web_search:20#6:~:text=Shared nodes pool traffic from many customers...vulnerable to noisy neighbors, rate limiting, and unpredictable congestion

For OSIRIS, you need:
1. **Primary**: Helius (staked, Solana-native, DAS API, webhooks)
2. **Secondary**: GetBlock or Triton One (lowest latency backup)
3. **Fallback**: dRPC (decentralized aggregator, automatic failover)



### Multi-Provider Connection Pool Implementation

```typescript
// src/lib/solana-connection-pool.ts
import { Connection, PublicKey, Commitment } from "@solana/web3.js";

interface RpcEndpoint {
  name: string;
  httpUrl: string;
  wsUrl: string;
  priority: number;        // Lower = higher priority
  weight: number;          // For weighted round-robin
  region: string;          // "us-east", "eu-west", "asia-sg"
  features: string[];      // ["staked", "jito", "geyser", "swqos"]
  maxRps: number;          // Rate limit
  currentRps: number;      // Tracked in-memory
  failedRequests: number;  // Health tracking
  lastUsed: number;        // Timestamp
  isHealthy: boolean;
}

interface ConnectionPoolConfig {
  endpoints: RpcEndpoint[];
  healthCheckIntervalMs: number;
  circuitBreakerThreshold: number; // Failed requests before marking unhealthy
  circuitBreakerResetMs: number;   // Time before retrying unhealthy endpoint
  defaultCommitment: Commitment;
}

class SolanaConnectionPool {
  private endpoints: RpcEndpoint[];
  private connections: Map<string, Connection> = new Map();
  private wsConnections: Map<string, WebSocket> = new Map();
  private config: ConnectionPoolConfig;
  private healthCheckTimer: NodeJS.Timeout | null = null;

  constructor(config: ConnectionPoolConfig) {
    this.endpoints = config.endpoints;
    this.config = config;
    this.initializeConnections();
    this.startHealthChecks();
  }

  private initializeConnections() {
    for (const ep of this.endpoints) {
      const conn = new Connection(ep.httpUrl, {
        wsEndpoint: ep.wsUrl,
        commitment: this.config.defaultCommitment,
        confirmTransactionInitialTimeout: 60000,
      });
      this.connections.set(ep.name, conn);
    }
  }

  // STRATEGY 1: Weighted Round-Robin for reads
  getConnectionForRead(): Connection {
    const healthy = this.endpoints.filter((e) => e.isHealthy);
    if (healthy.length === 0) {
      throw new Error("All RPC endpoints unhealthy");
    }

    // Weighted selection based on priority + current load
    const totalWeight = healthy.reduce((sum, e) => sum + e.weight, 0);
    let random = Math.random() * totalWeight;

    for (const ep of healthy) {
      random -= ep.weight;
      if (random <= 0) {
        ep.currentRps++;
        ep.lastUsed = Date.now();
        return this.connections.get(ep.name)!;
      }
    }

    return this.connections.get(healthy[0].name)!;
  }

  // STRATEGY 2: Fastest endpoint wins for time-critical operations
  async getFastestConnection(
    operation: "getAccountInfo" | "getLatestBlockhash" | "sendTransaction",
    timeoutMs: number = 500
  ): Promise<Connection> {
    const healthy = this.endpoints.filter((e) => e.isHealthy);

    const races = healthy.map(async (ep) => {
      const conn = this.connections.get(ep.name)!;
      const start = performance.now();
      try {
        if (operation === "getLatestBlockhash") {
          await conn.getLatestBlockhash();
        } else if (operation === "getAccountInfo") {
          await conn.getAccountInfo(SystemProgram.programId);
        }
        const latency = performance.now() - start;
        return { conn, latency, name: ep.name };
      } catch {
        return { conn, latency: Infinity, name: ep.name };
      }
    });

    const winner = await Promise.race(races);
    return winner.conn;
  }

  // STRATEGY 3: Geographic affinity (route users to nearest endpoint)
  getConnectionForRegion(userRegion: string): Connection {
    const regional = this.endpoints.filter(
      (e) => e.isHealthy && e.region === userRegion
    );
    if (regional.length > 0) {
      return this.connections.get(regional[0].name)!;
    }
    return this.getConnectionForRead();
  }

  // STRATEGY 4: Staked endpoint for sends (higher landing rate)
  getConnectionForSend(): Connection {
    const staked = this.endpoints.filter(
      (e) => e.isHealthy && e.features.includes("swqos")
    );
    if (staked.length > 0) {
      return this.connections.get(staked[0].name)!;
    }
    return this.getConnectionForRead();
  }

  // Health checks
  private async startHealthChecks() {
    const check = async () => {
      for (const ep of this.endpoints) {
        try {
          const conn = this.connections.get(ep.name)!;
          const slot = await conn.getSlot();
          const currentSlot = await this.getReferenceSlot();

          // Mark unhealthy if lagging > 5 slots or failing
          if (currentSlot - slot > 5) {
            ep.failedRequests++;
          } else {
            ep.failedRequests = Math.max(0, ep.failedRequests - 1);
          }

          ep.isHealthy = ep.failedRequests < this.config.circuitBreakerThreshold;
          ep.currentRps = 0; // Reset per-interval
        } catch {
          ep.failedRequests++;
          ep.isHealthy = ep.failedRequests < this.config.circuitBreakerThreshold;
        }
      }
    };

    await check();
    this.healthCheckTimer = setInterval(check, this.config.healthCheckIntervalMs);
  }

  private async getReferenceSlot(): Promise<number> {
    // Use fastest endpoint as reference
    const conn = this.getConnectionForRead();
    return conn.getSlot();
  }

  // Parallel reads for critical data (first to respond wins)
  async parallelRead<T>(
    operation: (conn: Connection) => Promise<T>,
    minResponses: number = 1
  ): Promise<T> {
    const healthy = this.endpoints.filter((e) => e.isHealthy);
    const promises = healthy.map((ep) =>
      operation(this.connections.get(ep.name)!).then((result) => ({
        result,
        name: ep.name,
      }))
    );

    // Race: return first successful response
    const winner = await Promise.race(promises);
    return winner.result;
  }

  // Parallel confirmation monitoring
  async confirmTransaction(
    signature: string,
    commitment: Commitment = "confirmed"
  ): Promise<any> {
    const healthy = this.endpoints.filter((e) => e.isHealthy);

    const promises = healthy.map((ep) =>
      this.connections
        .get(ep.name)!
        .confirmTransaction(signature, commitment)
        .then((result) => ({ result, name: ep.name }))
        .catch(() => ({ result: null, name: ep.name }))
    );

    // Wait for first successful confirmation from any endpoint
    for (const promise of promises) {
      const { result } = await promise;
      if (result) return result;
    }

    throw new Error("Transaction confirmation failed on all endpoints");
  }

  destroy() {
    if (this.healthCheckTimer) clearInterval(this.healthCheckTimer);
    for (const ws of this.wsConnections.values()) {
      ws.close();
    }
  }
}

// Configuration for OSIRIS
export const connectionPool = new SolanaConnectionPool({
  endpoints: [
    {
      name: "helius-primary",
      httpUrl: process.env.HELIUS_RPC_URL!,
      wsUrl: process.env.HELIUS_WS_URL!,
      priority: 1,
      weight: 50,
      region: "us-east",
      features: ["staked", "jito", "webhooks", "enhanced-api"],

      currentRps: 0,
      failedRequests: 0,
      lastUsed: 0,
      isHealthy: true,
    },
    {
      name: "getblock-backup",
      httpUrl: process.env.GETBLOCK_RPC_URL!,

      name: "drpc-fallback",
      httpUrl: process.env.DRPC_RPC_URL!,
      wsUrl: process.env.DRPC_WS_URL!,
      priority: 3,
      weight: 20,

      maxRps: 300,
      currentRps: 0,
      failedRequests: 0,
      lastUsed: 0,

  defaultCommitment: "confirmed",
});
```



### Endpoint Selection Strategy by Operation

| Operation | Strategy | Reason |
|-----------|----------|--------|
| `getLatestBlockhash` | Fastest endpoint wins | Blockhash expires in ~90s, stale = failed tx |
| `getAccountInfo` | Weighted round-robin | Read-heavy, distribute load |
| `getMultipleAccounts` | Weighted round-robin | Batch reads, distribute load |
| `sendTransaction` | Staked endpoint (SWQoS) | Higher landing rate under congestion |
| `confirmTransaction` | Parallel across all endpoints | First confirmation wins, reduces wait time |
| `simulateTransaction` | Fastest endpoint wins | Pre-flight validation must be fast |
| WebSocket subscriptions | Regional affinity | Lower latency for real-time data |



### Cost-Optimized Provider Setup (Free Tier)

```
Helius (Free): 1M credits/month
  - Primary RPC + WebSocket
  - Enhanced APIs (DAS, parsed transactions)
  - Webhooks (copy trading)
  - Sender API (transaction submission)

GetBlock (Free): 40M requests/month
  - Backup RPC for reads
  - No WebSocket on free tier
  - Use for batch account queries

dRPC (Free): 210M CU/month
  - Fallback for reads
  - Aggregated routing
  - Use when Helius/GetBlock rate-limited
```

## PART 2: REDIS CACHING STRATEGY



### Why Redis?

Your PostgreSQL database will be hammered by:
- Token metadata lookups (every trade needs decimals, symbol, isToken2022)
- Jupiter quote caching (same pair quoted repeatedly)
- Account balance checks (before every trade)
- PNL calculations (aggregated per wallet, per token)
- Session state checks (every job handler checks session status)

Without caching, you'll hit database connection limits and add 10-50ms of latency per query. Redis keeps hot data in memory with <1ms access time.



### Cache-Aside Strategy (Primary Pattern)

```typescript
// src/lib/cache.ts
import { createClient, RedisClientType } from "redis";

class CacheManager {
  private client: RedisClientType;
  private defaultTtl: number;

  constructor(redisUrl: string, defaultTtlSeconds: number = 300) {
    this.client = createClient({ url: redisUrl });
    this.defaultTtl = defaultTtlSeconds;
    this.client.connect();
  }

  // Cache-aside: check cache first, fetch from DB if miss
  async getOrSet<T>(
    key: string,
    fetchFn: () => Promise<T>,
    ttlSeconds?: number
  ): Promise<T> {
    const cached = await this.client.get(key);
    if (cached) {
      return JSON.parse(cached);
    }

    const data = await fetchFn();
    await this.client.setEx(
      key,
      ttlSeconds || this.defaultTtl,
      JSON.stringify(data)
    );
    return data;
  }

  // With distributed lock to prevent thundering herd
  async getOrSetWithLock<T>(
    key: string,
    fetchFn: () => Promise<T>,
    ttlSeconds?: number,
    lockTimeoutMs: number = 10000
  ): Promise<T> {
    const cached = await this.client.get(key);
    if (cached) {
      return JSON.parse(cached);
    }

    const lockKey = `lock:${key}`;
    const lockValue = crypto.randomUUID();

    // Try to acquire lock
    const acquired = await this.client.set(lockKey, lockValue, {
      NX: true,
      PX: lockTimeoutMs,
    });

    if (acquired) {
      try {
        const data = await fetchFn();
        await this.client.setEx(
          key,
          ttlSeconds || this.defaultTtl,
          JSON.stringify(data)
        );
        return data;
      } finally {
        // Release lock (only if we still own it)
        const currentLock = await this.client.get(lockKey);
        if (currentLock === lockValue) {
          await this.client.del(lockKey);
        }
      }
    }

    // Another process is fetching, wait and retry
    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 50));
    return this.getOrSetWithLock(key, fetchFn, ttlSeconds, lockTimeoutMs);
  }

  async invalidate(key: string): Promise<void> {
    await this.client.del(key);
  }

  async invalidatePattern(pattern: string): Promise<void> {
    const keys = await this.client.keys(pattern);
    if (keys.length > 0) {
      await this.client.del(keys);
    }
  }

  async get<T>(key: string): Promise<T | null> {
    const cached = await this.client.get(key);
    return cached ? JSON.parse(cached) : null;
  }

  async set<T>(key: string, value: T, ttlSeconds?: number): Promise<void> {
    if (ttlSeconds) {
      await this.client.setEx(key, ttlSeconds, JSON.stringify(value));
    } else {
      await this.client.set(key, JSON.stringify(value));
    }
  }
}

export const cache = new CacheManager(process.env.REDIS_URL!);
```



### Cache Key Strategy

```typescript
// src/lib/cache-keys.ts
export const cacheKeys = {
  // Token metadata (rarely changes)
  tokenMetadata: (mint: string) => `token:metadata:${mint}`,
  tokenDecimals: (mint: string) => `token:decimals:${mint}`,
  token2022Extensions: (mint: string) => `token:t2022:${mint}`,

  // Jupiter quotes (short TTL, price-sensitive)
  jupiterQuote: (inputMint: string, outputMint: string, amount: string) =>
    `jupiter:quote:${inputMint}:${outputMint}:${amount}`,

  // Account balances (medium TTL, changes on trades)
  accountBalance: (address: string, mint: string) =>
    `balance:${address}:${mint}`,
  solBalance: (address: string) => `balance:sol:${address}`,

  // PNL data (short TTL for unrealized, long for realized)
  position: (walletId: string, mint: string) =>
    `position:${walletId}:${mint}`,
  realizedPnl: (walletId: string) => `pnl:realized:${walletId}`,
  unrealizedPnl: (walletId: string) => `pnl:unrealized:${walletId}`,

  // Session state (very short TTL, critical for revocation speed)
  session: (sessionId: string) => `session:${sessionId}`,
  activeSession: (userId: string) => `session:active:${userId}`,

  // Circuit breaker state (short TTL)
  circuitBreaker: (userId: string) => `circuit:${userId}`,

  // Rate limits (exact TTL = window duration)
  rateLimit: (userId: string, action: string) =>
    `ratelimit:${userId}:${action}`,

  // Copy trading targets (medium TTL)
  copyTargets: (userId: string) => `copy:targets:${userId}`,

  // External API responses
  dexscreenerPrice: (mint: string) => `dexscreener:price:${mint}`,
  birdeyePrice: (mint: string) => `birdeye:price:${mint}`,
  rugcheckReport: (mint: string) => `rugcheck:${mint}`,

  // Program verification status (long TTL, rarely changes)
  programVerified: (programId: string) => `program:verified:${programId}`,
};
```



### TTL Strategy by Data Type

| Data Type | TTL | Reason |
|-----------|-----|--------|
| Token metadata | 1 hour | Changes rarely (only if metadata updated) |
| Token-2022 extensions | 5 minutes | Authority can change, but infrequently |
| Jupiter quotes | 10 seconds | Prices change every slot (~400ms) |
| Account balances | 30 seconds | Changes on every trade/deposit |
| SOL balance | 15 seconds | Critical for trade execution |
| Position data | 30 seconds | Unrealized PNL changes with price |
| Realized PNL | 5 minutes | Only changes on completed trades |
| Session state | 10 seconds | Must reflect revocation immediately |
| Circuit breaker | 10 seconds | Must reflect trips immediately |
| Rate limits | Exact window | e.g., 60s for per-minute limits |
| DexScreener price | 30 seconds | Price data |
| Birdeye price | 15 seconds | More frequent price updates |
| RugCheck report | 1 hour | Risk scores change slowly |
| Program verification | 24 hours | Verification status rarely changes |



### Token Metadata Caching with Write-Through

```typescript
// src/services/safety/token2022.ts
async function getTokenMetadata(mint: string): Promise<TokenMetadata> {
  return cache.getOrSetWithLock(
    cacheKeys.tokenMetadata(mint),
    async () => {
      // 1. Check database first
      const dbRecord = await db.query.tokenMetadata.findFirst({
        where: eq(tokenMetadata.mint, mint),
      });

      if (dbRecord) {
        return dbRecord;
      }

      // 2. Fetch from Jupiter token list
      const jupiterToken = await fetchJupiterToken(mint);
      if (jupiterToken) {
        const record = {
          mint,
          name: jupiterToken.name,
          symbol: jupiterToken.symbol,
          decimals: jupiterToken.decimals,
          logoUri: jupiterToken.logoURI,
          isToken2022: false,
          isVerified: true,
        };
        // Write-through to DB
        await db.insert(tokenMetadata).values(record).onConflictDoNothing();
        return record;
      }

      // 3. Fallback: on-chain fetch
      const onChainData = await fetchOnChainTokenData(mint);
      await db.insert(tokenMetadata).values(onChainData).onConflictDoNothing();
      return onChainData;
    },
    3600 // 1 hour TTL
  );
}
```



### Jupiter Quote Caching (Short TTL)

```typescript
// src/lib/jupiter.ts
async function getCachedQuote(
  inputMint: string,
  outputMint: string,
  amount: string,
  slippageBps: number
): Promise<QuoteResponse | null> {
  const cacheKey = cacheKeys.jupiterQuote(inputMint, outputMint, amount);

  // Try cache first (very short TTL)
  const cached = await cache.get<QuoteResponse>(cacheKey);
  if (cached) {
    // Verify quote hasn't expired (blockhash valid for ~90s)
    const age = Date.now() - (cached as any)._cachedAt;
    if (age < 5000) { // 5 seconds max
      return cached;
    }
  }

  // Fetch fresh quote
  const quote = await fetchJupiterQuote({
    inputMint,
    outputMint,
    amount,
    slippageBps,
  });

  // Cache with metadata
  (quote as any)._cachedAt = Date.now();
  await cache.set(cacheKey, quote, 10); // 10 seconds TTL

  return quote;
}
```



### Session State Caching (Critical Path)

Session revocation must be the fastest path in the system. Cache session status with very short TTL + immediate invalidation on revoke:

```typescript
// src/services/trading/session.ts
async function getSessionStatus(sessionId: string): Promise<SessionStatus> {
  return cache.getOrSet(
    cacheKeys.session(sessionId),
    async () => {
      const session = await db.query.tradingSessions.findFirst({
        where: eq(tradingSessions.id, sessionId),
      });
      return session?.status || "revoked";
    },
    10 // 10 seconds TTL
  );
}

async function revokeSession(sessionId: string): Promise<void> {
  // 1. Update DB
  await db
    .update(tradingSessions)
    .set({ status: "revoked", revokedAt: new Date() })
    .where(eq(tradingSessions.id, sessionId));

  // 2. IMMEDIATELY invalidate cache
  await cache.invalidate(cacheKeys.session(sessionId));

  // 3. Also invalidate active session cache for user
  const session = await db.query.tradingSessions.findFirst({
    where: eq(tradingSessions.id, sessionId),
  });
  if (session) {
    await cache.invalidate(cacheKeys.activeSession(session.userId));
  }
}
```

### Connection Pool Sizing

| Scenario | Pool Size | Reason |
|----------|-----------|--------|
| Single Next.js instance | 10-15 | Limited by Node.js event loop |
| PM2 cluster (4 instances) | 20 each = 80 total | Each process has its own pool |
| Dedicated worker process | 10 | Workers are job-heavy, not query-heavy |
| Total DB connections | 100 | PostgreSQL default max = 100 |

If you need more than 100 concurrent connections, add PgBouncer as a connection pooler:

```yaml
# docker-compose.yml (add PgBouncer)
  pgbouncer:
    image: pgbouncer/pgbouncer:latest
    environment:
      DATABASES_HOST: postgres
      DATABASES_PORT: 5432
      DATABASES_DATABASE: osiris
      DATABASES_USER: osiris
      POOL_MODE: transaction  # Best for ORM workloads
      MAX_CLIENT_CONN: 1000
      DEFAULT_POOL_SIZE: 25
      RESERVE_POOL_SIZE: 5
    ports:
      - "6432:6432"
```

Then update DATABASE_URL to point to PgBouncer:
```
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://osiris:${DB_PASSWORD}@localhost:6432/osiris
```

### Why pg-boss Scales Horizontally

pg-boss uses PostgreSQL's `SKIP LOCKED` to ensure no two workers pick up the same job. cite🛠web_search:20#1:~:text=pg-boss's SKIP LOCKED ensures no two instances process the same job. This makes horizontal scaling natural: add more application instances and queue throughput increases proportionally

This means:
- You can run multiple `osiris-pg-boss` instances
- Each picks up jobs independently
- No duplicate processing
- Throughput scales linearly with instances



### Load Balancing Across PM2 Instances

Caddy reverse proxy with upstream health checks:

```
# /etc/caddy/Caddyfile
osiris.trade {
    # Load balance across PM2 instances
    reverse_proxy localhost:3000 localhost:3001 localhost:3002 localhost:3003 {
        lb_policy round_robin
        health_uri /api/health
        health_interval 10s
        health_timeout 5s
    }

    tls {
        dns cloudflare {env.CF_API_TOKEN}
    }
}
```

Note: PM2 cluster mode handles port binding internally. When `instances: "max"` with `exec_mode: "cluster"`, PM2 binds all instances to the same port (3000) and load balances internally. Caddy just proxies to localhost:3000.

## PART 5: RATE LIMITING & BACKPRESSURE



### Redis-Based Rate Limiting

```typescript
// src/lib/rate-limiter.ts
import { cache } from "./cache";

interface RateLimitConfig {
  windowSeconds: number;
  maxRequests: number;
}

async function checkRateLimit(
  key: string,
  config: RateLimitConfig
): Promise<{ allowed: boolean; remaining: number; resetAt: number }> {
  const now = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);
  const windowStart = Math.floor(now / config.windowSeconds) * config.windowSeconds;
  const redisKey = `ratelimit:${key}:${windowStart}`;

  const current = await cache.client.incr(redisKey);
  if (current === 1) {
    // Set expiry on first request
    await cache.client.expire(redisKey, config.windowSeconds);
  }

  const remaining = Math.max(0, config.maxRequests - current);
  const resetAt = windowStart + config.windowSeconds;

  return {
    allowed: current <= config.maxRequests,
    remaining,
    resetAt,
  };
}

// Per-user trade rate limits
export async function checkTradeRateLimit(userId: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const { allowed } = await checkRateLimit(`trade:${userId}`, {
    windowSeconds: 60,
    maxRequests: 10, // 10 trades per minute per user
  });
  return allowed;
}

// Per-IP API rate limits
export async function checkApiRateLimit(ip: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const { allowed } = await checkRateLimit(`api:${ip}`, {
    windowSeconds: 60,
    maxRequests: 100, // 100 requests per minute per IP
  });
  return allowed;
}
```



### Backpressure for Queue Depth

```typescript
// src/jobs/manager.ts (updated with backpressure)
class JobManager {
  private async checkBackpressure(): Promise<boolean> {
    // Check queue depth
    const queueDepth = await this.boss.getQueueSize("trade:quote");
    const maxDepth = 1000;

    if (queueDepth > maxDepth) {
      logger.warn("Queue backpressure detected", { queueDepth, maxDepth });
      return true; // Backpressure active
    }
    return false;
  }

  async send<T>(name: string, data: T, options?: PgBoss.SendOptions): Promise<string | null> {
    if (await this.checkBackpressure()) {
      // Drop non-critical jobs during backpressure
      if (name.startsWith("copy:")) {
        logger.warn("Dropping copy trade due to backpressure");
        return null;
      }
      // Delay critical jobs
      options = { ...options, startAfter: 30 };
    }
    return this.boss.send(name, data, options);
  }
}
```

## PART 6: COMPLETE PERFORMANCE BUDGET



### Target Latencies

| Operation | Target | Max Acceptable | Optimization |
|-----------|--------|----------------|--------------|
| Jupiter quote | < 500ms | 2s | Cache 5s, parallel RPC |
| Transaction build | < 200ms | 1s | Pre-compute ATAs |
| Transaction sign | < 50ms | 200ms | KEK in memory, ephemeral keys |
| Helius Sender submit | < 100ms | 500ms | Regional endpoint, skip preflight |
| Confirmation (confirmed) | < 5s | 15s | Parallel confirmation across RPCs |
| Session revocation | < 50ms | 200ms | Cache invalidation, no DB read |
| Copy trade (webhook→send) | < 2s | 5s | Pre-warmed connections, cached metadata |
| PNL update (unrealized) | < 100ms | 500ms | Cached prices, incremental calc |
| Token-2022 safety check | < 200ms | 1s | Cache extensions, parallel checks |
| Circuit breaker check | < 10ms | 50ms | Redis cache only |



### Performance Monitoring

```typescript
// src/lib/performance.ts
import { logger } from "./logger";

class PerformanceTracker {
  private histograms = new Map<string, number[]>();

  track(operation: string, durationMs: number) {
    if (!this.histograms.has(operation)) {
      this.histograms.set(operation, []);
    }
    this.histograms.get(operation)!.push(durationMs);

    // Log slow operations
    if (durationMs > 1000) {
      logger.warn("Slow operation detected", { operation, durationMs });
    }
  }

  getStats(operation: string) {
    const times = this.histograms.get(operation) || [];
    if (times.length === 0) return null;

    const sorted = [...times].sort((a, b) => a - b);
    const sum = sorted.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0);

    return {
      count: times.length,
      min: sorted[0],
      max: sorted[sorted.length - 1],
      mean: sum / times.length,
      p50: sorted[Math.floor(sorted.length * 0.5)],
      p95: sorted[Math.floor(sorted.length * 0.95)],
      p99: sorted[Math.floor(sorted.length * 0.99)],
    };
  }
}

export const perf = new PerformanceTracker();

// Middleware for API routes
export function withTiming(handler: Function, operation: string) {
  return async (...args: any[]) => {
    const start = performance.now();
    try {
      return await handler(...args);
    } finally {
      perf.track(operation, performance.now() - start);
    }
  };
}
```

================================================================================
ADDENDUM L: COMPLETE SECURITY ARCHITECTURE FOR OSIRIS
================================================================================

User asked: "I want this to be completely secure so they can trust me. So how can we implement security for that type of like how would we do it? Do deep research on this."

Short answer: Security for a trading bot handling real money requires defense in depth across 8 layers: key management, encryption, authentication, authorization, infrastructure, application, monitoring, and compliance. One breach = total loss of user funds and irreversible reputational damage. Here is the complete architecture.

---



## LAYER 1: KEY MANAGEMENT — THE FOUNDATION OF EVERYTHING



### Threat Model

The single most critical asset in OSIRIS is private keys. If an attacker gains access to a user's private key, they can drain the wallet instantly. Solana transactions are irreversible. There is no "undo" button.

Threats:
- Server compromise → attacker reads keys from filesystem/memory
- Database breach → attacker reads encrypted keys, needs KEK to decrypt
- Insider threat → employee with DB access tries to decrypt keys
- Memory dump → attacker dumps Node.js heap, finds decrypted DEK in memory
- Backup theft → attacker steals backups, has encrypted keys + potentially KEK
- Supply chain attack → compromised npm package steals keys at runtime



### Envelope Encryption with Hardware-Backed KEK

The spec already mentions envelope encryption (KEK/DEK). This is correct and industry-standard. But the KEK must live in hardware, not in an environment variable.

```typescript
// src/lib/crypto/envelope-encryption.ts
import { createCipheriv, createDecipheriv, randomBytes, scryptSync } from "crypto";

interface EncryptedData {
  ciphertext: string;      // base64
  iv: string;              // base64 (16 bytes)
  tag: string;             // base64 (16 bytes for GCM)
  encryptedDek: string;    // base64 (DEK encrypted by KEK)
  kekVersion: string;      // For key rotation tracking
}

interface DEK {
  key: Buffer;             // 32-byte AES-256 key
  id: string;              // Unique DEK identifier
  createdAt: Date;
}

// KEK Provider Interface — pluggable backends
interface KEKProvider {
  wrap(data: Buffer): Promise<Buffer>;      // Encrypt DEK with KEK
  unwrap(wrappedData: Buffer): Promise<Buffer>; // Decrypt DEK with KEK
  getCurrentVersion(): Promise<string>;
  rotate(): Promise<string>;                // Returns new version ID
}

// Implementation 1: AWS KMS (Production Recommended)
class AWSKMSProvider implements KEKProvider {
  private kmsClient: KMSClient;
  private keyId: string;

  constructor(region: string, keyId: string) {
    this.kmsClient = new KMSClient({ region });
    this.keyId = keyId;
  }

  async wrap(data: Buffer): Promise<Buffer> {
    const command = new EncryptCommand({
      KeyId: this.keyId,
      Plaintext: data,
    });
    const response = await this.kmsClient.send(command);
    return Buffer.from(response.CiphertextBlob!);
  }

  async unwrap(wrappedData: Buffer): Promise<Buffer> {
    const command = new DecryptCommand({
      CiphertextBlob: wrappedData,
      KeyId: this.keyId, // Optional but recommended for key binding
    });
    const response = await this.kmsClient.send(command);
    return Buffer.from(response.Plaintext!);
  }

  async getCurrentVersion(): Promise<string> {
    // AWS KMS tracks versions automatically
    return this.keyId;
  }

  async rotate(): Promise<string> {
    // AWS KMS handles automatic rotation
    // For manual rotation, create new key alias
    return this.keyId;
  }
}

// Implementation 2: HashiCorp Vault (Self-Hosted Alternative)
class VaultProvider implements KEKProvider {
  private vault: VaultClient;
  private transitKey: string;

  constructor(vaultAddr: string, token: string, transitKey: string) {
    this.vault = new VaultClient({
      apiVersion: "v1",
      endpoint: vaultAddr,
      token,
    });
    this.transitKey = transitKey;
  }

  async wrap(data: Buffer): Promise<Buffer> {
    const response = await this.vault.write(`transit/encrypt/${this.transitKey}`, {
      plaintext: data.toString("base64"),
    });
    return Buffer.from(response.data.ciphertext, "base64");
  }

  async unwrap(wrappedData: Buffer): Promise<Buffer> {
    const response = await this.vault.write(`transit/decrypt/${this.transitKey}`, {
      ciphertext: wrappedData.toString("base64"),
    });
    return Buffer.from(response.data.plaintext, "base64");
  }

  async getCurrentVersion(): Promise<string> {
    const response = await this.vault.read(`transit/keys/${this.transitKey}`);
    return response.data.latest_version.toString();
  }

  async rotate(): Promise<string> {
    await this.vault.write(`transit/keys/${this.transitKey}/rotate`, {});
    return this.getCurrentVersion();
  }
}

// Implementation 3: Google Cloud KMS
class GCPKMSProvider implements KEKProvider {
  private kmsClient: KeyManagementServiceClient;
  private keyName: string;

  constructor(projectId: string, location: string, keyRing: string, keyName: string) {
    this.kmsClient = new KeyManagementServiceClient();
    this.keyName = `projects/${projectId}/locations/${location}/keyRings/${keyRing}/cryptoKeys/${keyName}`;
  }

  async wrap(data: Buffer): Promise<Buffer> {
    const [result] = await this.kmsClient.encrypt({
      name: this.keyName,
      plaintext: data,
    });
    return Buffer.from(result.ciphertext!);
  }

  async unwrap(wrappedData: Buffer): Promise<Buffer> {
    const [result] = await this.kmsClient.decrypt({
      name: this.keyName,
      ciphertext: wrappedData,
    });
    return Buffer.from(result.plaintext!);
  }

  async getCurrentVersion(): Promise<string> {
    const [versions] = await this.kmsClient.listCryptoKeyVersions({
      parent: this.keyName,
      filter: "state=ENABLED",
    });
    return versions[0]?.name || this.keyName;
  }

  async rotate(): Promise<string> {
    const [version] = await this.kmsClient.createCryptoKeyVersion({
      parent: this.keyName,
    });
    return version.name!;
  }
}

// Envelope Encryption Service
class EnvelopeEncryptionService {
  private kekProvider: KEKProvider;

  constructor(kekProvider: KEKProvider) {
    this.kekProvider = kekProvider;
  }

  // Generate a fresh DEK and encrypt data
  async encrypt(plaintext: Buffer): Promise<EncryptedData> {
    // 1. Generate fresh DEK (32 bytes for AES-256)
    const dek = randomBytes(32);
    const dekId = crypto.randomUUID();

    // 2. Generate IV (16 bytes for AES-GCM)
    const iv = randomBytes(16);

    // 3. Encrypt data with DEK
    const cipher = createCipheriv("aes-256-gcm", dek, iv);
    const ciphertext = Buffer.concat([cipher.update(plaintext), cipher.final()]);
    const tag = cipher.getAuthTag();

    // 4. Wrap DEK with KEK
    const encryptedDek = await this.kekProvider.wrap(dek);

    // 5. Securely discard plaintext DEK from memory
    dek.fill(0);

    return {
      ciphertext: ciphertext.toString("base64"),
      iv: iv.toString("base64"),
      tag: tag.toString("base64"),
      encryptedDek: encryptedDek.toString("base64"),
      kekVersion: await this.kekProvider.getCurrentVersion(),
    };
  }

  // Decrypt data using envelope encryption
  async decrypt(encryptedData: EncryptedData): Promise<Buffer> {
    // 1. Unwrap DEK
    const encryptedDekBuffer = Buffer.from(encryptedData.encryptedDek, "base64");
    const dek = await this.kekProvider.unwrap(encryptedDekBuffer);

    try {
      // 2. Decrypt data
      const iv = Buffer.from(encryptedData.iv, "base64");
      const ciphertext = Buffer.from(encryptedData.ciphertext, "base64");
      const tag = Buffer.from(encryptedData.tag, "base64");

      const decipher = createDecipheriv("aes-256-gcm", dek, iv);
      decipher.setAuthTag(tag);

      const plaintext = Buffer.concat([
        decipher.update(ciphertext),
        decipher.final(),
      ]);

      return plaintext;
    } finally {
      // 3. Securely discard DEK from memory
      dek.fill(0);
    }
  }

  // Rotate KEK: re-encrypt all DEKs with new KEK version
  async rotateKEK(): Promise<void> {
    const newVersion = await this.kekProvider.rotate();
    logger.info("KEK rotated", { newVersion });

    // ACTION REQUIRED: Background job to re-wrap all existing encrypted DEKs
    // This is a batch operation that should run during low-traffic hours
  }
}

// Usage in OSIRIS
export const envelopeEncryption = new EnvelopeEncryptionService(
  new AWSKMSProvider(
    process.env.AWS_REGION!,
    process.env.AWS_KMS_KEY_ID!
  )
);
```



### Zero-Memory Signing Architecture

The spec mentions "zero-memory signing." This means the private key should never exist in plaintext in application memory for longer than absolutely necessary.

```typescript
// src/lib/crypto/zero-memory-signing.ts
import { Keypair, Transaction, VersionedTransaction } from "@solana/web3.js";

interface SecureKeypair {
  publicKey: string;
  // Private key is NEVER stored here
  // Only exists momentarily during signing
}

class SecureSigner {
  private envelopeEncryption: EnvelopeEncryptionService;

  constructor(envelopeEncryption: EnvelopeEncryptionService) {
    this.envelopeEncryption = envelopeEncryption;
  }

  // Sign a transaction with ephemeral key that exists only for this operation
  async signTransaction(
    encryptedPrivateKey: EncryptedData,
    transaction: Transaction | VersionedTransaction
  ): Promise<{ signature: string; publicKey: string }> {
    // 1. Decrypt private key (DEK exists only in this scope)
    const privateKeyBytes = await this.envelopeEncryption.decrypt(encryptedPrivateKey);

    try {
      // 2. Create ephemeral keypair
      const keypair = Keypair.fromSecretKey(privateKeyBytes);

      // 3. Sign transaction
      if (transaction instanceof VersionedTransaction) {
        transaction.sign([keypair]);
      } else {
        transaction.partialSign(keypair);
      }

      // 4. Return signature
      const signature = transaction.signature?.toString("base64") || "";

      return {
        signature,
        publicKey: keypair.publicKey.toBase58(),
      };
    } finally {
      // 5. CRITICAL: Zero out private key from memory
      privateKeyBytes.fill(0);

      // 6. Zero out keypair (best effort — V8 may not immediately GC)
      // Force garbage collection hint (Node.js --expose-gc flag required)
      if (global.gc) {
        global.gc();
      }
    }
  }

  // Generate new wallet with encrypted private key
  async generateWallet(): Promise<{ publicKey: string; encryptedPrivateKey: EncryptedData }> {
    const keypair = Keypair.generate();
    const privateKey = keypair.secretKey;

    try {
      const encryptedPrivateKey = await this.envelopeEncryption.encrypt(
        Buffer.from(privateKey)
      );

      return {
        publicKey: keypair.publicKey.toBase58(),
        encryptedPrivateKey,
      };
    } finally {
      privateKey.fill(0);
    }
  }
}
```



### Key Rotation Strategy

```typescript
// src/services/security/key-rotation.ts
interface KeyRotationConfig {
  autoRotateIntervalDays: number;  // 90 days
  emergencyRotationTrigger: string; // Secret webhook to force rotation
}

class KeyRotationService {
  async scheduleRotation(): Promise<void> {
    // 1. Generate new KEK version
    const newVersion = await envelopeEncryption.rotateKEK();

    // 2. Queue background job to re-encrypt all wallet keys
    await jobManager.send("security:key-rotation", {
      fromVersion: "current",
      toVersion: newVersion,
      batchSize: 100, // Process 100 wallets at a time
    });
  }

  async emergencyRotation(): Promise<void> {
    // Called when compromise is suspected
    // 1. Immediately disable all trading
    await db.update(tradingSessions)
      .set({ status: "revoked", revokedReason: "EMERGENCY_KEY_ROTATION" });

    // 2. Rotate KEK
    await this.scheduleRotation();

    // 3. Notify all users
    await notifyAllUsers({
      type: "system",
      title: "Security Alert",
      body: "We have rotated encryption keys as a precautionary measure. Please review your account.",
    });

    // 4. Log for audit
    await auditLog("EMERGENCY_KEY_ROTATION", { triggeredAt: new Date() });
  }
}
```

### Telegram Bot Auth Security

Telegram bot messages are NOT end-to-end encrypted. Telegram servers can read them. For a trading bot handling wallet commands, this is a critical risk.

```typescript
// src/bot/security.ts
import { createHash, timingSafeEqual } from "crypto";

// Verify Telegram webhook signature
export function verifyTelegramWebhook(
  botToken: string,
  rawBody: Buffer,
  signature: string
): boolean {
  const secret = createHash("sha256").update(botToken).digest();
  const expected = createHash("sha256")
    .update(secret)
    .update(rawBody)
    .digest("hex");

  // Timing-safe comparison to prevent timing attacks
  return timingSafeEqual(
    Buffer.from(signature, "hex"),
    Buffer.from(expected, "hex")
  );
}

// Encrypt sensitive bot messages before processing
// Since Telegram doesn't support E2EE for bots, we encrypt sensitive data
// in the bot messages themselves
export function encryptBotMessage(plaintext: string, key: Buffer): string {
  const iv = randomBytes(16);
  const cipher = createCipheriv("aes-256-gcm", key, iv);
  const encrypted = Buffer.concat([cipher.update(plaintext, "utf8"), cipher.final()]);
  const tag = cipher.getAuthTag();
  return `${iv.toString("base64")}:${tag.toString("base64")}:${encrypted.toString("base64")}`;
}

export function decryptBotMessage(ciphertext: string, key: Buffer): string {
  const [ivB64, tagB64, dataB64] = ciphertext.split(":");
  const iv = Buffer.from(ivB64, "base64");
  const tag = Buffer.from(tagB64, "base64");
  const data = Buffer.from(dataB64, "base64");

  const decipher = createDecipheriv("aes-256-gcm", key, iv);
  decipher.setAuthTag(tag);
  return decipher.update(data).toString("utf8") + decipher.final("utf8");
}
```



### Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)

```typescript
// src/lib/rbac.ts
enum Role {
  USER = "user",           // Standard trading user
  ADMIN = "admin",         // Can view all users, manage system
  SUPPORT = "support",     // Can view user data, cannot trade
  SYSTEM = "system",       // Internal services only
}

enum Permission {
  TRADE_CREATE = "trade:create",
  TRADE_EXECUTE = "trade:execute",
  SESSION_REVOKE = "session:revoke",
  WALLET_VIEW = "wallet:view",
  WALLET_CREATE = "wallet:create",
  USER_VIEW = "user:view",
  USER_MANAGE = "user:manage",
  SYSTEM_CONFIG = "system:config",
  AUDIT_READ = "audit:read",
}

const ROLE_PERMISSIONS: Record<Role, Permission[]> = {
  [Role.USER]: [
    Permission.TRADE_CREATE,
    Permission.TRADE_EXECUTE,
    Permission.SESSION_REVOKE,
    Permission.WALLET_VIEW,
    Permission.WALLET_CREATE,
  ],
  [Role.SUPPORT]: [
    Permission.USER_VIEW,
    Permission.AUDIT_READ,
  ],
  [Role.ADMIN]: [
    ...ROLE_PERMISSIONS[Role.USER],
    ...ROLE_PERMISSIONS[Role.SUPPORT],
    Permission.USER_MANAGE,
    Permission.SYSTEM_CONFIG,
  ],
  [Role.SYSTEM]: [
    Permission.TRADE_EXECUTE,
    Permission.AUDIT_READ,
  ],
};

export function hasPermission(role: Role, permission: Permission): boolean {
  return ROLE_PERMISSIONS[role]?.includes(permission) || false;
}

// Middleware for API routes
export function requirePermission(permission: Permission) {
  return async (req: Request, context: any) => {
    const session = await auth.api.getSession({ headers: req.headers });
    if (!session) {
      return new Response("Unauthorized", { status: 401 });
    }

    const userRole = (session.user as any).role || Role.USER;
    if (!hasPermission(userRole, permission)) {
      // Log unauthorized access attempt
      await auditLog("UNAUTHORIZED_ACCESS_ATTEMPT", {
        userId: session.user.id,
        permission,
        path: req.url,
        timestamp: new Date(),
      });
      return new Response("Forbidden", { status: 403 });
    }

    return context.next();
  };
}
```

## LAYER 3: INFRASTRUCTURE SECURITY



### Oracle Cloud ARM Hardening

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# scripts/harden-oracle-cloud.sh

# 1. Update system
apt update && apt upgrade -y

# 2. Install and configure fail2ban
apt install -y fail2ban
systemctl enable fail2ban

cat > /etc/fail2ban/jail.local << 'EOF'
[DEFAULT]
bantime = 3600
findtime = 600
maxretry = 3
backend = systemd

[sshd]
enabled = true
port = ssh
filter = sshd
logpath = /var/log/auth.log
maxretry = 3

[nginx-http-auth]
enabled = true
filter = nginx-http-auth
port = http,https
logpath = /var/log/nginx/error.log

[osiris-api]
enabled = true
filter = osiris-api
port = http,https
logpath = /opt/osiris/logs/error.log
maxretry = 10
findtime = 60
EOF

# 3. Configure UFW firewall
ufw default deny incoming
ufw default allow outgoing
ufw allow 22/tcp      # SSH (change to custom port in production)
ufw allow 80/tcp      # HTTP
ufw allow 443/tcp     # HTTPS
ufw allow 5432/tcp    # PostgreSQL (only from localhost)
ufw allow 6379/tcp    # Redis (only from localhost)
ufw --force enable

# 4. SSH hardening
cat >> /etc/ssh/sshd_config << 'EOF'
PermitRootLogin no
PasswordAuthentication no
PubkeyAuthentication yes
MaxAuthTries 3
ClientAliveInterval 300
ClientAliveCountMax 2
AllowUsers ubuntu
EOF
systemctl restart sshd

# 5. Install and configure AIDE (file integrity monitoring)
apt install -y aide
aideinit
mv /var/lib/aide/aide.db.new /var/lib/aide/aide.db

# 6. Kernel hardening
cat >> /etc/sysctl.conf << 'EOF'
# Disable IP source routing
net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_source_route = 0
net.ipv6.conf.all.accept_source_route = 0

# Disable ICMP redirects
net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_redirects = 0
net.ipv6.conf.all.accept_redirects = 0

# Enable SYN flood protection
net.ipv4.tcp_syncookies = 1

# Disable IPv6 if not needed
net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6 = 1
EOF
sysctl -p

# 7. Memory protection
cat >> /etc/sysctl.conf << 'EOF'
# Enable ASLR
kernel.randomize_va_space = 2

# Restrict ptrace
kernel.yama.ptrace_scope = 1
EOF
sysctl -p

# 8. Secure shared memory
echo "tmpfs /run/shm tmpfs defaults,noexec,nosuid,nodev 0 0" >> /etc/fstab

# 9. Install auditd for system call auditing
apt install -y auditd
systemctl enable auditd

# 10. Docker security
cat > /etc/docker/daemon.json << 'EOF'
{
  "userns-remap": "default",
  "live-restore": true,
  "no-new-privileges": true,
  "seccomp-profile": "/etc/docker/seccomp-default.json",
  "log-driver": "json-file",
  "log-opts": {
    "max-size": "10m",
    "max-file": "3"
  }
}
EOF
systemctl restart docker
```

## LAYER 4: APPLICATION SECURITY



### Input Validation & Sanitization

```typescript
// src/lib/validation.ts
import { z } from "zod";

// Strict validation for all user inputs
export const SolanaAddressSchema = z
  .string()
  .regex(/^[1-9A-HJ-NP-Za-km-z]{32,44}$/, "Invalid Solana address")
  .transform((val) => val.trim());

export const TokenMintSchema = z
  .string()
  .regex(/^[1-9A-HJ-NP-Za-km-z]{32,44}$/, "Invalid token mint")
  .refine(async (mint) => {
    // Check if mint exists on-chain
    const account = await connection.getAccountInfo(new PublicKey(mint));
    return account !== null;
  }, "Token mint does not exist");

export const TradeAmountSchema = z
  .string()
  .regex(/^\d+$/, "Amount must be a positive integer")
  .refine((val) => {
    const num = BigInt(val);
    return num > 0n && num < 2n ** 64n;
  }, "Amount out of range");

export const SlippageSchema = z
  .number()
  .int()
  .min(10, "Minimum 0.1% slippage")
  .max(1000, "Maximum 10% slippage");

// Sanitize all string inputs to prevent injection
export function sanitizeInput(input: string): string {
  return input
    .replace(/[<>]/g, "")        // Remove HTML tags
    .replace(/['";]/g, "")       // Remove SQL injection chars
    .replace(/[␀-]/g, "") // Remove control characters
    .trim()
    .slice(0, 1000);             // Max length
}
```



### SQL Injection Prevention (Drizzle ORM)

Drizzle ORM uses parameterized queries by default, which prevents SQL injection. But raw queries must be carefully constructed:

```typescript
// SAFE: Drizzle handles parameterization
await db.select().from(users).where(eq(users.id, userId));

// UNSAFE: Never do this
await db.execute(`SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = '${userId}'`);

// SAFE: Even raw queries use parameters
await db.execute(sql`SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ${userId}`);
```



### CSRF Protection

```typescript
// src/middleware/csrf.ts
import { NextResponse } from "next/server";

const CSRF_TOKEN_HEADER = "X-CSRF-Token";
const CSRF_COOKIE = "csrf_token";

export function csrfProtection(req: Request) {
  // Skip for GET, HEAD, OPTIONS (safe methods)
  if (["GET", "HEAD", "OPTIONS"].includes(req.method)) {
    return null; // Continue
  }

  const token = req.headers.get(CSRF_TOKEN_HEADER);
  const cookie = req.cookies.get(CSRF_COOKIE);

  if (!token || !cookie || token !== cookie.value) {
    return new NextResponse("CSRF token mismatch", { status: 403 });
  }

  return null; // Continue
}
```



### Secure Session Management

```typescript
// src/lib/session.ts
import { sealData, unsealData } from "iron-session";

const SESSION_SECRET = process.env.SESSION_SECRET!; // 32+ byte random
const SESSION_TTL = 60 * 60 * 24 * 7; // 7 days

export async function createSecureSession(userId: string): Promise<string> {
  const token = await sealData(
    { userId, createdAt: Date.now() },
    {
      password: SESSION_SECRET,
      ttl: SESSION_TTL,
    }
  );
  return token;
}

export async function verifySecureSession(token: string): Promise<{ userId: string } | null> {
  try {
    const data = await unsealData(token, {
      password: SESSION_SECRET,
      ttl: SESSION_TTL,
    });
    return data as { userId: string };
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}
```

## LAYER 5: MONITORING & DETECTION



### Security Event Logging

```typescript
// src/lib/security-logger.ts
interface SecurityEvent {
  eventType: string;
  severity: "low" | "medium" | "high" | "critical";
  userId?: string;
  ipAddress: string;
  userAgent?: string;
  details: Record<string, any>;
  timestamp: Date;
}

class SecurityLogger {
  async log(event: SecurityEvent): Promise<void> {
    // 1. Write to database (append-only audit log)
    await db.insert(auditLogs).values({
      eventType: event.eventType,
      severity: event.severity,
      userId: event.userId,
      ipAddress: event.ipAddress,
      userAgent: event.userAgent,
      details: event.details,
      timestamp: event.timestamp,
    });

    // 2. Alert on critical events
    if (event.severity === "critical") {
      await this.sendCriticalAlert(event);
    }

    // 3. Send to SIEM if configured
    if (process.env.SIEM_WEBHOOK_URL) {
      await fetch(process.env.SIEM_WEBHOOK_URL, {
        method: "POST",
        headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
        body: JSON.stringify(event),
      });
    }
  }

  private async sendCriticalAlert(event: SecurityEvent): Promise<void> {
    // Send to admin Telegram, PagerDuty, etc.
    await telegramBot.api.sendMessage(
      process.env.ADMIN_CHAT_ID!,
      `🚨 CRITICAL SECURITY EVENT

` +
        `Type: ${event.eventType}
` +
        `User: ${event.userId || "N/A"}
` +
        `IP: ${event.ipAddress}
` +
        `Time: ${event.timestamp.toISOString()}
` +
        `Details: ${JSON.stringify(event.details)}`
    );
  }
}

export const securityLogger = new SecurityLogger();

// Events to log
const CRITICAL_EVENTS = [
  "UNAUTHORIZED_ACCESS_ATTEMPT",
  "KEY_DECRYPTION_FAILURE",
  "MASS_WALLET_EXPORT_ATTEMPT",
  "SUSPICIOUS_TRADE_PATTERN",
  "RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED",
  "SESSION_HIJACKING_DETECTED",
  "DATABASE_CONNECTION_FROM_UNKNOWN_IP",
  "PRIVILEGE_ESCALATION_ATTEMPT",
];
```

### Anomaly Detection

```typescript
// src/lib/anomaly-detection.ts
interface TradeAnomaly {
  userId: string;
  anomalyType: string;
  confidence: number; // 0-1
  details: Record<string, any>;
}

class AnomalyDetector {
  async detectTradeAnomalies(userId: string, trade: Trade): Promise<TradeAnomaly[]> {
    const anomalies: TradeAnomaly[] = [];

    // 1. Unusual trade size (3x average)
    const avgTradeSize = await this.getAverageTradeSize(userId, 30);
    if (avgTradeSize > 0 && Number(trade.inputAmount) > avgTradeSize * 3) {
      anomalies.push({
        userId,
        anomalyType: "UNUSUAL_TRADE_SIZE",
        confidence: 0.8,
        details: { amount: trade.inputAmount, average: avgTradeSize },
      });
    }

    // 2. Rapid trading (10+ trades in 1 minute)
    const recentTrades = await this.getRecentTradeCount(userId, 60);
    if (recentTrades > 10) {
      anomalies.push({
        userId,
        anomalyType: "RAPID_TRADING",
        confidence: 0.7,
        details: { count: recentTrades, window: "1m" },
      });
    }

    // 3. Trading outside normal hours (3am for user timezone)
    const userTimezone = await this.getUserTimezone(userId);
    const localHour = new Date().toLocaleString("en-US", {
      timeZone: userTimezone,
      hour: "numeric",
      hour12: false,
    });
    if (parseInt(localHour) >= 2 && parseInt(localHour) <= 5) {
      anomalies.push({
        userId,
        anomalyType: "OFF_HOURS_TRADING",
        confidence: 0.5,
        details: { localHour },
      });
    }

    // 4. New destination token (never traded before)
    const hasTradedBefore = await this.hasTradedToken(userId, trade.outputMint);
    if (!hasTradedBefore) {
      anomalies.push({
        userId,
        anomalyType: "NEW_TOKEN_TRADE",
        confidence: 0.4,
        details: { token: trade.outputMint },
      });
    }

    // Log anomalies
    for (const anomaly of anomalies) {
      await securityLogger.log({
        eventType: anomaly.anomalyType,
        severity: anomaly.confidence > 0.7 ? "high" : "medium",
        userId: anomaly.userId,
        ipAddress: "",
        details: anomaly.details,
        timestamp: new Date(),
      });
    }

    return anomalies;
  }

  private async getAverageTradeSize(userId: string, days: number): Promise<number> {
    const trades = await db.query.trades.findMany({
      where: and(
        eq(trades.userId, userId),
        gte(trades.createdAt, subDays(new Date(), days))
      ),
    });
    if (trades.length === 0) return 0;
    return trades.reduce((sum, t) => sum + Number(t.inputAmount), 0) / trades.length;
  }

  private async getRecentTradeCount(userId: string, seconds: number): Promise<number> {
    const result = await db
      .select({ count: sql<number>`count(*)` })
      .from(trades)
      .where(
        and(
          eq(trades.userId, userId),
          gte(trades.createdAt, subSeconds(new Date(), seconds))
        )
      );
    return result[0]?.count || 0;
  }
}
```
