## LAYER 6: INCIDENT RESPONSE



### Automated Response Playbook

```typescript
// src/lib/incident-response.ts
interface SecurityIncident {
  id: string;
  type: string;
  severity: "low" | "medium" | "high" | "critical";
  affectedUserIds: string[];
  description: string;
  detectedAt: Date;
}

class IncidentResponse {
  async handleIncident(incident: SecurityIncident): Promise<void> {
    // 1. Log incident
    await this.createIncidentRecord(incident);

    // 2. Immediate containment based on severity
    switch (incident.severity) {
      case "critical":
        await this.criticalResponse(incident);
        break;
      case "high":
        await this.highResponse(incident);
        break;
      case "medium":
        await this.mediumResponse(incident);
        break;
      default:
        await this.lowResponse(incident);
    }

    // 3. Notify response team
    await this.notifyResponseTeam(incident);

    // 4. Update status
    await this.updateIncidentStatus(incident.id, "contained");
  }

  private async criticalResponse(incident: SecurityIncident): Promise<void> {
    // 1. Revoke all active sessions for affected users
    for (const userId of incident.affectedUserIds) {
      await db
        .update(tradingSessions)
        .set({
          status: "revoked",
          revokedAt: new Date(),
          revokedReason: `SECURITY_INCIDENT: ${incident.id}`,
        })
        .where(eq(tradingSessions.userId, userId));

      // Invalidate cache
      await cache.invalidatePattern(`session:*:${userId}`);
    }

    // 2. Disable trading for affected users
    await db
      .update(users)
      .set({ tier: "free" }) // Downgrade to free (no trading)
      .where(inArray(users.id, incident.affectedUserIds));

    // 3. Force password reset
    await db
      .update(accounts)
      .set({ password: null })
      .where(inArray(accounts.userId, incident.affectedUserIds));

    // 4. Rotate KEK if keys may be compromised
    if (incident.type.includes("KEY") || incident.type.includes("BREACH")) {
      await keyRotationService.emergencyRotation();
    }

    // 5. Alert admin immediately
    await telegramBot.api.sendMessage(
      process.env.ADMIN_CHAT_ID!,
      `🚨 CRITICAL INCIDENT ${incident.id}

` +
        `Type: ${incident.type}
` +
        `Users affected: ${incident.affectedUserIds.length}
` +
        `All sessions revoked. Trading disabled. KEK rotated.`
    );
  }

  private async highResponse(incident: SecurityIncident): Promise<void> {
    // Revoke suspicious sessions only
    for (const userId of incident.affectedUserIds) {
      const suspiciousSessions = await db.query.tradingSessions.findMany({
        where: and(
          eq(tradingSessions.userId, userId),
          eq(tradingSessions.status, "active")
        ),
      });

      for (const session of suspiciousSessions) {
        // Check if session matches anomaly pattern
        if (await this.isSessionSuspicious(session)) {
          await revokeSession(session.id, `SECURITY_INCIDENT: ${incident.id}`);
        }
      }
    }
  }

  private async isSessionSuspicious(session: TradingSession): Promise<boolean> {
    // Check for unusual patterns
    const trades = await db.query.trades.findMany({
      where: eq(trades.sessionId, session.id),
      orderBy: desc(trades.createdAt),
      limit: 10,
    });

    // If all trades are losses, session might be compromised
    const allLosses = trades.every((t) => {
      // Check if trade was unprofitable
      return t.executedPrice && t.quotedPrice &&
        Number(t.executedPrice) < Number(t.quotedPrice) * 0.95;
    });

    return allLosses && trades.length > 5;
  }
}
```

## LAYER 7: COMPLIANCE & AUDIT



### Immutable Audit Log

```typescript
// src/db/schema.ts (audit log table)
export const auditLogs = pgTable(
  "audit_logs",
  {
    id: serial("id").primaryKey(),
    eventType: text("event_type").notNull(),
    severity: text("severity").notNull(),
    userId: text("user_id"),
    sessionId: text("session_id"),
    ipAddress: text("ip_address"),
    userAgent: text("user_agent"),
    details: jsonb("details"),
    hash: text("hash").notNull(), // Blockchain-style chaining
    previousHash: text("previous_hash"),
    createdAt: timestamp("created_at", { withTimezone: true }).defaultNow().notNull(),
  },
  (table) => [
    index("audit_logs_event_type_idx").on(table.eventType),
    index("audit_logs_user_id_idx").on(table.userId),
    index("audit_logs_created_at_idx").on(table.createdAt),
    index("audit_logs_severity_idx").on(table.severity),
  ]
);

// Hash chaining for tamper evidence
async function appendAuditLog(
  event: Omit<AuditLog, "id" | "hash" | "previousHash" | "createdAt">
): Promise<void> {
  // Get previous log's hash
  const lastLog = await db.query.auditLogs.findFirst({
    orderBy: desc(auditLogs.id),
  });

  const previousHash = lastLog?.hash || "0";

  // Create hash of current event + previous hash
  const data = JSON.stringify({ ...event, previousHash });
  const hash = createHash("sha256").update(data).digest("hex");

  await db.insert(auditLogs).values({
    ...event,
    previousHash,
    hash,
  });
}
```



### Data Retention Policy

```typescript
// src/services/compliance/data-retention.ts
interface RetentionPolicy {
  table: string;
  retentionDays: number;
  anonymizeAfterDays?: number;
}

const RETENTION_POLICIES: RetentionPolicy[] = [
  { table: "trades", retentionDays: 2555 },           // 7 years (tax)
  { table: "audit_logs", retentionDays: 2555 },         // 7 years (compliance)
  { table: "notifications", retentionDays: 90 },        // 3 months
  { table: "webhook_events", retentionDays: 30 },       // 1 month
  { table: "rate_limits", retentionDays: 7 },           // 1 week
  { table: "sessions", retentionDays: 365 },            // 1 year
];

async function enforceRetentionPolicies(): Promise<void> {
  for (const policy of RETENTION_POLICIES) {
    const cutoffDate = subDays(new Date(), policy.retentionDays);

    await db.execute(sql`
      DELETE FROM ${sql.identifier(policy.table)}
      WHERE created_at < ${cutoffDate}
    `);

    logger.info("Retention policy enforced", {
      table: policy.table,
      cutoffDate,
    });
  }
}
```

## SCENARIO 1: KEYLOGGER ON YOUR LAPTOP



### How They Get You
You download a cracked game, a "trading tool" from a Telegram group, or a malicious npm package. The keylogger records every keystroke. When you type your password, seed phrase, or private key — they have it. They wait. They watch your balance grow. Then they drain you.



### Defense: Multi-Layer Keylogger Resistance

```typescript
// src/lib/security/anti-keylogger.ts

/**
 * Virtual Keyboard Input — No physical keystrokes
 * Renders an on-screen keyboard. Mouse clicks only.
 * Keyloggers that hook keyboard interrupts see nothing.
 */
export class VirtualKeyboardInput {
  private inputBuffer: string[] = [];
  private maxLength: number;

  constructor(maxLength: number = 64) {
    this.maxLength = maxLength;
  }

  // User clicks virtual keys — no keyboard events
  clickKey(char: string): void {
    if (this.inputBuffer.length < this.maxLength) {
      this.inputBuffer.push(char);
    }
  }

  getValue(): string {
    return this.inputBuffer.join("");
  }

  // Clear from memory immediately
  destroy(): void {
    this.inputBuffer.fill("");
    this.inputBuffer = [];
  }
}

/**
 * Password Splitting — Never type full password
 * Split password into 3 parts entered via different methods
 */
export async function splitPasswordEntry(): Promise<string> {
  // Part 1: Virtual keyboard (mouse clicks)
  const part1 = await getVirtualKeyboardInput("Enter first 8 characters");

  // Part 2: Paste from password manager (clipboard, not keyboard)
  const part2 = await getClipboardInput("Paste from password manager");

  // Part 3: On-screen pattern (draw a pattern like Android unlock)
  const part3 = await getPatternInput("Draw your pattern");

  return part1 + part2 + part3;
}

/**
 * Time-Delayed Input — Keylogger can't correlate
 * Type one character, wait random 1-5 seconds, type next
 * Keylogger sees: "h" ... 3s ... "e" ... 1s ... "l" ... 4s ... "l" ... 2s ... "o"
 * Cannot reconstruct the word from timing alone
 */
export async function timeDelayedInput(
  prompt: string,
  minDelayMs: number = 1000,
  maxDelayMs: number = 5000
): Promise<string> {
  console.log(prompt);
  const chars: string[] = [];

  // In real implementation: capture one char at a time from hidden input
  // For each char, wait random delay before accepting next
  // This breaks keylogger's ability to reconstruct the string

  return chars.join("");
}

/**
 * Decoy Keystroke Generator
 * Runs in background, types random characters into a hidden textarea
 * Keylogger captures noise + real input = impossible to distinguish
 */
export class DecoyKeystrokeGenerator {
  private interval: NodeJS.Timeout | null = null;
  private decoyChars = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789!@#$%^&*()";

  start(): void {
    const hiddenInput = document.createElement("textarea");
    hiddenInput.style.position = "absolute";
    hiddenInput.style.opacity = "0";
    hiddenInput.style.pointerEvents = "none";
    document.body.appendChild(hiddenInput);

    this.interval = setInterval(() => {
      const char = this.decoyChars[Math.floor(Math.random() * this.decoyChars.length)];
      hiddenInput.value += char;
      // Simulate keyboard event
      hiddenInput.dispatchEvent(new KeyboardEvent("keydown", { key: char }));
      hiddenInput.dispatchEvent(new KeyboardEvent("keyup", { key: char }));
    }, 50); // 20 fake keystrokes per second
  }

  stop(): void {
    if (this.interval) clearInterval(this.interval);
  }
}
```



### Defense: Hardware Security Key (FIDO2/WebAuthn) — FREE with phone

```typescript
// src/lib/security/webauthn.ts
import { generateRegistrationOptions, verifyRegistrationResponse } from "@simplewebauthn/server";

/**
 * FIDO2/WebAuthn — Unphishable, unkeyloggable
 * Uses your phone's biometric (fingerprint/face) or hardware key
 * Private key NEVER leaves the secure element
 */
export async function registerSecurityKey(userId: string): Promise<void> {
  const options = await generateRegistrationOptions({
    rpName: "OSIRIS",
    rpID: "osiris.trade",
    userID: Buffer.from(userId),
    userName: userId,
    attestationType: "direct",
    authenticatorSelection: {
      residentKey: "required",
      userVerification: "required",
      authenticatorAttachment: "platform", // Use phone's secure element
    },
  });

  // Store challenge for verification
  await db.update(users)
    .set({ webauthnChallenge: options.challenge })
    .where(eq(users.id, userId));

  // Return options to client for registration
  return options;
}

export async function verifySecurityKey(
  userId: string,
  credential: any
): Promise<boolean> {
  const user = await db.query.users.findFirst({
    where: eq(users.id, userId),
  });

  if (!user?.webauthnChallenge) return false;

  const verification = await verifyRegistrationResponse({
    response: credential,
    expectedChallenge: user.webauthnChallenge,
    expectedOrigin: "https://osiris.trade",
    expectedRPID: "osiris.trade",
  });

  if (verification.verified) {
    // Store credential ID for future authentication
    await db.update(users)
      .set({
        webauthnCredentialId: verification.registrationInfo?.credentialID,
        webauthnPublicKey: verification.registrationInfo?.credentialPublicKey,
      })
      .where(eq(users.id, userId));
  }

  return verification.verified;
}
```



### Defense: Clipboard Monitor (Detect Suspicious Clipboard Access)

```typescript
// src/lib/security/clipboard-monitor.ts

/**
 * Monitor clipboard for suspicious patterns
 * Keyloggers often read clipboard to capture pasted passwords
 */
export class ClipboardMonitor {
  private suspiciousPatterns = [
    /[a-zA-Z0-9]{44,}/,           // Solana private key (88 chars base58)
    /[a-zA-Z0-9]{64}/,             // Hex private key
    /[a-z]+ [a-z]+ [a-z]+ [a-z]+ [a-z]+ [a-z]+ [a-z]+ [a-z]+ [a-z]+ [a-z]+ [a-z]+ [a-z]+/, // Seed phrase
  ];

  startMonitoring(): void {
    // On web: monitor paste events
    document.addEventListener("paste", (e) => {
      const pasted = e.clipboardData?.getData("text") || "";
      this.checkClipboard(pasted);
    });
  }

  private checkClipboard(content: string): void {
    for (const pattern of this.suspiciousPatterns) {
      if (pattern.test(content)) {
        // ALERT: Clipboard contains what looks like a private key
        securityLogger.log({
          eventType: "SUSPICIOUS_CLIPBOARD_CONTENT",
          severity: "critical",
          details: {
            pattern: pattern.toString(),
            contentLength: content.length,
            // NEVER log the actual content
          },
          timestamp: new Date(),
          ipAddress: "",
        });

        // Clear clipboard immediately
        navigator.clipboard.writeText("");

        // Warn user
        alert("⚠️ SECURITY ALERT: Your clipboard contains sensitive data. It has been cleared.");
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## SCENARIO 2: SCREEN RECORDER / REMOTE ACCESS TROJAN (RAT)



### How They Get You
You install a "free VPN", a "system optimizer", or a cracked Adobe product. The RAT gives the attacker live screen access. They watch you log in. They see your balance. They wait for you to enter your 2FA code. The moment you do, they take over your session and drain everything.



### Defense: Screen Obfuscation + Session Binding

```typescript
// src/lib/security/anti-screen-recording.ts

/**
 * Dynamic UI Obfuscation
 * Changes element positions, colors, and labels randomly on each render
 * Screen recording shows different layout than what user sees
 */
export class UIObfuscation {
  private seed: number;

  constructor() {
    // Seed derived from session + timestamp
    this.seed = Date.now() + Math.random() * 1000000;
  }

  // Obfuscate sensitive values (balance, wallet address)
  obfuscateValue(value: string): string {
    // Display: "1.8M SOL" but actual DOM contains scrambled characters
    // Screen recorder sees scrambled text, user sees clear via CSS
    const scrambled = value.split("").map((char, i) => {
      // CSS transforms this back to correct character for user
      // But screen recorder captures raw DOM = gibberish
      return String.fromCharCode(char.charCodeAt(0) + (this.seed % 10));
    }).join("");
    return scrambled;
  }

  // Randomize button positions
  randomizeLayout(): void {
    const buttons = document.querySelectorAll("[data-sensitive]");
    buttons.forEach((btn) => {
      const el = btn as HTMLElement;
      // Actual clickable area is offset from visual position
      // Screen recorder sees button at X,Y but click must be at X+50, Y+30
      el.style.setProperty("--click-offset-x", `${Math.random() * 100}px`);
      el.style.setProperty("--click-offset-y", `${Math.random() * 50}px`);
    });
  }
}

/**
 * Session Fingerprinting — Bind session to device characteristics
 * If RAT takes over, device fingerprint changes = instant lockout
 */
export async function createSessionFingerprint(): Promise<string> {
  const fingerprint = {
    // Canvas fingerprint (GPU rendering unique per device)
    canvas: await getCanvasFingerprint(),
    // WebGL fingerprint
    webgl: getWebGLFingerprint(),
    // Font list
    fonts: getFontList(),
    // Screen properties
    screen: {
      width: screen.width,
      height: screen.height,
      colorDepth: screen.colorDepth,
      pixelRatio: window.devicePixelRatio,
    },
    // Timezone
    timezone: Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone,
    // Language
    language: navigator.language,
    // Touch support
    touch: "ontouchstart" in window,
    // Hardware concurrency
    cores: navigator.hardwareConcurrency,
  };

  return createHash("sha256")
    .update(JSON.stringify(fingerprint))
    .digest("hex");
}

export async function verifySessionFingerprint(
  sessionId: string,
  currentFingerprint: string
): Promise<boolean> {
  const session = await db.query.sessions.findFirst({
    where: eq(sessions.id, sessionId),
  });

  if (!session?.fingerprint) return true; // First login

  // Allow small variations (browser update, plugin change)
  // But reject major changes (new device, RAT takeover)
  const similarity = calculateFingerprintSimilarity(
    session.fingerprint,
    currentFingerprint
  );

  if (similarity < 0.8) {
    // Fingerprint changed significantly — possible RAT or device switch
    await securityLogger.log({
      eventType: "SESSION_FINGERPRINT_MISMATCH",
      severity: "high",
      userId: session.userId,
      details: { similarity, expected: session.fingerprint, got: currentFingerprint },
      timestamp: new Date(),
      ipAddress: "",
    });

    // Revoke session immediately
    await revokeSession(sessionId, "FINGERPRINT_MISMATCH");
    return false;
  }

  return true;
}
```



### Defense: Behavioral Biometrics (How You Type/Move Mouse)

```typescript
// src/lib/security/behavioral-biometrics.ts

/**
 * Behavioral Biometrics — How you interact, not what you know
 * RAT attacker types differently than you: speed, rhythm, mouse paths
 * Free implementation using JavaScript timing APIs
 */
export class BehavioralBiometrics {
  private keystrokeTimings: number[] = [];
  private mousePaths: Array<{ x: number; y: number; t: number }> = [];
  private baseline: any = null;

  startCollection(): void {
    // Collect keystroke dynamics
    document.addEventListener("keydown", (e) => {
      this.keystrokeTimings.push(performance.now());
    });

    // Collect mouse movement patterns
    document.addEventListener("mousemove", (e) => {
      this.mousePaths.push({ x: e.clientX, y: e.clientY, t: performance.now() });
      // Keep only last 1000 points
      if (this.mousePaths.length > 1000) this.mousePaths.shift();
    });
  }

  // Create baseline during enrollment (first few logins)
  async createBaseline(): Promise<void> {
    this.baseline = {
      avgTypingSpeed: this.calculateTypingSpeed(),
      typingRhythm: this.calculateTypingRhythm(),
      mouseJitter: this.calculateMouseJitter(),
      mouseStraightness: this.calculateMouseStraightness(),
    };

    // Store encrypted baseline
    await db.update(users)
      .set({ behavioralBaseline: this.baseline })
      .where(eq(users.id, currentUserId));
  }

  // Verify current behavior matches baseline
  async verifyBehavior(): Promise<{ match: boolean; confidence: number }> {
    const current = {
      avgTypingSpeed: this.calculateTypingSpeed(),
      typingRhythm: this.calculateTypingRhythm(),
      mouseJitter: this.calculateMouseJitter(),
      mouseStraightness: this.calculateMouseStraightness(),
    };

    // RAT operators type faster and more consistently (no human variation)
    // Their mouse movements are more direct (they see the screen, not feel it)
    const speedDiff = Math.abs(current.avgTypingSpeed - this.baseline.avgTypingSpeed) / this.baseline.avgTypingSpeed;
    const jitterDiff = Math.abs(current.mouseJitter - this.baseline.mouseJitter) / this.baseline.mouseJitter;

    const confidence = 1 - (speedDiff + jitterDiff) / 2;

    return {
      match: confidence > 0.7,
      confidence,
    };
  }

  private calculateTypingSpeed(): number {
    if (this.keystrokeTimings.length < 2) return 0;
    const totalTime = this.keystrokeTimings[this.keystrokeTimings.length - 1] - this.keystrokeTimings[0];
    return this.keystrokeTimings.length / (totalTime / 1000); // chars per second
  }

  private calculateTypingRhythm(): number[] {
    // Calculate intervals between keystrokes
    const intervals: number[] = [];
    for (let i = 1; i < this.keystrokeTimings.length; i++) {
      intervals.push(this.keystrokeTimings[i] - this.keystrokeTimings[i - 1]);
    }
    return intervals;
  }

  private calculateMouseJitter(): number {
    // Human hand has micro-tremors. RAT mouse is pixel-perfect.
    let totalJitter = 0;
    for (let i = 1; i < this.mousePaths.length; i++) {
      const dx = this.mousePaths[i].x - this.mousePaths[i - 1].x;
      const dy = this.mousePaths[i].y - this.mousePaths[i - 1].y;
      totalJitter += Math.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy);
    }
    return totalJitter / this.mousePaths.length;
  }

  private calculateMouseStraightness(): number {
    // Humans curve slightly. RAT goes straight to target.
    // Calculate deviation from straight line between start and end
    if (this.mousePaths.length < 3) return 1;
    const start = this.mousePaths[0];
    const end = this.mousePaths[this.mousePaths.length - 1];
    const straightLine = Math.sqrt(
      Math.pow(end.x - start.x, 2) + Math.pow(end.y - start.y, 2)
    );

    let actualPath = 0;
    for (let i = 1; i < this.mousePaths.length; i++) {
      const dx = this.mousePaths[i].x - this.mousePaths[i - 1].x;
      const dy = this.mousePaths[i].y - this.mousePaths[i - 1].y;
      actualPath += Math.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy);
    }

    return straightLine / actualPath; // 1.0 = perfectly straight (suspicious)
  }
}
```

## SCENARIO 3: SIM SWAP ATTACK



### How They Get You
You use SMS 2FA. Attacker calls your phone company, pretends to be you, says they lost their phone. Your number is ported to their SIM. They reset your password via SMS. They drain you.



### Defense: NO SMS 2FA. Ever.

```typescript
// src/lib/auth/mfa.ts

/**
 * MFA Policy — SMS is banned
 */
export const MFA_POLICY = {
  allowedMethods: ["totp", "webauthn", "email"] as const,
  bannedMethods: ["sms", "voice"] as const,

  // TOTP (Google Authenticator, Authy) — Free
  totp: {
    issuer: "OSIRIS",
    algorithm: "SHA256",
    digits: 8,        // More digits = harder to brute force
    period: 30,       // 30-second window
    window: 2,        // Allow 2 windows (±60s) for clock skew
  },

  // WebAuthn/FIDO2 — Free with phone
  webauthn: {

    expiryMinutes: 15,
    maxAttempts: 3,
  },

/**
 * SIM Swap Detection
 * Monitor for phone number changes, carrier changes, device changes
 */
export async function detectSimSwap(userId: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const user = await db.query.users.findFirst({
    where: eq(users.id, userId),
  });

  if (!user?.phoneNumber) return false;

  // Check if phone number was recently changed
  const recentChange = await db.query.userPhoneChanges.findFirst({
    where: and(
      eq(userPhoneChanges.userId, userId),
      gte(userPhoneChanges.changedAt, subDays(new Date(), 7))
    ),
  });

  if (recentChange) {
    // Phone changed in last 7 days — high SIM swap risk
    await securityLogger.log({
      eventType: "SIM_SWAP_RISK_DETECTED",
      severity: "critical",
      userId,
      details: {
        oldNumber: recentChange.oldNumber,
        newNumber: recentChange.newNumber,
        changedAt: recentChange.changedAt,
      },
      timestamp: new Date(),
      ipAddress: "",
    });

    // Lock account for 24 hours
    await db.update(users)
      .set({
        lockedUntil: new Date(Date.now() + 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000),
        lockReason: "SIM_SWAP_PROTECTION",
      })
      .where(eq(users.id, userId));

    return true;
  }

  return false;
}
```

```typescript
// src/lib/security/package-verification.ts

/**
 * Verify npm package integrity before installation
 * Check checksums, signatures, and known malicious packages
 */
export async function verifyPackage(packageName: string, version: string): Promise<{
  safe: boolean;
  warnings: string[];
}> {
  const warnings: string[] = [];

  // 1. Check against known malicious packages
  const maliciousPackages = [
    "lodash-utils", "node-fetch-utils", "express-middleware",
    "crypto-utils", "solana-web3-utils", "phantom-wallet-connect",
  ];
  if (maliciousPackages.includes(packageName)) {
    return { safe: false, warnings: ["KNOWN MALICIOUS PACKAGE"] };
  }

  // 2. Check for typosquatting (lodash vs. 1odash)
  const popularPackages = ["lodash", "express", "react", "next", "@solana/web3.js"];
  for (const popular of popularPackages) {
    const distance = levenshteinDistance(packageName, popular);
    if (distance <= 2 && packageName !== popular) {
      warnings.push(`Possible typosquatting of ${popular}`);
    }
  }

  // 3. Check package age (new packages are riskier)
  const pkgInfo = await fetch(`https://registry.npmjs.org/${packageName}/${version}`).then(r => r.json());
  const publishDate = new Date(pkgInfo.time[version]);
  const ageDays = (Date.now() - publishDate.getTime()) / (1000 * 60 * 60 * 24);
  if (ageDays < 30) {
    warnings.push(`Package is only ${Math.floor(ageDays)} days old`);
  }

  // 4. Check download count (low downloads = suspicious)
  const downloads = await fetch(
    `https://api.npmjs.org/downloads/point/last-month/${packageName}`
  ).then(r => r.json());
  if (downloads.downloads < 100) {
    warnings.push(`Only ${downloads.downloads} downloads last month`);
  }

  return {
    safe: warnings.length === 0,
    warnings,
  };
}

function levenshteinDistance(a: string, b: string): number {
  const matrix = Array(b.length + 1).fill(null).map(() => Array(a.length + 1).fill(null));
  for (let i = 0; i <= a.length; i++) matrix[0][i] = i;
  for (let j = 0; j <= b.length; j++) matrix[j][0] = j;
  for (let j = 1; j <= b.length; j++) {
    for (let i = 1; i <= a.length; i++) {
      matrix[j][i] = a[i - 1] === b[j - 1]
        ? matrix[j - 1][i - 1]
        : Math.min(matrix[j - 1][i - 1] + 1, matrix[j][i - 1] + 1, matrix[j - 1][i] + 1);
    }
  }
  return matrix[b.length][a.length];
}
```

```typescript
// src/lib/security/insider-threat.ts

/**
 * Database Access Monitoring
 * Log every query that accesses sensitive tables
 */
export class DatabaseAccessMonitor {
  private sensitiveTables = [
    "wallets",
    "key_encryption_keys",
    "trading_sessions",
    "trades",
    "users",
  ];

  monitorQuery(query: string, params: any[]): void {
    for (const table of this.sensitiveTables) {
      if (query.toLowerCase().includes(table)) {
        securityLogger.log({
          eventType: "SENSITIVE_DB_ACCESS",
          severity: "medium",
          details: {
            table,
            query: query.substring(0, 200), // Truncate
            paramCount: params.length,
            stackTrace: new Error().stack?.substring(0, 500),
          },
          timestamp: new Date(),
          ipAddress: "",
        });
      }
    }
  }
}

/**
 * KEK Access Control — No single person has full access
 * Require 2-of-3 admin approval for KEK operations
 */
export class KEKAccessControl {
  private requiredApprovals = 2;
  private adminCount = 3;

  async requestKEKAccess(
    requesterId: string,
    reason: string
  ): Promise<{ approved: boolean; token?: string }> {
    // Create approval request
    const request = await db.insert(kekAccessRequests).values({
      requesterId,
      reason,
      status: "pending",
      createdAt: new Date(),
    }).returning();

    // Notify other admins
    const admins = await db.query.users.findMany({
      where: eq(users.role, "admin"),
    });

    for (const admin of admins) {
      if (admin.id !== requesterId) {
        await telegramBot.api.sendMessage(
          admin.telegramId!,
          `🔐 KEK ACCESS REQUEST

` +
            `From: ${requesterId}
` +
            `Reason: ${reason}
` +
            `Approve: /approve_${request[0].id}
` +
            `Reject: /reject_${request[0].id}`
        );
      }
    }

    return { approved: false };
  }

  async approveRequest(
    requestId: string,
    approverId: string
  ): Promise<boolean> {
    const request = await db.query.kekAccessRequests.findFirst({
      where: eq(kekAccessRequests.id, requestId),
    });

    if (!request || request.status !== "pending") return false;

    // Record approval
    await db.insert(kekAccessApprovals).values({
      requestId,
      approverId,
      approvedAt: new Date(),
    });

    // Check if threshold reached
    const approvalCount = await db
      .select({ count: sql<number>`count(*)` })
      .from(kekAccessApprovals)
      .where(eq(kekAccessApprovals.requestId, requestId));

    if (approvalCount[0].count >= this.requiredApprovals) {
      // Grant temporary access token (expires in 1 hour)
      const token = crypto.randomUUID();
      await db.update(kekAccessRequests)
        .set({ status: "approved", accessToken: token, expiresAt: new Date(Date.now() + 60 * 60 * 1000) })
        .where(eq(kekAccessRequests.id, requestId));

      return true;
    }

    return false;
  }
}
```

## SCENARIO 8: BRUTE FORCE / CREDENTIAL STUFFING



### How They Get You
You reuse your password from a breached site (LinkedIn 2012, etc.). Attacker has the breached database. They try your email + password on OSIRIS. It works. They drain you.



### Defense: Breached Password Detection + Rate Limiting

```typescript
// src/lib/security/credential-stuffing.ts

/**
 * Check password against known breached databases
 * Uses Have I Been Pwned API (free, k-anonymity)
 */
export async function isPasswordBreached(password: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const hash = createHash("sha1").update(password).digest("hex").toUpperCase();
  const prefix = hash.substring(0, 5);
  const suffix = hash.substring(5);

  // k-anonymity: send only first 5 chars of hash
  const response = await fetch(`https://api.pwnedpasswords.com/range/${prefix}`);
  const data = await response.text();

  // Check if our suffix is in the response
  const lines = data.split("
");
  for (const line of lines) {
    const [lineSuffix] = line.split(":");
    if (lineSuffix === suffix) {
      return true; // Password found in breach database
    }
  }

  return false;
}

/**
 * Progressive Delay — Exponential backoff on failed logins
 * 1st fail: 1s, 2nd: 2s, 3rd: 4s, 4th: 8s, 5th: 16s, 6th+: 1 hour
 */
export async function getLoginDelay(failedAttempts: number): Promise<number> {
  if (failedAttempts >= 6) return 60 * 60 * 1000; // 1 hour
  return Math.pow(2, failedAttempts - 1) * 1000;
}
```

## SCENARIO 9: COLD STORAGE / AIR-GAPPED WALLET FOR $1.8M



### The Reality
With $1.8M, you cannot keep everything in a hot wallet. Period. The spec mentions "non-custodial" but for the OWNER'S funds (not user funds), you need cold storage.



### Defense: Air-Gapped Signing for Owner's Treasury

```typescript
// src/lib/security/air-gapped-signing.ts

/**
 * Air-Gapped Transaction Signing
 * For the owner's $1.8M treasury, use completely offline signing
 * 
 * Workflow:
 * 1. Online machine creates unsigned transaction
 * 2. Export as QR code or file
 * 3. Transfer to offline machine (air-gapped)
 * 4. Offline machine signs with private key
 * 5. Export signed transaction as QR code or file
 * 6. Transfer back to online machine
 * 7. Broadcast signed transaction
 * 
 * The private key NEVER touches an internet-connected device.
 */

interface UnsignedTransaction {
  recentBlockhash: string;
  feePayer: string;
  instructions: Array<{
    programId: string;
    accounts: Array<{ pubkey: string; isSigner: boolean; isWritable: boolean }>;
    data: string; // base64
  }>;
}

interface SignedTransaction {
  signatures: string[]; // base64
  message: string;      // base64 serialized message
}

// ONLINE MACHINE — Creates transaction
export async function createTreasuryTransaction(
  connection: Connection,
  from: string,
  to: string,
  amountLamports: number
): Promise<UnsignedTransaction> {
  const transaction = new Transaction().add(
    SystemProgram.transfer({
      fromPubkey: new PublicKey(from),
      toPubkey: new PublicKey(to),
      lamports: amountLamports,
    })
  );

  const { blockhash } = await connection.getLatestBlockhash();
  transaction.recentBlockhash = blockhash;
  transaction.feePayer = new PublicKey(from);

  return {
    recentBlockhash: blockhash,
    feePayer: from,
    instructions: transaction.instructions.map((ix) => ({
      programId: ix.programId.toBase58(),
      accounts: ix.keys.map((k) => ({
        pubkey: k.pubkey.toBase58(),
        isSigner: k.isSigner,
        isWritable: k.isWritable,
      })),
      data: ix.data.toString("base64"),
    })),
  };
}

// OFFLINE MACHINE — Signs transaction (NEVER connected to internet)
export function signTreasuryTransactionOffline(
  unsignedTx: UnsignedTransaction,
  privateKey: Uint8Array
): SignedTransaction {
  // Reconstruct transaction
  const transaction = new Transaction();
  transaction.recentBlockhash = unsignedTx.recentBlockhash;
  transaction.feePayer = new PublicKey(unsignedTx.feePayer);

  for (const ix of unsignedTx.instructions) {
    transaction.add(
      new TransactionInstruction({
        programId: new PublicKey(ix.programId),
        keys: ix.accounts.map((a) => ({
          pubkey: new PublicKey(a.pubkey),
          isSigner: a.isSigner,
          isWritable: a.isWritable,
        })),
        data: Buffer.from(ix.data, "base64"),
      })
    );
  }

  // Sign with private key
  const keypair = Keypair.fromSecretKey(privateKey);
  transaction.sign(keypair);

  return {
    signatures: transaction.signatures.map((s) => s?.signature?.toString("base64") || ""),
    message: transaction.serializeMessage().toString("base64"),
  };
}

// ONLINE MACHINE — Broadcast signed transaction
export async function broadcastSignedTransaction(
  connection: Connection,
  signedTx: SignedTransaction
): Promise<string> {
  // Reconstruct and send
  const message = Message.from(Buffer.from(signedTx.message, "base64"));
  const transaction = new VersionedTransaction(message);

  // Add signatures
  for (let i = 0; i < signedTx.signatures.length; i++) {
    if (signedTx.signatures[i]) {
      transaction.addSignature(
        message.staticAccountKeys[i],
        Buffer.from(signedTx.signatures[i], "base64")
      );
    }
  }

  return connection.sendRawTransaction(transaction.serialize());
}
```



### Defense: Multisig Treasury with Squads (Free, Already Researched)

```typescript
// src/lib/security/multisig-treasury.ts

/**
 * Squads Multisig for Owner's $1.8M Treasury
 * Requires 2-of-3 or 3-of-5 signatures for any withdrawal
 * Even if one key is compromised, funds are safe
 * 
 * Squads v4 is formally verified, immutable since Nov 2024
 * Secures $15B+ across 450+ teams on Solana
 */

import { Squads } from "@sqds/sdk";

const SQUADS_PROGRAM_ID = new PublicKey("SQDS4ep65T869zKXZapS4jL6WZhf2nT6oYd2d3V8phX");

export async function createTreasuryMultisig(
  connection: Connection,
  ownerKeypair: Keypair,
  members: PublicKey[]
): Promise<string> {
  const squads = Squads.endpoint(
    connection.rpcEndpoint,
    ownerKeypair,
    { commitment: "confirmed" }
  );

  // Create 2-of-3 multisig
  const createKey = Keypair.generate();
  const [multisigPda] = PublicKey.findProgramAddressSync(
    [Buffer.from("multisig"), createKey.publicKey.toBuffer()],
    SQUADS_PROGRAM_ID
  );

  await squads.createMultisig(
    members.length,      // Total members
    2,                   // Threshold (2-of-3)
    createKey.publicKey,
    members,
    "OSIRIS Treasury"
  );

  return multisigPda.toBase58();
}

export async function proposeTreasuryWithdrawal(
  squads: Squads,
  multisigPda: PublicKey,
  destination: PublicKey,
  amountLamports: number
): Promise<string> {
  // Create transaction proposal
  const transaction = await squads.createTransaction(multisigPda, 1);

  // Add transfer instruction
  await squads.addInstruction(
    transaction.publicKey,
    SystemProgram.transfer({
      fromPubkey: multisigPda, // Vault PDA
      toPubkey: destination,
      lamports: amountLamports,
    })
  );

  // Activate for voting
  await squads.activateTransaction(transaction.publicKey);

  return transaction.publicKey.toBase58();
}

export async function approveTreasuryWithdrawal(
  squads: Squads,
  transactionPda: PublicKey,
  approverKeypair: Keypair
): Promise<void> {
  await squads.approveTransaction(transactionPda, approverKeypair);
}

export async function executeTreasuryWithdrawal(
  squads: Squads,
  transactionPda: PublicKey
): Promise<string> {
  // Only executes after threshold approvals reached
  return squads.executeTransaction(transactionPda);
}
```

## SCENARIO 10: SOCIAL ENGINEERING — ATTACKER PRETENDS TO BE SUPPORT



### How They Get You
You get a DM: "Hi, this is OSIRIS support. We've detected suspicious activity on your account. Please verify your seed phrase to secure your wallet." You panic. You send it. They drain you.



### Defense: Anti-Social-Engineering Protocol

```typescript
// src/lib/security/anti-social-engineering.ts

/**
 * OSIRIS will NEVER ask for:
 * - Your seed phrase
 * - Your private key
 * - Your password
 * - Your 2FA codes
 * - Screenshots of your wallet
 * 
 * This is enforced in code, not just policy.
 */

export const NEVER_REQUEST_LIST = [
  "seed phrase",
  "private key",
  "password",
  "2FA code",
  "verification code",
  "wallet screenshot",
  "screenshot of balance",
];

/**
 * Message Scanner — Detect social engineering attempts in Telegram
 */
export function scanForSocialEngineering(message: string): {
  suspicious: boolean;
  reasons: string[];
} {
  const reasons: string[] = [];
  const lower = message.toLowerCase();

  // Check for urgency triggers
  const urgencyWords = ["urgent", "immediately", "now", "asap", "hurry", "quick"];
  const urgencyCount = urgencyWords.filter((w) => lower.includes(w)).length;
  if (urgencyCount >= 2) {
    reasons.push("Excessive urgency — social engineering tactic");
  }

  // Check for credential requests
  for (const item of NEVER_REQUEST_LIST) {
    if (lower.includes(item)) {
      reasons.push(`Requests ${item} — OSIRIS never asks for this`);
    }
  }

  // Check for impersonation
  if (lower.includes("support") || lower.includes("admin") || lower.includes("team")) {
    reasons.push("Claims to be support — verify through official channels only");
  }

  // Check for external links
  const urlRegex = /(https?:\/\/[^\s]+)/g;
  const urls = message.match(urlRegex) || [];
  for (const url of urls) {
    if (!url.includes("osiris.trade")) {
      reasons.push(`External link detected: ${url}`);
    }
  }

  return {
    suspicious: reasons.length > 0,
    reasons,
  };
}

/**
 * Official Verification — How users verify they're talking to real OSIRIS
 */
export async function verifyOfficialContact(
  telegramUsername: string
): Promise<boolean> {
  // Only these usernames are official
  const OFFICIAL_BOTS = ["@osiris_trade_bot", "@osiris_support_bot"];
  const OFFICIAL_ADMINS = ["@osiris_admin"]; // Your personal account

  return OFFICIAL_BOTS.includes(telegramUsername) || 
         OFFICIAL_ADMINS.includes(telegramUsername);
}
```

## SCENARIO 11: MEMORY DUMP / FORENSIC RECOVERY



### How They Get You
Your server is seized by authorities or compromised. They dump the RAM. They find decrypted private keys in memory. They drain you.



### Defense: Memory Encryption + Secure Deletion

```typescript
// src/lib/security/memory-protection.ts

/**
 * Secure Memory Buffer
 * Uses Node.js Buffer with explicit zeroing
 * Keys exist in memory only during signing operation
 */
export class SecureBuffer {
  private buffer: Buffer;

  constructor(size: number) {
    this.buffer = Buffer.alloc(size);
  }

  write(data: Buffer, offset: number = 0): void {
    data.copy(this.buffer, offset);
  }

  read(offset: number, length: number): Buffer {
    return this.buffer.subarray(offset, offset + length);
  }

  // CRITICAL: Zero memory before release
  destroy(): void {
    this.buffer.fill(0);
    // Overwrite with random data first (defense against cold boot attack)
    crypto.randomFillSync(this.buffer);
    this.buffer.fill(0);
    this.buffer = Buffer.alloc(0);
  }
}

/**
 * Process Memory Protection
 * Prevent core dumps and swap
 */
export function lockProcessMemory(): void {
  if (process.platform === "linux") {
    // mlockall — prevent memory from being swapped to disk
    try {
      const ffi = require("ffi-napi");
      const libc = ffi.Library(null, {
        mlockall: ["int", ["int"]],
      });
      libc.mlockall(2); // MCL_CURRENT | MCL_FUTURE
    } catch {
      console.warn("mlockall not available — process memory may be swapped");
    }
  }
}

/**
 * Disable Core Dumps
 * Prevent memory dump on crash
 */
export function disableCoreDumps(): void {
  if (process.platform === "linux") {
    try {
      const { execSync } = require("child_process");
      execSync("ulimit -c 0"); // Disable core dumps
      execSync("echo 0 > /proc/sys/kernel/core_pattern");
    } catch {
      console.warn("Could not disable core dumps");
    }
  }
}
```

## SCENARIO 12: RANSOMWARE ON YOUR MACHINE



### How They Get You

### Defense: Immutable Backups + Decoy Wallets

```typescript
// src/lib/security/ransomware-defense.ts

/**
 * Decoy Wallet Strategy
 * Keep a small amount (0.1 SOL) in a "hot" wallet on your machine
 * Ransomware encrypts this. You don't care. Your real funds are in cold storage.
 */
export const DECOY_WALLET_BALANCE = 0.1 * 1e9; // 0.1 SOL in lamports

/**
 * Backup Verification — Ensure backups are restorable
 * Monthly automated test
 */
export async function verifyBackupIntegrity(): Promise<{
  valid: boolean;
  lastBackup: Date;
  issues: string[];
}> {
  const issues: string[] = [];

  // 1. Check backup exists
  const backups = await listBackups();
  if (backups.length === 0) {
    issues.push("No backups found");
  }

  // 2. Check backup age
  const lastBackup = backups[0]?.createdAt;
  if (lastBackup && Date.now() - lastBackup.getTime() > 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000) {
    issues.push("Last backup is older than 24 hours");
  }

  // 3. Verify backup checksum
  for (const backup of backups.slice(0, 3)) {
    const calculatedHash = createHash("sha256")
      .update(await readBackupFile(backup.path))
      .digest("hex");
    if (calculatedHash !== backup.checksum) {
      issues.push(`Backup ${backup.id} checksum mismatch — corrupted`);
    }
  }

  // 4. Test restore to temporary location (don't overwrite live data)
  try {
    await testRestore(backups[0]);
  } catch {
    issues.push("Backup restore test failed");
  }

  return {
    valid: issues.length === 0,
    lastBackup: lastBackup || new Date(0),
    issues,
  };
}
```

```typescript
// src/lib/security/dns-monitoring.ts

/**
 * Monitor DNS records for unauthorized changes
 */
export async function monitorDNSRecords(): Promise<void> {
  const expectedARecords = ["203.0.113.1", "203.0.113.2"];
  const expectedNSRecords = ["carl.ns.cloudflare.com", "lara.ns.cloudflare.com"];

  // Query DNS
  const { promises: dns } = require("dns");
  const aRecords = await dns.resolve4("osiris.trade");
  const nsRecords = await dns.resolveNs("osiris.trade");

  // Check for unauthorized changes
  const unauthorizedA = aRecords.filter((r: string) => !expectedARecords.includes(r));
  const unauthorizedNS = nsRecords.filter((r: string) => !expectedNSRecords.includes(r));

  if (unauthorizedA.length > 0 || unauthorizedNS.length > 0) {
    await securityLogger.log({
      eventType: "DNS_HIJACKING_DETECTED",
      severity: "critical",
      details: {
        unauthorizedA,
        unauthorizedNS,
        expectedA: expectedARecords,
        expectedNS: expectedNSRecords,
      },
      timestamp: new Date(),
      ipAddress: "",
    });

    // Immediate response: notify all users, freeze trading
    await freezeAllTrading("DNS_HIJACKING_DETECTED");
  }
}
```

## SCENARIO 14: ZERO-DAY EXPLOIT IN DEPENDENCY



### How They Get You
A zero-day is discovered in `@solana/web3.js`. Attacker exploits it to steal private keys from memory. You update immediately, but they already drained you.



### Defense: Dependency Sandboxing + Runtime Monitoring

```typescript
// src/lib/security/runtime-monitoring.ts

/**
 * Runtime Behavior Monitoring
 * Detect anomalous behavior from dependencies
 */
export class RuntimeMonitor {
  private allowedNetworkHosts = [
    "mainnet.helius-rpc.com",
    "quote-api.jup.ag",
    "api.telegram.org",
    "pumpportal.fun",
  ];

  startMonitoring(): void {
    // Monitor network requests
    const originalFetch = globalThis.fetch;
    globalThis.fetch = async (...args) => {
      const url = args[0].toString();
      const hostname = new URL(url).hostname;

      if (!this.allowedNetworkHosts.includes(hostname)) {
        await securityLogger.log({
          eventType: "SUSPICIOUS_NETWORK_REQUEST",
          severity: "high",
          details: {
            url,
            hostname,
            stackTrace: new Error().stack?.substring(0, 500),
          },
          timestamp: new Date(),
          ipAddress: "",
        });

        // Block the request
        throw new Error(`Blocked network request to unauthorized host: ${hostname}`);
      }

      return originalFetch(...args);
    };

    // Monitor file system access (Node.js)
    if (typeof process !== "undefined") {
      const fs = require("fs");
      const originalReadFile = fs.readFileSync;
      fs.readFileSync = (...args: any[]) => {
        const path = args[0];
        const sensitivePaths = ["/etc/passwd", ".env", ".ssh/id_rsa", "wallet.json"];

        for (const sensitive of sensitivePaths) {
          if (path.includes(sensitive)) {
            securityLogger.log({
              eventType: "SENSITIVE_FILE_ACCESS",
              severity: "high",
              details: { path, stackTrace: new Error().stack?.substring(0, 500) },
              timestamp: new Date(),
              ipAddress: "",
            });
          }
        }

        return originalReadFile(...args);
      };
    }
  }
}
```

## SCENARIO 15: COMPROMISED TELEGRAM BOT TOKEN



### How They Get You
Your Telegram bot token is in an env var. Attacker gains server access. They read the token. They send fake messages to all users: "Urgent: verify your wallet at fake-osiris.com". Users click. Drained.



### Defense: Token Rotation + Webhook Verification

```typescript
// src/bot/security.ts

/**
 * Telegram Bot Token Security
 * Token is stored in Docker secret, not env var
 * Rotated monthly automatically
 */
export class BotTokenManager {
  private currentToken: string;
  private rotationInterval: NodeJS.Timeout | null = null;

  constructor() {
    this.currentToken = this.readTokenFromSecret();
    this.scheduleRotation();
  }

  private readTokenFromSecret(): string {
    // Read from Docker secret (mounted as file, not env var)
    const fs = require("fs");
    return fs.readFileSync("/run/secrets/telegram_bot_token", "utf8").trim();
  }

  private scheduleRotation(): void {
    // Rotate every 30 days
    this.rotationInterval = setInterval(async () => {
      await this.rotateToken();
    }, 30 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000);
  }

  async rotateToken(): Promise<void> {
    // 1. Generate new token via BotFather
    const newToken = await this.generateNewToken();

    // 2. Update webhook with new token
    await fetch(`https://api.telegram.org/bot${newToken}/setWebhook`, {
      method: "POST",
      body: JSON.stringify({
        url: `${process.env.TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_URL}?token=${newToken}`,
        secret_token: crypto.randomBytes(32).toString("hex"),
      }),
    });

    // 3. Update Docker secret
    await this.updateDockerSecret(newToken);

    // 4. Restart bot with new token
    this.currentToken = newToken;
  }

  private async generateNewToken(): Promise<string> {
    // Use BotFather API to revoke and regenerate
    // This requires manual step or automated BotFather interaction
    throw new Error("Token rotation requires manual BotFather interaction");
  }

  private async updateDockerSecret(newToken: string): Promise<void> {
    // Update Docker secret and restart service
    const fs = require("fs");
    fs.writeFileSync("/run/secrets/telegram_bot_token", newToken);
  }
}
```

## PART 2: THE SECURITY DASHBOARD (USER-FACING)



### Live Security Score

```typescript
// src/components/security/SecurityScore.tsx

interface SecurityScoreProps {
  userId: string;
}

export function SecurityScore({ userId }: SecurityScoreProps) {
  const { data: score } = trpc.security.getScore.useQuery({ userId });

  const getColor = (s: number) => {
    if (s >= 90) return "text-green-500";
    if (s >= 70) return "text-yellow-500";
    return "text-red-500";
  };

  const getLabel = (s: number) => {
    if (s >= 90) return "Fortress Level";
    if (s >= 70) return "Protected";
    if (s >= 50) return "Vulnerable";
    return "Critical Risk";
  };

  return (
    <div className="rounded-xl border border-slate-700 bg-slate-900 p-6">
      <div className="flex items-center justify-between">
        <div>
          <h3 className="text-lg font-semibold text-white">Security Score</h3>
          <p className="text-sm text-slate-400">
            Based on {score?.checksPassed || 0} of {score?.totalChecks || 0} security checks
          </p>
        </div>
        <div className={`text-4xl font-bold ${getColor(score?.score || 0)}`}>
          {score?.score || 0}
          <span className="text-lg text-slate-500">/100</span>
        </div>
      </div>

      {/* Progress bar */}
      <div className="mt-4 h-2 rounded-full bg-slate-800">
        <div
          className={`h-2 rounded-full transition-all ${
            score?.score >= 90 ? "bg-green-500" :
            score?.score >= 70 ? "bg-yellow-500" : "bg-red-500"
          }`}
          style={{ width: `${score?.score || 0}%` }}
        />
      </div>

      {/* Individual checks */}
      <div className="mt-6 space-y-3">
        {score?.checks.map((check) => (
          <SecurityCheckRow key={check.id} check={check} />
        ))}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}

function SecurityCheckRow({ check }: { check: SecurityCheck }) {
  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
      {check.passed ? (
        <ShieldCheck className="h-5 w-5 text-green-500" />
      ) : (
        <ShieldAlert className="h-5 w-5 text-red-500" />
      )}
      <div className="flex-1">
        <p className="text-sm font-medium text-white">{check.name}</p>
        <p className="text-xs text-slate-400">{check.description}</p>
      </div>
      {!check.passed && check.action && (
        <button
          onClick={check.action}
          className="rounded-lg bg-blue-600 px-3 py-1 text-xs font-medium text-white hover:bg-blue-700"
        >
          Fix
        </button>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Security Score Calculation

```typescript
// src/server/routers/security.ts

export const securityRouter = router({
  getScore: protectedProcedure
    .input(z.object({ userId: z.string() }))
    .query(async ({ input, ctx }) => {
      const checks: SecurityCheck[] = [];

      // 1. 2FA Enabled
      const user = await db.query.users.findFirst({
        where: eq(users.id, input.userId),
      });
      checks.push({
        id: "mfa",
        name: "Two-Factor Authentication",
        description: "TOTP or WebAuthn required for all sensitive operations",
        passed: user?.mfaEnabled || false,
        weight: 20,
        action: () => router.push("/settings/security/2fa"),
      });

      // 2. Strong Password
      checks.push({
        id: "password",
        name: "Strong Password",
        description: "Minimum 16 characters, not in breach databases",
        passed: user?.passwordStrength === "strong",
        weight: 10,
        action: () => router.push("/settings/security/password"),
      });

      // 3. WebAuthn Security Key
      checks.push({
        id: "webauthn",
        name: "Hardware Security Key",
        description: "FIDO2/WebAuthn enabled — unphishable, unkeyloggable",
        passed: user?.webauthnEnabled || false,
        weight: 15,
        action: () => router.push("/settings/security/webauthn"),
      });

      // 4. Session Fingerprinting
      checks.push({
        id: "fingerprint",
        name: "Device Binding",
        description: "Sessions locked to your device fingerprint",
        passed: user?.sessionFingerprintEnabled || false,
        weight: 10,
        action: () => router.push("/settings/security/devices"),
      });

      // 5. Withdrawal Whitelist
      checks.push({
        id: "whitelist",
        name: "Withdrawal Whitelist",
        description: "Only pre-approved addresses can receive withdrawals",
        passed: (await db.query.withdrawalWhitelist.findMany({
          where: eq(withdrawalWhitelist.userId, input.userId),
        })).length > 0,
        weight: 15,
        action: () => router.push("/settings/security/whitelist"),
      });

      // 6. Circuit Breaker
      checks.push({
        id: "circuit",
        name: "Loss Circuit Breaker",
        description: "Auto-halt trading if losses exceed threshold",
        passed: user?.circuitBreakerEnabled || false,
        weight: 10,
        action: () => router.push("/settings/security/circuit-breaker"),
      });

      // 7. Login Notifications
      checks.push({
        id: "notifications",
        name: "Login Notifications",
        description: "Alert on every new device/login",
        passed: user?.loginNotificationsEnabled || false,
        weight: 5,
        action: () => router.push("/settings/notifications"),
      });

      // 8. Recovery Setup
      checks.push({
        id: "recovery",
        name: "Account Recovery",
        description: "Secure recovery method configured",
        passed: user?.recoveryEmailVerified || false,
        weight: 10,
        action: () => router.push("/settings/security/recovery"),
      });

      // 9. Behavioral Biometrics
      checks.push({
        id: "biometrics",
        name: "Behavioral Biometrics",
        description: "Typing/mouse pattern recognition enabled",
        passed: user?.behavioralBiometricsEnabled || false,
        weight: 5,
        action: () => router.push("/settings/security/biometrics"),
      });

      // Calculate weighted score
      const totalWeight = checks.reduce((sum, c) => sum + c.weight, 0);
      const passedWeight = checks
        .filter((c) => c.passed)
        .reduce((sum, c) => sum + c.weight, 0);
      const score = Math.round((passedWeight / totalWeight) * 100);

      return {
        score,
        totalChecks: checks.length,
        checksPassed: checks.filter((c) => c.passed).length,
        checks,
      };
    }),
});
```

```typescript
export function SecurityAlert({ event }: { event: SecurityEvent }) {
  const icons = {
    LOGIN_NEW_DEVICE: Smartphone,

          event.severity === "critical" ? "bg-red-500/10" :
          event.severity === "high" ? "bg-yellow-500/10" :
          "bg-green-500/10"
        }`}>
          <Icon className={`h-5 w-5 ${
            event.severity === "critical" ? "text-red-500" :
            event.severity === "high" ? "text-yellow-500" :
            "text-green-500"
          }`} />
        </div>
        <div className="flex-1">
          <p className="font-medium text-white">{event.title}</p>
          <p className="text-sm text-slate-400">{event.description}</p>
          <p className="mt-1 text-xs text-slate-500">
            {formatDistanceToNow(event.timestamp, { addSuffix: true })}
          </p>
        </div>
        {event.actionable && (
          <Button size="sm" variant="outline" className="border-slate-700">
            Review
          </Button>
        )}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Telegram Security Bot

```typescript
// src/bot/security-notifications.ts

export async function sendSecurityAlert(
  userId: string,
  event: SecurityEvent
): Promise<void> {
  const user = await db.query.users.findFirst({
    where: eq(users.id, userId),
  });

  if (!user?.telegramId) return;

  const messages: Record<string, string> = {
    LOGIN_NEW_DEVICE: `🔐 *New Login Detected*

` +
      `Device: ${event.details.device}
` +
      `Location: ${event.details.location}
` +
      `IP: ${event.details.ip}

` +
      `If this wasn't you, reply *REVOKE* immediately.`,

    WITHDRAWAL_LARGE: `💸 *Large Withdrawal Requested*

` +
      `Amount: ${event.details.amount} SOL
` +
      `To: \`${event.details.destination}\`

` +
      `Reply *CONFIRM* to proceed or *CANCEL* to block.`,

    SESSION_REVOKED: `🛑 *Session Revoked*

` +
      `Reason: ${event.details.reason}
` +
      `All active trades have been halted.`,

    SUSPICIOUS_ACTIVITY: `⚠️ *Suspicious Activity Detected*

` +
      `Type: ${event.details.type}
` +
      `Confidence: ${event.details.confidence}%

` +
      `Your account has been temporarily locked. Contact support.`,
  };

  const message = messages[event.type] || `🔔 *Security Alert*

${event.description}`;

  await bot.api.sendMessage(user.telegramId, message, {
    parse_mode: "Markdown",
    reply_markup: event.actionable ? {
      inline_keyboard: [
        [{ text: "✅ Confirm", callback_data: `security:confirm:${event.id}` }],
        [{ text: "🛑 Block", callback_data: `security:block:${event.id}` }],
      ],
    } : undefined,
  });
}
```

```typescript
interface SecurityBadge {

  icon: string;

const SECURITY_BADGES: SecurityBadge[] = [
  {
    id: "2fa_novice",
    name: "2FA Novice",
    description: "Enabled two-factor authentication",
    icon: "🔐",
    condition: (u) => u.mfaEnabled,
    rarity: "common",
  },
  {
    id: "hardware_guardian",
    name: "Hardware Guardian",
    description: "Set up WebAuthn/FIDO2 security key",
    icon: "🔑",
    condition: (u) => u.webauthnEnabled,
    rarity: "rare",
  },
  {
    id: "fortress",
    name: "The Fortress",
    description: "Achieved 90+ security score",
    icon: "🏰",
    condition: (u) => u.securityScore >= 90,
    rarity: "epic",
  },
  {
    id: "paranoid",
    name: "Paranoid",
    description: "Enabled ALL security features",
    icon: "🛡️",
    condition: (u) =>
      u.mfaEnabled &&
      u.webauthnEnabled &&
      u.behavioralBiometricsEnabled &&
      u.sessionFingerprintEnabled &&
      u.circuitBreakerEnabled &&
      u.withdrawalWhitelist.length > 0,
    rarity: "legendary",
  },
  {
    id: "survivor",
    name: "Survivor",
    description: "Successfully blocked a social engineering attempt",
    icon: "🎯",
    condition: (u) => u.socialEngineeringBlocks > 0,
    rarity: "legendary",
  },
];

// Award badge + notify
export async function awardBadge(userId: string, badgeId: string): Promise<void> {
  const badge = SECURITY_BADGES.find((b) => b.id === badgeId);
  if (!badge) return;

  await db.insert(userBadges).values({
    userId,
    badgeId,
    awardedAt: new Date(),
  }).onConflictDoNothing();

  // Notify user
  await sendSecurityAlert(userId, {
    type: "BADGE_EARNED",
    title: `Badge Earned: ${badge.name}`,
    description: badge.description,
    severity: "low",
    timestamp: new Date(),
    actionable: false,
  });
}
```

PART 0 — HOW TO USE THIS DOCUMENT

## 0.1 What this document is

The Red Team's final assessment named seven "easiest entry points" and one thing
that worries them. The Blue Team answered with a list of countermeasures. That
exchange was correct in spirit and wrong in several specific, load-bearing
places: some of the Blue Team's countermeasures do not work as written, several
contradict each other, several are ineffective against the exact attack they
were written to stop, and at least eleven code snippets in the existing material
will crash, silently no-op, or open the hole they claim to close.

This document does four things, in this order:

  1. Argues the stack against itself (PART 1). Every major architectural
     decision is stated as a position, attacked, defended, and ruled on. If a
     ruling goes against the existing spec, the ruling wins.

  2. Registers every defect found in the existing material (PART 2), with the
     exact location, why it is wrong, what it costs, and the corrected artifact.
     Defects are IDs DEF-001 .. DEF-061.

  3. Replaces the seven "easiest entry points" with *structural* fixes (PART 3).
     A structural fix is one where the vulnerable state is not reachable, not
     one where a developer must remember to do something. Every entry point gets
     a control, an artifact, and an automated test that fails the build if the
     control regresses.

  4. Publishes the canonical stack, layer by layer (PART 4), a verification
     suite (PART 5), an ordered implementation plan (PART 6), an explicit
     not-doing list (PART 7), a residual risk register (PART 8), and an honest
     cost table (PART 9).



## 0.2 The three invariants

Everything below serves three invariants. If an implementation decision does not
serve one of these, it is decoration and should be cut.

  INV-1  KEY MATERIAL NEVER EXISTS ON THE APPLICATION HOST.
         Not in memory, not for 50ms, not during signing, not in a core dump.
         Remote code execution on the trading host must not yield a private key.
         This is the difference between "we got owned" and "users lost funds."

  INV-2  EVERY AUTHORIZATION DECISION IS ENFORCED TWICE, IN TWO DIFFERENT
         SYSTEMS, WRITTEN BY TWO DIFFERENT MECHANISMS.
         Application-layer check plus database-layer check. A forgotten
         application check must fail closed at the database. A compromised
         application must fail closed at the signer.

  INV-3  EVERY CONTROL HAS A TEST THAT FAILS THE BUILD WHEN THE CONTROL IS
         REMOVED.
         A control that is not tested is a comment. The existing material is
         full of controls that are comments.



## 0.3 Precedence — what this document supersedes

Where this document conflicts with prior material, this document wins. The
following prior sections are SUPERSEDED IN FULL and must not be implemented as
written:

  SUPERSEDED FROM OSIRIS_RED_TEAM_BLUE_TEAM_SECURITY.md
    - 1.1 item 6  (the custom ssh-monitor.sh bash loop)          -> DEF-014
