```dockerfile
# Dockerfile — multi-stage, non-root, distroless-adjacent, no shell in the
# runtime layer.
FROM node:22-bookworm-slim@sha256:PIN_ME AS deps
WORKDIR /app
COPY package.json package-lock.json .npmrc ./
RUN npm ci --ignore-scripts                     # DEF-032
COPY scripts/run-allowed-build-scripts.mjs ./scripts/
RUN node scripts/run-allowed-build-scripts.mjs  # explicit allowlist only

FROM node:22-bookworm-slim@sha256:PIN_ME AS build
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=deps /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY . .
RUN npm run build && npm prune --omit=dev --ignore-scripts

FROM gcr.io/distroless/nodejs22-debian12:nonroot@sha256:PIN_ME AS runtime
# distroless has no shell, no package manager, no coreutils. Post-RCE tooling
# has to be brought in, which is loud, and many exploit chains simply break.
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=build --chown=nonroot:nonroot /app/.next/standalone ./
COPY --from=build --chown=nonroot:nonroot /app/.next/static ./.next/static
COPY --from=build --chown=nonroot:nonroot /app/public ./public
USER nonroot
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["server.js"]
```
Note: distroless `nonroot` is UID 65532. If you use it, set `user: "65532:65532"`
in compose, or omit `user:` and rely on the image's USER. Do not guess — run
TEST-203.

```typescript
// src/server/boot/assert-container-hardening.ts
// Runs FIRST, before the server listens. If the container is not hardened, the
// app does not start. This survives edits to docker-compose.yml, which is
// exactly the failure mode we are defending against.
import { statSync, accessSync, constants, readFileSync } from "node:fs";

export function assertContainerHardening(): void {
  if (process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production") return;
  const fail = (m: string): never => {
    console.error(JSON.stringify({ level: "fatal", event: "hardening_failed", reason: m }));
    process.exit(1);
  };

  // 1. Not root.
  if (typeof process.getuid === "function" && process.getuid() === 0)
    fail("running as uid 0");

  // 2. Root filesystem is read-only. Writing must fail.
  try {
    require("node:fs").writeFileSync("/.osiris-write-probe", "x");
    require("node:fs").unlinkSync("/.osiris-write-probe");
    fail("root filesystem is writable");
  } catch { /* expected: EROFS or EACCES */ }

  // 3. The Docker socket must not be present.
  try { statSync("/var/run/docker.sock"); fail("docker socket is mounted"); }
  catch { /* expected */ }

  // 4. No dangerous capabilities. CapEff must be empty.
  try {
    const status = readFileSync("/proc/self/status", "utf8");
    const eff = /^CapEff:\s*([0-9a-f]+)$/m.exec(status)?.[1];
    if (eff && BigInt("0x" + eff) !== 0n) fail(`non-empty CapEff: ${eff}`);
  } catch { /* /proc unavailable: ignore rather than crash */ }

  // 5. no_new_privs must be set.
  try {
    const status = readFileSync("/proc/self/status", "utf8");
    if (!/^NoNewPrivs:\s*1$/m.test(status)) fail("no_new_privs is not set");
  } catch { /* ignore */ }

  // 6. Not in the host PID namespace: PID 1 must be us or our supervisor,
  //    and /proc/1/cmdline must not look like systemd.
  try {
    const p1 = readFileSync("/proc/1/cmdline", "utf8");
    if (p1.includes("systemd") || p1.includes("/sbin/init"))
      fail("host PID namespace");
  } catch { /* ignore */ }
}
```
```typescript
// server.js entrypoint
import { assertContainerHardening } from "./src/server/boot/assert-container-hardening.js";
assertContainerHardening();     // before anything else
```

```javascript
// scripts/verify-compose-hardening.mjs — runs in CI. Fails the build.
import { parse } from "yaml";
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";

const c = parse(readFileSync("docker-compose.yml", "utf8"));
const errors = [];
for (const [name, s] of Object.entries(c.services)) {
  if (s.privileged) errors.push(`${name}: privileged`);
  if (!s.read_only) errors.push(`${name}: read_only not set`);
  if (!s.security_opt?.includes("no-new-privileges:true"))
    errors.push(`${name}: no-new-privileges missing`);
  if (!s.cap_drop?.includes("ALL")) errors.push(`${name}: cap_drop ALL missing`);
  if (!s.user) errors.push(`${name}: no user: key`);
  if (!s.pids_limit) errors.push(`${name}: no pids_limit`);
  if (!s.mem_limit) errors.push(`${name}: no mem_limit`);
  if (!/@sha256:/.test(s.image ?? "")) errors.push(`${name}: image not digest-pinned`);
  for (const v of s.volumes ?? [])
    if (String(v).includes("docker.sock")) errors.push(`${name}: docker socket mounted`);
  for (const p of s.ports ?? [])
    if (!String(p).startsWith("127.0.0.1:"))
      errors.push(`${name}: port ${p} not bound to loopback`);
  for (const cap of s.cap_add ?? [])
    if (["SYS_ADMIN","SYS_PTRACE","NET_ADMIN","SYS_MODULE","DAC_READ_SEARCH"].includes(cap))
      errors.push(`${name}: dangerous cap_add ${cap}`);
}
if (errors.length) { console.error(errors.join("\n")); process.exit(1); }
console.log("compose hardening OK");
```

Plus the DEF-010 DOCKER-USER firewall rules, which mean that even a mistaken
`ports: ["0.0.0.0:5432:5432"]` is not reachable from outside.

RESIDUAL
  - A kernel exploit escapes any container configuration. Mitigated by
    unattended-upgrades and by the fact that, under CTL-100, host root does not
    yield key material.
  - Distroless makes post-exploitation harder, not impossible; a pure-Node
    payload runs fine.
  - Recorded as RISK-007.

TESTS
  TEST-203  For every service, `docker run --rm <image> id <user>` matches the
            compose `user:` value. No hardcoded UID goes unverified.
  TEST-209  `verify-compose-hardening.mjs` passes.
  TEST-210  Boot the app image with `--user 0` and assert it exits non-zero
            with `hardening_failed`. This is the test that proves the runtime
            assertion works.
  TEST-211  Boot without `read_only` and assert it exits non-zero.
  TEST-202  From an external host, connections to the public IP on 5432 and
            6379 time out.

================================================================================
EP-3 — A MISSING AUTH CHECK ON ONE tRPC ENDPOINT
================================================================================

ATTACK
"tRPC endpoints might have missing auth checks. I fuzz all endpoints with typical
mutations. I find one that doesn't verify the user owns the session. I revoke
someone else's session. I trade with their wallet. I drain them."

WHY THE EXISTING FIX IS NOT ENOUGH
The Blue Team wrote: "Every tRPC procedure MUST have auth middleware. Resource
ownership verification on EVERY mutation." Both are correct requirements and
neither is a control. They are instructions to a human — and increasingly, to an
AI agent generating endpoints from an existing pattern, which will faithfully
reproduce whichever pattern it happened to see, including a public one.

The Red Team's phrasing is precise and worth sitting with: *one* endpoint. Not
a systematic failure. One. Out of what will be sixty or eighty procedures across
a dozen routers, written over months, some by an agent. The probability that all
of them are correct is not high, and the probability that all of them *stay*
correct through six months of feature work is lower.

There is also a second bypass the corpus does not consider at all: an attacker
with database write access can move a ciphertext blob into a row they own
(DEF-027), at which point every ownership check passes and returns the right
answer to the wrong question.

STRUCTURAL FIX — four independent mechanisms

  M1  UNCONSTRUCTIBLE. The raw tRPC procedure builder is not exported. There is
      no way to write an unauthenticated procedure without importing from a file
      that lint forbids importing.
  M2  ENUMERATED. A test walks the built router at runtime, lists every
      procedure, and asserts each one carries the auth middleware — except those
      in an explicit allowlist file. Adding a public endpoint requires editing
      that file, which is a diff a reviewer sees.
  M3  DATABASE-ENFORCED. PostgreSQL row-level security on every user-scoped
      table. A forgotten ownership check returns zero rows instead of another
      user's data. Different mechanism, different language, different failure
      mode (INV-2).
  M4  SIGNER-ENFORCED. Even with a valid session and a returned row, the signer
      independently verifies that the wallet's derived public key matches the
      request context, and the AAD binding (DEF-027) makes a swapped blob
      undecryptable. The last line does not trust the application at all.

Any one of M1-M4 holding is sufficient to prevent the attack. All four failing
simultaneously is the requirement.

ARTIFACTS — M1: unconstructible

```typescript
// src/server/trpc/base.ts — THE ONLY FILE ALLOWED TO IMPORT @trpc/server
import { initTRPC, TRPCError } from "@trpc/server";
import superjson from "superjson";
import type { Context } from "./context";

const t = initTRPC.context<Context>().create({ transformer: superjson });

// t is NOT exported. This is the whole trick.
export const router = t.router;
export const mergeRouters = t.mergeRouters;

/** Marker middlewares. Their presence is what TEST-401 detects. */
const AUTH_MARKER = "osiris.auth.v1";
const authed = t.middleware(async ({ ctx, next }) => {
  const session = await ctx.getSession();
  if (!session?.user) throw new TRPCError({ code: "UNAUTHORIZED" });
  // Revocation epoch check: a panic revoke invalidates everything older,
  // without waiting for a cache TTL (DEF-029).
  if (await isRevoked(session)) throw new TRPCError({ code: "UNAUTHORIZED" });
  return next({ ctx: { ...ctx, session, userId: session.user.id } });
});
Object.defineProperty(authed, "__osirisMarker", { value: AUTH_MARKER });

const originGuard = t.middleware(async ({ ctx, next, type }) => {
  if (type === "mutation") assertSameOrigin(ctx.req);   // DEF-023
  return next();
});

/** Runs every user-scoped query inside a transaction with the RLS setting
 *  applied. Nothing else may open a transaction for user data. */
const withRls = t.middleware(async ({ ctx, next }) => {
  return ctx.db.transaction(async (tx) => {
    await tx.execute(sql`SELECT set_config('osiris.user_id', ${ctx.userId}, true)`);
    return next({ ctx: { ...ctx, tx } });
  });
});

/** Public procedures still get rate limiting and origin checks. There is no
 *  such thing as an unguarded procedure in this codebase. */
export const publicProcedure = t.procedure
  .use(originGuard)
  .use(rateLimit({ bucket: "public", policy: "fail_closed" }));

export const protectedProcedure = publicProcedure
  .use(authed)
  .use(withRls)
  .use(rateLimit({ bucket: "user", policy: "fail_closed" }));

/** For anything that touches a live trading session. Adds session validity,
 *  ownership, and the lease CAS from DEF-028. */
export const sessionProcedure = protectedProcedure.use(sessionGuard);

export const adminProcedure = protectedProcedure.use(adminGuard);
```

```typescript
// test/security/all-procedures-protected.test.ts   (TEST-401)
import { appRouter } from "@/server/routers/_app";
import { INTENTIONALLY_PUBLIC } from "@/server/trpc/public-procedures";

function walk(router: any, prefix = ""): Array<[string, any]> {
  const out: Array<[string, any]> = [];
  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries<any>(router._def.record ?? router._def.procedures ?? {})) {
    const path = prefix ? `${prefix}.${k}` : k;
    if (v._def?.router) out.push(...walk(v, path));
    else out.push([path, v]);
  }
  return out;
}

describe("every tRPC procedure is authenticated", () => {
  const procedures = walk(appRouter);

  it("finds procedures at all (guards against a broken walker)", () => {
    expect(procedures.length).toBeGreaterThan(10);
  });

  it.each(procedures)("%s", (path, proc) => {
    if (INTENTIONALLY_PUBLIC.has(path)) return;
    const markers = (proc._def.middlewares ?? []).map((m: any) => m.__osirisMarker);
    expect(markers).toContain("osiris.auth.v1");
  });

  it("the public allowlist contains no stale entries", () => {
    const known = new Set(procedures.map(([p]) => p));
    for (const p of INTENTIONALLY_PUBLIC) expect(known.has(p)).toBe(true);
  });

  it("every mutation on a user resource is a protected or session procedure", () => {
    for (const [path, proc] of procedures) {
      if (proc._def.mutation && !INTENTIONALLY_PUBLIC.has(path)) {
        const markers = (proc._def.middlewares ?? []).map((m: any) => m.__osirisMarker);
        expect(markers).toContain("osiris.auth.v1");
      }
    }
  });
});
```
Note on maintenance: tRPC's internal `_def` shape changes between major
versions. Pin the tRPC version, and if this test breaks after an upgrade, FIX
THE TEST — do not skip it. A skipped TEST-401 is an unlocked front door.

ARTIFACTS — M3: row-level security

```sql
-- migrations/0002_rls.sql
-- Roles. The application NEVER connects as the owner.
CREATE ROLE osiris_owner NOLOGIN;
CREATE ROLE osiris_app   LOGIN PASSWORD :'app_password' NOINHERIT;
CREATE ROLE osiris_ro    LOGIN PASSWORD :'ro_password'  NOINHERIT;

-- osiris_app can act on data and nothing else.
REVOKE ALL ON SCHEMA public FROM PUBLIC;
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO osiris_app, osiris_ro;
GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO osiris_app;
GRANT USAGE, SELECT ON ALL SEQUENCES IN SCHEMA public TO osiris_app;
GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO osiris_ro;
-- No DDL. No CREATE. Migrations run as osiris_owner via a separate DATABASE_URL
-- that the running application does not possess.
REVOKE CREATE ON SCHEMA public FROM osiris_app, osiris_ro;

-- The audit log is append-only for the application (DEF-042).
REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE ON audit_logs FROM osiris_app;

-- Enable RLS. FORCE means even the table owner is subject, which closes the
-- "but the app connects as owner" hole before it can be opened.
DO $$
DECLARE t text;
BEGIN
  FOREACH t IN ARRAY ARRAY[
    'wallets','trading_sessions','trades','tax_lots','positions',
    'copy_targets','notifications','user_settings','trade_intents',
    'user_security_holds','withdrawal_allowlist'
  ] LOOP
    EXECUTE format('ALTER TABLE %I ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY', t);
    EXECUTE format('ALTER TABLE %I FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY', t);
    EXECUTE format($f$
      CREATE POLICY %1$I_owner ON %1$I
        USING      (user_id = current_setting('osiris.user_id', true))
        WITH CHECK (user_id = current_setting('osiris.user_id', true))
    $f$, t);
  END LOOP;
END $$;

-- current_setting(..., true) returns NULL when unset. NULL = NULL is NULL, not
-- true, so an unset context matches no rows. Fail-closed by construction: if a
-- code path forgets withUser(), it sees an empty database rather than
-- everything.
```
```typescript
// src/db/with-user.ts — the ONLY sanctioned path for user-scoped queries
/**
 * CRITICAL: set_config(..., is_local = true) is transaction-scoped and reverts
 * on commit or rollback. A non-local SET would persist on the pooled connection
 * and leak to the NEXT request that borrows it — a cross-user data disclosure
 * far worse than having no RLS. Under PgBouncer transaction pooling the local
 * form is still correct; the non-local form is catastrophic. Never change the
 * third argument.
 */
export async function withUser<T>(
  userId: string,
  fn: (tx: Transaction) => Promise<T>
): Promise<T> {
  if (!userId) throw new Error("withUser called without a userId");
  return db.transaction(async (tx) => {
    await tx.execute(sql`SELECT set_config('osiris.user_id', ${userId}, true)`);
    return fn(tx);
  });
}

/** For background jobs that legitimately act across users (the copy-trading
 *  engine, the reaper). Narrowly granted, separately audited, and it logs. */
export async function withSystemContext<T>(
  reason: string,
  fn: (tx: Transaction) => Promise<T>
): Promise<T> {
  await auditLog({ eventType: "SYSTEM_CONTEXT_USED", severity: "low", details: { reason } });
  return db.transaction(async (tx) => {
    await tx.execute(sql`SELECT set_config('osiris.bypass_rls', 'on', true)`);
    return fn(tx);
  });
}
```
The system-context policy is added as a second permissive policy:
```sql
CREATE POLICY %1$I_system ON %1$I
  USING (current_setting('osiris.bypass_rls', true) = 'on');
```
and `withSystemContext` is lint-restricted to `src/jobs/**`, with every call
site reviewed.

```typescript
// test/security/rls.test.ts   (TEST-402)
it("cross-user read returns nothing even without an app-layer check", async () => {
  const rows = await withUser(userA.id, (tx) =>
    tx.select().from(wallets).where(eq(wallets.id, userB.walletId))   // no ownership check!
  );
  expect(rows).toHaveLength(0);
});

it("cross-user write is refused", async () => {
  await expect(
    withUser(userA.id, (tx) =>
      tx.update(tradingSessions).set({ status: "revoked" })
        .where(eq(tradingSessions.id, userB.sessionId))
    )
  ).resolves.toHaveLength(0);        // WITH CHECK blocks the row
});

it("no user context sees nothing", async () => {
  const rows = await db.select().from(wallets);   // deliberately outside withUser
  expect(rows).toHaveLength(0);
});

it("the RLS setting does not leak across pooled connections", async () => {
  // Hammer the pool concurrently with two identities and assert no crossover.
  await Promise.all(Array.from({ length: 200 }, (_, i) => {
    const u = i % 2 ? userA : userB;
    return withUser(u.id, async (tx) => {
      const r = await tx.select().from(wallets);
      expect(r.every((w) => w.userId === u.id)).toBe(true);
    });
  }));
});

it("every user-scoped table has RLS enabled and forced", async () => {
  const rows = await ownerDb.execute(sql`
    SELECT relname, relrowsecurity, relforcerowsecurity
    FROM pg_class WHERE relname = ANY(${USER_SCOPED_TABLES})`);
  for (const r of rows) {
    expect(r.relrowsecurity).toBe(true);
    expect(r.relforcerowsecurity).toBe(true);
  }
});
```
Add a Postgres event trigger so that disabling RLS is itself an alert:
```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION osiris_guard_rls() RETURNS event_trigger AS $$
DECLARE r record;
BEGIN
  FOR r IN SELECT * FROM pg_event_trigger_ddl_commands() LOOP
    IF r.command_tag = 'ALTER TABLE' THEN
      INSERT INTO audit_logs(event_type, severity, details, hash, previous_hash)
      VALUES ('DDL_ALTER_TABLE','high', to_jsonb(r), 'PENDING','PENDING');
    END IF;
  END LOOP;
END $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
CREATE EVENT TRIGGER osiris_ddl_guard ON ddl_command_end EXECUTE FUNCTION osiris_guard_rls();
```

RESIDUAL
  - A bug in `withUser` itself, or a query issued outside it, bypasses M3. The
    "no user context sees nothing" test plus the lint restriction is the
    mitigation.
  - M4 still holds regardless.
  - Recorded as RISK-003.

TESTS  TEST-401 (all procedures protected), TEST-402 (RLS, four assertions),
       TEST-404 (lint rule present and failing on a deliberate violation).

================================================================================
EP-4 — TELEGRAM WEBHOOK WITHOUT A SIGNATURE CHECK
================================================================================

ATTACK
"I send a fake POST to /api/telegram/webhook. It looks like a Telegram update.
OSIRIS processes it. I execute arbitrary bot commands. I send messages to all
users. I steal data."

WHY THE EXISTING FIX IS NOT ENOUGH
Both proposed verification routines are wrong — different wrong, both wrong —
and neither would ever accept a real Telegram request (DEF-001). Additionally
the `timingSafeEqual` calls crash on a length mismatch, giving a remote
unauthenticated DoS (DEF-007), and the IP allowlist cannot work behind
Cloudflare (DEF-056, DEF-025). So the endpoint that the Red Team correctly
identifies as high-value has: a verification function that rejects legitimate
traffic (which pressures a developer to remove it), a crash primitive, and an IP
check that rejects everything.

STRUCTURAL FIX
Four layers, ordered cheapest-first, each independently sufficient to stop the
basic attack:

  L1  Cloudflare WAF rule: only Telegram's published ranges may reach
      `/api/telegram/webhook`. Enforced at the edge where the true client IP is
      known. Costs nothing, uses no origin resources.
  L2  Secret token comparison, implemented correctly (DEF-001), constant-time
      and crash-proof (DEF-007). This is the actual authentication.
  L3  Replay defence: `update_id` deduplication in Redis, and rejection of
      messages whose `date` is more than 5 minutes old.
  L4  Authorization is not identity: even a perfectly authenticated Telegram
      update only reaches Trust Tier 0 and Tier 1 capabilities (ARGUMENT 9).
      Forging a webhook, if it were possible, would not authorize a withdrawal
      or a settings change.

L4 is the structural part. L1-L3 make forgery hard; L4 makes successful forgery
insufficient. That is the difference between a control and an architecture.

ARTIFACTS

```typescript
// src/app/api/telegram/webhook/route.ts
export const runtime = "nodejs";
export const dynamic = "force-dynamic";

export async function POST(req: Request): Promise<Response> {
  // L2 — authentication. First. Before body parsing, before logging, before
  // anything that costs work.
  if (!verifyTelegramWebhook(req.headers.get("x-telegram-bot-api-secret-token"))) {
    // Empty body, no detail. Do not confirm the endpoint exists or the shape of
    // the expected secret.
    await securityLog("TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_BAD_SECRET", {
      severity: "medium", ip: safeClientIp(req.headers),
    });
    return new Response(null, { status: 401 });
  }

  // Bound the body BEFORE parsing. A 50 MB JSON body is a memory DoS.
  const raw = await readBounded(req, 1024 * 64);
  if (raw === null) return new Response(null, { status: 413 });

  let update: unknown;
  try { update = parseUntrustedJson(raw); }        // DEF-026 reviver
  catch { return new Response(null, { status: 400 }); }

  const parsed = TelegramUpdateSchema.safeParse(update);   // Zod, .strict()
  if (!parsed.success) {
    await securityLog("TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SCHEMA_FAIL", { severity: "low" });
    // 200: never make Telegram retry a payload we will never accept.
    return new Response(null, { status: 200 });
  }
  const u = parsed.data;

  // L3 — replay. SET NX is atomic; a duplicate loses the race and returns 200.
  const fresh = await redis.set(`tg:update:${u.update_id}`, "1", "EX", 86400, "NX");
  if (fresh !== "OK") return new Response(null, { status: 200 });

  const messageDate = u.message?.date ?? u.callback_query?.message?.date;
  if (messageDate && Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) - messageDate > 300) {
    await securityLog("TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_STALE", { severity: "low" });
    return new Response(null, { status: 200 });
  }

  // L1 defence-in-depth signal only; never a rejection (DEF-056).
  const ip = safeClientIp(req.headers);
  if (ip && !inAnyCidr(ip, TELEGRAM_RANGES)) {
    await securityLog("TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_UNEXPECTED_SOURCE", { severity: "low", ip });
  }

  // Return 200 immediately; process asynchronously. Telegram retries on
  // non-200 and on timeout, and a slow handler becomes an amplifier.
  await boss.send("telegram:update", u, {
    singletonKey: `tg:${u.update_id}`, expireInSeconds: 60,
  });
  return new Response(null, { status: 200 });
}
```
```typescript
// Bounded body reader. Never call req.text() on an untrusted request.
async function readBounded(req: Request, max: number): Promise<string | null> {
  const reader = req.body?.getReader();
  if (!reader) return "";
  const chunks: Uint8Array[] = [];
  let total = 0;
  for (;;) {
    const { done, value } = await reader.read();
    if (done) break;
    total += value.byteLength;
    if (total > max) { await reader.cancel(); return null; }
    chunks.push(value);
  }
  return new TextDecoder().decode(Buffer.concat(chunks));
}
```

```bash
# handler contract, and on any suspicion.

curl -sS -X POST "https://api.telegram.org/bot${BOT_TOKEN}/setWebhook" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "$(jq -n --arg url "https://osiris.trade/api/telegram/webhook" \
              --arg secret "$SECRET" '{
        url: $url,
        secret_token: $secret,
        max_connections: 40,
        drop_pending_updates: true,
        allowed_updates: ["message","callback_query"]
      }')"
# allowed_updates is a real control: the bot never receives update types it does
# not handle, which removes whole categories of parser surface.
```

================================================================================
EP-5 — A RAW SQL QUERY SOMEWHERE
================================================================================

ATTACK
"Drizzle prevents basic SQLi, but I find a raw query. Or second-order: I put
malicious data in the DB and it gets used in a raw query later. Or time-based
blind injection in a search feature."

WHY THE EXISTING FIX IS NOT ENOUGH
"Zero raw queries" and "never use string concatenation" are instructions.
Drizzle's `sql` template tag IS parameterized and safe — but `sql.raw()` is
not, `sql.identifier()` is not automatically safe with dynamic input, and
`db.execute()` with a template built by string concatenation compiles fine and
looks almost identical to the safe form. The difference between:
```typescript
sql`SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ${userId}`        // safe: parameterized
sql.raw(`SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = '${userId}'`) // injectable
```
is four characters and a review that catches it. Meanwhile ADDENDUM L's own
retention job uses `sql.identifier(policy.table)` with values from a config
array — safe today only because the array is static, and one refactor away from
being dynamic (DEF-038).

STRUCTURAL FIX
Four mechanisms, again layered so that no single lapse is fatal:

  M1  LINT. `sql.raw`, `sql.identifier` with a non-literal, and `db.execute`
      outside the migration directory are compile-time errors.
  M2  CI GREP. A second, mechanism-independent check that does not depend on the
      TypeScript AST or on ESLint being configured correctly.
  M3  LEAST PRIVILEGE. Even a successful injection runs as `osiris_app`, which
      has no DDL, no `pg_read_server_files`, no superuser, no `COPY ... TO
      PROGRAM`, and no DELETE on the audit log. `DROP TABLE users` fails.
  M4  RLS. Even a successful `SELECT * FROM wallets` returns only the current
      user's rows, because the policy applies to every query on the connection
      including an injected one (EP-3 M3). This is the mechanism that turns a
      full database dump into a single-user disclosure.

M4 is the one worth emphasizing. RLS is usually discussed as an authorization
control. It is also the most effective SQL-injection blast-radius control
available, and it is free, and neither document mentions it.

ARTIFACTS


```typescript
const SORTABLE = {
  createdAt: trades.createdAt,
  amount:    trades.inputAmount,
  status:    trades.status,
} as const;

function orderBy(key: string) {

```
```
SECOND-ORDER INJECTION — the case the corpus raises and does not close.
The defence is not "sanitize on write." It is: data read from the database is
treated with exactly the same suspicion as data read from a request. Concretely:
  - Values from the DB are never concatenated into SQL. Ever. Same lint rules
    apply, because the lint rules are about the sink, not the source.
  - Values from the DB are never rendered as HTML. Same CSP and Trusted Types
    apply (EP-6).
  - Values from the DB that came from on-chain metadata go through the token
    label normalizer (CTL-603) on every render, not once on write. Normalizing
    on write means a bug in the normalizer is baked into stored rows forever;
    normalizing on read means fixing the normalizer fixes history.
```
```
DETECTION (M5, cheap and worth having):
  Enable pg_stat_statements. A weekly job snapshots the set of normalized query
  fingerprints. A fingerprint that has never been seen before is either a
  deploy or an injection. Correlate with deploy timestamps; alert on the
  uncorrelated ones. Low volume, high signal.
```

RESIDUAL
  - An injection inside `withSystemContext` (which bypasses RLS) is not bounded
    by M4. Hence the lint restriction of `withSystemContext` to `src/jobs/**`
    and the audit log entry on every use.
  - Recorded as RISK-008.

TESTS
  TEST-405  Assert `osiris_app` has `rolsuper=false`, `rolbypassrls=false`,
            `rolcreatedb=false`, `rolcreaterole=false`, and no DDL grants.
  TEST-406  A deliberately injectable test procedure is exercised with
            `' OR 1=1 --` and asserted to return only the current user's rows
            (proving M4 independently of M1/M2).
  TEST-407  `no-raw-sql.sh` exits non-zero when a `sql.raw` is added to a
            scratch file (proving M2 detects).

================================================================================
EP-6 — XSS IN THE TOKEN NAME DISPLAY
================================================================================

ATTACK
"I inject JavaScript into OSIRIS — through a trade note, a token name, or a URL
parameter. I steal the session cookie. I make requests as the user. I drain their
wallet. Or I show a fake UI that tricks them into signing a malicious
transaction."

WHY THE EXISTING FIX IS NOT ENOUGH
The Blue Team's answer is: React escapes by default, use DOMPurify if HTML is
needed, CSP, HttpOnly cookies, SRI. Correct as far as it goes, and it does not
go far enough for this specific input class.

  1. The CSP that actually ships contains `'unsafe-inline'` (DEF-018), so the
     CSP contributes nothing to XSS defence.
  2. React escapes text nodes. It does not protect `href`, `src`, `style`,
     `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, `ref` callbacks touching `innerHTML`, or any of
     the DOM sinks a charting library reaches for. React's default is a good
     default, not a boundary.
  3. HttpOnly cookies mean the attacker cannot *read* the session. They can
     still *use* it: every fetch from the page carries the cookie
     automatically. For a trading app, "make requests as the user" is the entire
     attack; reading the cookie is optional. Treating HttpOnly as an XSS
     mitigation understates the impact badly.
  4. Most importantly: token names are not merely "untrusted input." They are
     input authored by the adversary, on-chain, for free, at scale, and
     displayed to the user next to a Buy button. The interesting attack is not
     even script injection — it is *visual* spoofing, which no amount of HTML
     escaping addresses:
       - Right-to-left override (U+202E) reverses displayed text, so a name can
         render as something entirely different from its bytes.
       - Homoglyphs: Cyrillic "а" (U+0430) is visually identical to Latin "a".
         "Bоnk" with a Cyrillic о is a different token from "Bonk".
       - Zero-width characters split or join words invisibly.
       - Combining marks and long names break layout and can push real
         information (the mint address, the risk warning) off screen.
       - A name containing text like "Verified by OSIRIS" or a checkmark
         impersonates the interface itself.
     None of these are stopped by React escaping, DOMPurify, or CSP. All of them
     cost the attacker nothing and target the user's eyes rather than the
     browser's parser.

STRUCTURAL FIX
Four mechanisms:

  M1  TRUSTED TYPES. `require-trusted-types-for 'script'` in the CSP makes DOM
      XSS sinks throw rather than execute in Chromium. Assigning a raw string to
      `innerHTML`, `outerHTML`, `srcdoc`, `eval`, `setTimeout(string)`, or a
      `<script>.text` becomes a runtime TypeError. This is the strongest
      available structural answer to DOM XSS and it is a header plus a small
      policy shim.
  M2  STRICT NONCE CSP. `script-src 'self' 'nonce-…' 'strict-dynamic'` with no
      `unsafe-inline`. Made possible by the single-origin server-rendered
      decision (ARGUMENT 11).
  M3  LINT BAN on `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` and direct `innerHTML` assignment,
      with a single reviewed exception path that must go through a Trusted Types
      policy backed by DOMPurify.
  M4  A TOKEN LABEL NORMALIZER that every adversary-authored string passes
      through on render, addressing the visual attacks that the other three do
      not touch.

ARTIFACTS

```typescript
// src/middleware.ts — per-request nonce (M2)
import { NextResponse, type NextRequest } from "next/server";

export function middleware(req: NextRequest) {
  const nonce = Buffer.from(crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(16))).toString("base64");
  const csp = [
    "default-src 'none'",
    "base-uri 'none'",
    "object-src 'none'",
    "frame-ancestors 'none'",
    "form-action 'self'",
    `script-src 'self' 'nonce-${nonce}' 'strict-dynamic'`,
    `style-src 'self' 'nonce-${nonce}'`,
    "img-src 'self' data:",
    "font-src 'self'",
    "connect-src 'self'",
    "manifest-src 'self'",
    "worker-src 'self'",
    "media-src 'none'",
    "require-trusted-types-for 'script'",
    "trusted-types default dompurify#html",
    "upgrade-insecure-requests",
    "report-uri /api/csp-report",
  ].join("; ");

  const headers = new Headers(req.headers);
  headers.set("x-nonce", nonce);
  const res = NextResponse.next({ request: { headers } });
  res.headers.set("Content-Security-Policy", csp);
  return res;
}
export const config = { matcher: ["/((?!_next/static|_next/image|favicon.ico).*)"] };
```

```typescript
// src/app/trusted-types.ts — loaded before anything else (M1)
if (typeof window !== "undefined" && window.trustedTypes?.createPolicy) {
  // The DEFAULT policy is the safety net: any string that reaches a sink
  // without an explicit policy lands here. Throwing is correct — it converts a
  // silent DOM XSS into a visible crash in development and a blocked action in
  // production.
  window.trustedTypes.createPolicy("default", {
    createHTML: (s) => { throw new TypeError("untrusted HTML assignment blocked"); },
    createScript: () => { throw new TypeError("untrusted script blocked"); },
    createScriptURL: (u) => {
      const url = new URL(u, location.origin);
      if (url.origin !== location.origin) throw new TypeError("cross-origin script URL");
      return u;                             // same-origin chunk loading only
    },
  });

  // The ONE sanctioned way to render HTML, for the rare case it is needed.
  window.trustedTypes.createPolicy("dompurify#html", {
    createHTML: (s) => DOMPurify.sanitize(s, {
      USE_PROFILES: { html: true },
      FORBID_TAGS: ["style", "form", "input", "button", "iframe", "object", "embed"],
      FORBID_ATTR: ["style", "srcdoc", "formaction", "form", "ping"],
      ALLOWED_URI_REGEXP: /^(?:https?|mailto):/i,
    }),
  });
}
```

```typescript
// src/lib/token-label.ts — M4. The most important file in this entry point.
/**
 * Token names and symbols are authored by the adversary. This normalizer runs
 * ON EVERY RENDER (not once at write time), so that improving it improves the
 * display of every token ever stored, including ones already in the database.
 */

// Characters that change how text is DISPLAYED without being visible. These
// are the spoofing primitives; strip them unconditionally.
const INVISIBLE_OR_DIRECTIONAL = new RegExp(
  "[" +
  "\\u0000-\\u001F\\u007F-\\u009F" +   // C0 / C1 controls
  "\\u00AD" +                          // soft hyphen
  "\\u061C" +                          // Arabic letter mark
  "\\u180E" +                          // Mongolian vowel separator
  "\\u200B-\\u200F" +                  // ZWSP, ZWNJ, ZWJ, LRM, RLM
  "\\u202A-\\u202E" +                  // LRE RLE PDF LRO RLO  <- the RTL attack
  "\\u2060-\\u2064" +                  // word joiner, invisible operators
  "\\u2066-\\u2069" +                  // LRI RLI FSI PDI
  "\\uFE00-\\uFE0F" +                  // variation selectors
  "\\uFEFF" +                          // BOM / ZWNBSP
  "]", "gu"
);
// Tag characters (U+E0000-U+E007F) can carry an invisible payload.
const TAG_CHARS = /[\u{E0000}-\u{E007F}]/gu;
// Combining marks: allow a couple, strip runs (Zalgo breaks layout).
const EXCESS_COMBINING = /(\p{M}){3,}/gu;

const SCRIPT_TESTS: Array<[string, RegExp]> = [
  ["Latin",    /\p{Script=Latin}/u],
  ["Cyrillic", /\p{Script=Cyrillic}/u],
  ["Greek",    /\p{Script=Greek}/u],
  ["Han",      /\p{Script=Han}/u],
  ["Arabic",   /\p{Script=Arabic}/u],
  ["Hebrew",   /\p{Script=Hebrew}/u],
];

const IMPERSONATION = /\b(osiris|official|verified|admin|support|team)\b/i;

export interface TokenLabel {
  display: string;
  flags: {
    mixedScript: boolean;      // homoglyph risk
    hadInvisible: boolean;     // something was hiding in there
    impersonatesUi: boolean;   // claims to be us
    truncated: boolean;
    emptyAfterNormalize: boolean;
  };
  scripts: string[];
}

export function normalizeTokenLabel(raw: unknown, maxLen = 32): TokenLabel {
  const flags = {
    mixedScript: false, hadInvisible: false, impersonatesUi: false,
    truncated: false, emptyAfterNormalize: false,
  };
  if (typeof raw !== "string" || raw.length === 0)
    return { display: "(unnamed)", flags: { ...flags, emptyAfterNormalize: true }, scripts: [] };

  // 1. BOUND FIRST. Always before any regex or normalization. A 5 MB name must
  //    not become 5 MB of Unicode work per row per render.
  let s = raw.slice(0, 256);

  // 2. NFKC folds compatibility forms (fullwidth, ligatures) to canonical ones,
  //    which collapses a family of lookalikes.
  try { s = s.normalize("NFKC"); } catch { /* lone surrogates: keep as-is */ }

  // 3. Strip the invisible and directional primitives.
  const before = s;
  s = s.replace(INVISIBLE_OR_DIRECTIONAL, "").replace(TAG_CHARS, "");
  flags.hadInvisible = s !== before;

  // 4. Collapse Zalgo.
  s = s.replace(EXCESS_COMBINING, "$1");

  // 5. Collapse whitespace runs, including exotic spaces NFKC did not fold.
  s = s.replace(/\s+/gu, " ").trim();

  if (s.length === 0)
    return { display: "(unnamed)", flags: { ...flags, emptyAfterNormalize: true }, scripts: [] };

  // 6. Script mixing. Latin+Cyrillic in one token name is the homoglyph attack;
  //    it is essentially never legitimate for a ticker.
  const scripts = SCRIPT_TESTS.filter(([, re]) => re.test(s)).map(([n]) => n);
  flags.mixedScript = scripts.length > 1;

  // 7. Impersonation of the interface.
  flags.impersonatesUi = IMPERSONATION.test(s);

  // 8. Display clamp, with a real ellipsis (not three dots, which can be
  //    spoofed by the token itself).
  if ([...s].length > maxLen) {
    s = [...s].slice(0, maxLen).join("") + "…";
    flags.truncated = true;
  }
  return { display: s, flags, scripts };
}
```
```tsx
// src/components/TokenIdentity.tsx — the ONLY component that renders a token
// name. Lint-ban rendering token.name / token.symbol anywhere else.
export function TokenIdentity({ mint, name, symbol }: Props) {
  const n = normalizeTokenLabel(name, 28);
  const s = normalizeTokenLabel(symbol, 12);
  const risky = n.flags.mixedScript || n.flags.hadInvisible ||
                n.flags.impersonatesUi || s.flags.mixedScript;

  return (
    <span className="token-identity">
      {/* Text node. React escapes. No dangerouslySetInnerHTML, ever. */}
      <span className="token-symbol" dir="ltr" translate="no">{s.display}</span>
      <span className="token-name"   dir="ltr" translate="no">{n.display}</span>

      {/* The mint is the only non-spoofable identity. It is ALWAYS shown next
          to the name, never replaced by it, and never truncated in a
          confirmation dialog. */}
      <Identicon seed={mint} aria-hidden />
      <code className="token-mint" title={mint}>
        {mint.slice(0, 4)}…{mint.slice(-4)}
      </code>

      {risky && (
        <span className="token-warning" role="alert">
          Unusual characters in this token&apos;s name. Verify the mint address
          before trading.
        </span>
      )}
    </span>
  );
}
```
Notes on the component that are not incidental:
  - `dir="ltr"` on the containing element re-anchors direction so that any
    residual bidi content cannot escape the span and reorder surrounding UI.
  - The identicon is derived from the mint, so two visually identical names with
    different mints produce visibly different glyphs. This is the single most
    effective anti-homoglyph measure available and it costs nothing.
  - The trade confirmation dialog shows the FULL mint address, never truncated,
    and requires the user to confirm against it.

```typescript
// src/lib/safe-href.ts
const SAFE = /^(https?:|mailto:|\/(?!\/)|#)/i;
export function safeHref(u: unknown): string {
  if (typeof u !== "string") return "#";
  // Strip control chars first: "java\tscript:" survives a naive prefix check.
  const cleaned = u.replace(/[\u0000-\u001F\u007F\s]/g, "");
  return SAFE.test(cleaned) ? cleaned : "#";
}
```

```typescript
// Cookies (unchanged in intent, corrected in framing): HttpOnly stops READING

// connect-src 'self'), Trusted Types (no sink), and passkey re-auth for Trust
// Tier 2/3 actions, which an XSS cannot satisfy without the physical
```

================================================================================
EP-7 — NO RATE LIMITING
================================================================================

ATTACK
"I don't need to hack in. I flood the API. I open 10,000 WebSocket connections.
I upload massive files. I trigger expensive database queries. The free ARM VM
has limited CPU. I bring it to its knees. Users can't trade."

WHY THE EXISTING FIX IS NOT ENOUGH
The Blue Team proposed UFW limits, Caddy rate limiting, application-level Redis
limiting, sysctl tuning, PM2 memory restart, body size limits, and query
timeouts. Five problems:

  1. `ufw limit 443` behind Cloudflare rate-limits Cloudflare and takes the site
     down (DEF-009).
  2. Caddy's `rate_limit` is not a built-in directive; the Caddyfile will not
     parse and Caddy will not start (DEF-008).
  3. Every per-IP limit keys on Cloudflare's IP, so it is either useless or a
     global outage (DEF-025). This is the big one — it makes the entire
     application-layer tier incorrect, not merely incomplete.
  4. The limiter's behaviour when Redis is unavailable is unspecified, and the
     natural implementation fails open, which is a free bypass (ARGUMENT 8).
  5. Counting *requests* is the wrong unit. One `/api/token/analyze` request may
     cost twenty upstream RPC calls, a Jupiter quote, and a RugCheck lookup. A
     limit of 30 requests/minute permits 600 upstream calls/minute from one
     user, which exhausts a free RPC tier long before it exhausts the CPU. The
     scarce resources here are upstream quota and CPU, not request count.

STRUCTURAL FIX — five tiers, each with a different failure mode

  T1  CLOUDFLARE EDGE. Attack traffic never reaches Oracle. Free plan gives one
      rate-limiting rule (IP-based, fixed 10-second window) — spend it on the
      highest-value target — plus Bot Fight Mode, managed challenges, and
      Under Attack mode. Cost: nothing. Fails: only if Cloudflare fails.
  T2  ORIGIN INGRESS. Caddy (built with caddy-ratelimit) limits by resolved
      client IP. Protects against anything that gets past T1 and against
      traffic from a compromised or misbehaving path.
  T3  APPLICATION IDENTITY. Redis sliding window keyed by user, session, and
      endpoint class — the dimensions that matter once a request is
      authenticated. Fail-closed for auth/trade/signer, fail-open for reads.
  T4  COST ACCOUNTING. A token bucket denominated in *work units*, not requests.
      Every upstream call, signer call, and expensive query debits the caller's
      bucket. This is the tier that actually protects the free RPC quota and the
      CPU.
  T5  SIGNER-SIDE. The remote signer enforces its own per-wallet, per-user, and
      global limits in Cloudflare storage. Not bypassable by compromising the
      app host, not dependent on Redis, and it is the limit that bounds
      financial loss rather than availability.

The tiers deliberately have disjoint failure modes: Cloudflare outage does not
disable T2-T5; Redis outage does not disable T1, T2, or T5; app-host compromise
does not disable T1 or T5.

ARTIFACTS

```
T1 — CLOUDFLARE (dashboard)
  Rate limiting rule (the one free rule — spend it where a bypass costs most):
    If:      http.request.uri.path contains "/api/auth/"
    Then:    Block for 10 seconds
    Counting: IP, 10 requests / 10 seconds
  WAF custom rules (free plan allows several; these are not rate limits and do
  not consume the rate-limiting rule):
    - Block  /api/telegram/webhook from outside Telegram ranges       (EP-4 L1)
    - Managed Challenge  /api/auth/*  when cf.threat_score > 20
    - Block  requests with an empty or bot-like User-Agent to /api/*
    - Block  method not in {GET, POST, HEAD, OPTIONS}
  Settings:
    - Bot Fight Mode: ON
    - Security Level: Medium (raise to "I'm Under Attack" during an incident)
    - Always Use HTTPS: ON;  Min TLS 1.2 (prefer 1.3)
    - Browser Integrity Check: ON
```

```typescript
// T3 — src/server/rate-limit.ts
export type LimiterPolicy = "fail_closed" | "fail_open";

interface LimitSpec {
  bucket: string;
  limit: number;
  windowSeconds: number;
  policy: LimiterPolicy;      // REQUIRED. No default. The call site must decide.
  key: (ctx: Ctx) => string;
}

/** Sliding window with a Lua script so check-and-increment is atomic. A
 *  read-then-write limiter is bypassable by concurrency, which is exactly what
 *  an attacker sends. */
const SCRIPT = `
local key   = KEYS[1]
local now   = tonumber(ARGV[1])
local win   = tonumber(ARGV[2])
local limit = tonumber(ARGV[3])
redis.call('ZREMRANGEBYSCORE', key, 0, now - win)
local count = redis.call('ZCARD', key)
if count >= limit then
  return {0, count}
end
redis.call('ZADD', key, now, ARGV[4])
redis.call('EXPIRE', key, math.ceil(win / 1000) + 1)
return {1, count + 1}
`;

export async function consume(spec: LimitSpec, ctx: Ctx): Promise<void> {
  const key = `rl:${spec.bucket}:${spec.key(ctx)}`;
  try {
    const [allowed] = (await redis.eval(
      SCRIPT, 1, key, Date.now(), spec.windowSeconds * 1000, spec.limit, randomUUID()
    )) as [number, number];
    if (!allowed) throw new RateLimitError(spec.bucket);
  } catch (err) {
    if (err instanceof RateLimitError) throw err;
    // Limiter is broken (Redis down, script error, timeout).
    await securityLog("RATE_LIMITER_UNAVAILABLE", { severity: "high", bucket: spec.bucket });
    if (spec.policy === "fail_closed") {
      throw new ServiceUnavailableError("rate limiter unavailable");
    }
    // fail_open: allow, but this is now a paging condition if it persists.
    metrics.increment("rate_limiter_fail_open", { bucket: spec.bucket });
  }
}

export const LIMITS = {
  authAttempt:   { bucket:"auth",     limit:5,   windowSeconds:900,  policy:"fail_closed", key:(c)=>c.clientIp },
  authPerUser:   { bucket:"authu",    limit:10,  windowSeconds:3600, policy:"fail_closed", key:(c)=>c.emailHash },
  passwordReset: { bucket:"pwreset",  limit:3,   windowSeconds:86400,policy:"fail_closed", key:(c)=>c.emailHash },
  tradeSubmit:   { bucket:"trade",    limit:30,  windowSeconds:60,   policy:"fail_closed", key:(c)=>c.userId },
  signerRequest: { bucket:"sign",     limit:20,  windowSeconds:60,   policy:"fail_closed", key:(c)=>c.walletId },
  sessionCreate: { bucket:"sess",     limit:10,  windowSeconds:3600, policy:"fail_closed", key:(c)=>c.userId },
  withdrawal:    { bucket:"wd",       limit:3,   windowSeconds:86400,policy:"fail_closed", key:(c)=>c.userId },
  priceRead:     { bucket:"price",    limit:600, windowSeconds:60,   policy:"fail_open",   key:(c)=>c.userId },
  publicRead:    { bucket:"pub",      limit:120, windowSeconds:60,   policy:"fail_open",   key:(c)=>c.clientIp },
} as const satisfies Record<string, LimitSpec>;
```
```typescript
// T4 — cost accounting. src/server/cost-budget.ts
/**
 * Requests are not the scarce resource. Upstream quota and CPU are. Every
 * expensive operation debits the caller's budget; a request that would exceed
 * the remaining budget is refused before it starts, not after it has already
 * consumed the quota.
 */
export const COST = {
  jupiterQuote:      3,
  heliusGetTx:       2,
  heliusGetAccount:  1,
  rugcheckLookup:    5,
  dexscreenerPair:   2,
  signerRequest:    10,
  fullTokenAnalyze: 25,   // fans out to several of the above
} as const;

const BUDGET_PER_MINUTE = { free: 60, basic: 200, pro: 600, whale: 2000 };

export async function debit(userId: string, tier: Tier, units: number): Promise<void> {
  const key = `cost:${userId}:${Math.floor(Date.now() / 60000)}`;
  const used = await redis.incrby(key, units);
  if (used === units) await redis.expire(key, 120);
  if (used > BUDGET_PER_MINUTE[tier]) {
    throw new RateLimitError("cost_budget_exceeded");
  }
}
```

RESIDUAL
  - A distributed attack from many IPs with valid sessions is bounded by T3/T4
    per-identity limits, and by account creation limits, but a determined
    attacker with many accounts can still consume quota. Account creation is
    therefore itself rate-limited and challenged (T1).
  - Cloudflare's free plan gives one rate-limiting rule with a fixed 10-second
    window; that is genuinely limited. If sustained L7 attack becomes a real
    problem, Cloudflare Pro is the honest answer and it costs money (PART 9).
  - Recorded as RISK-010.
