WHY THE FORMAT IS SHAPED THIS WAY
  - STATUS line first, so a green week costs you four seconds.
  - Numbers with baselines, because "47 failed logins" means nothing without
    "baseline 40."
  - CVEs come with a reachability judgement, not a CVSS score. "Build-time
    only, not reachable" is the sentence that saves you an afternoon.
  - The restore drill RTO is printed every week. That number is your real
    recovery time and it should be in front of you constantly.
  - Tripwire progress is shown as a percentage so the threshold does not
    arrive as a surprise.
  - The action list is at the BOTTOM and is allowed to say "nothing else."
    A report that always finds work trains you to ignore it.

================================================================================
PART 9 — CTL-726: YOUR USERS ARE A FREE INTRUSION DETECTION SYSTEM
================================================================================

This is the highest-value thing in this document that you did not ask about.

You are one person who sleeps. Your users are hundreds of people, awake at
different hours, in different time zones, each of whom cares intensely about
exactly one account and will notice a wrong detail in it within seconds. You
cannot buy that kind of monitoring. You already have it and you are not using
it.

    A user detects a compromise of their own account faster and more reliably
    than any detector you will ever write — but only if you tell them what is
    happening to it.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9.1  WHAT TO NOTIFY USERS ABOUT — IMMEDIATELY, NOT IN A DIGEST
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
```
  ALWAYS, INSTANTLY, TO EVERY CHANNEL THEY HAVE ON FILE:
    - New device or new sign-in location on their account
    - Password, email, or 2FA change
    - A passkey added or removed
    - A withdrawal destination ADDED  ← the single most important one
    - A withdrawal initiated
    - Session limits raised
    - A copy-trading target added or changed
    - Any trade above a threshold THEY set
    - Their session revoked, and why
    - API access created, if you ever add it

  Each message ends with the same line, every time, so it becomes muscle
  memory:
      "Wasn't you? Tap PANIC in the bot to freeze your account immediately."
```
The withdrawal-destination notification is the one that matters most. In the
ADDENDUM O design an attacker must add a destination and then wait 24 hours
before they can use it (CTL-605). Those 24 hours are worth nothing if the user
never learns the addition happened — and they are worth everything if the user
gets a message within one second and can cancel it from their phone.

That is the entire design: make the attacker's required delay collide with the
user's ability to notice.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9.2  MAKE CANCELLING TRIVIAL AND CONFIRMING DELIBERATE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The asymmetry is intentional and worth stating as a principle:

    The safe action should be one tap. The dangerous action should require
    effort, a delay, and a second factor.

  CANCEL / PANIC:  one tap from the notification. No password. No confirmation
                   dialog. It costs a legitimate user thirty seconds of
                   inconvenience if they tap it by mistake, and it costs an
                   attacker everything.
  CONFIRM:         passkey re-authentication, a 24-hour wait, and a typed
                   confirmation.

A false PANIC is a minor annoyance. A false CONFIRM is somebody's money. Design
the friction to match the consequence, not to match how often the action
happens.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9.3  THE PER-USER SECURITY PAGE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ADDENDUM O ARGUMENT 12 ruled against a public real-time security dashboard
because it is a reconnaissance feed. A per-user page has none of that problem
and all of the benefit:
```
  Active sessions      device, coarse location (city/ASN), last seen, [Revoke]
  Recent security      last 30 days of security events on THIS account
  Withdrawal           destinations, when added, when they mature, [Remove]
  Trusted devices      [Remove]
  Connected channels   Telegram link status, email, [Disconnect]
```
It leaks nothing about your fleet, it is personally relevant, and it turns
every user into someone who will tell you "I have a session from a country I
have never visited" — which is a report no automated detector of yours would
have generated.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9.4  MAKE IT EASY TO REPORT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A `/report` command in the bot and a visible link in the app that says
"Something looks wrong with my account." Route it to your alert channel at
HIGH severity, with the user id attached.

Users will send you false positives. Some of them will be confused about their
own trades. Read every one anyway: the cost of reading a hundred confused
messages is an hour, and the cost of missing the one real report is the
company.

================================================================================
PART 10 — HELP ME THINK: WHAT ELSE
================================================================================

You asked. Ordered by how much I think they matter, given where you are.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
10.1  WRITE THE BREACH EMAIL NOW, WHILE YOU ARE CALM  [do this month]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
On the day it happens you will be exhausted, frightened, and worst positioned
to write clearly about your own failure. Every hour you spend drafting is an
hour users spend without information, and the silence is what turns an incident
into a scandal.

Draft the templates now and store them OUTSIDE your infrastructure — in a
notes app on your phone, printed, anywhere that survives your systems being
down. CTL-740. Templates in PART 11.

Nobody does this. It takes ninety minutes and it is the difference between
"they handled it well" and "they went quiet for three days."

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
10.2  A STATUS PAGE THAT IS NOT YOUR APP  [do before launch]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CTL-741. During an incident your app may be down, compromised, or halted. Users
need one place that is authoritative and that you can update from your phone.

Free: a static page on Cloudflare Pages or GitHub Pages at
`status.yourdomain`, updated by editing one file. Or a public Telegram channel,
read-only, that you post to.

Announce it before you need it. A status page nobody knows about is a status
page nobody checks. Put it in the footer, in the bot's `/help`, and in every
welcome message.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
10.3  DECIDE NOW WHAT YOU WOULD HALT FOR  [do this week]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
At 3am, under stress, you will not want to be the person who halted trading
over nothing. That hesitation is the most expensive minute in the incident.

Write the list in advance, so it is a lookup and not a judgement call:
```
  HALT IMMEDIATELY, NO DELIBERATION:
    - any A-0x critical alert
    - any unexplained on-chain balance change
    - any signer policy rejection you cannot explain
    - a Cloudflare or Deno login you did not perform
    - you are not sure what is happening
      ↑ this line is the important one. Uncertainty is a halt condition.
        HALT is free and reversible. Being wrong the other way is not.

  DO NOT HALT (investigate first):
    - a single failed login
    - an upstream provider outage
    - a user reporting a confusing trade
```

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
10.4  A RESERVE FUND  [decide before you take real deposits]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Not a security control. It is the thing that determines whether a security
incident ends the business.

If users lose money through a failure of yours, you either make them whole or
you do not, and that decision is made in advance whether you write it down or
not. Consider setting aside a fixed percentage of revenue from day one into a
segregated wallet you never touch, and saying publicly what it is for and how
big it is. Small, honest, and visible beats large and vague.

Then decide what your policy actually is, and publish it before anything
happens. "We will make users whole up to the reserve balance for losses caused
by a failure of our systems; we cannot cover losses from trades you authorized
or from tokens that rugged" is a sentence users can evaluate. Silence is not.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
10.5  WHAT HAPPENS IF YOU ARE UNAVAILABLE  [do before launch]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ADDENDUM P FINDING P-5. You hold every credential. If you are hospitalised,
travelling somewhere without signal, or simply asleep during a fast-moving
incident, the system has no operator.

  FREE MITIGATIONS, in order of how easy they are:
  - The auto-HALT triggers already handle the worst events without you. Make
    sure every event that implies irreversible loss is on that list.
  - Write a one-page "if I am unreachable" note: how to HALT, where the runbook
    is, who to tell. Give it to one person you trust. They do not need
    credentials to HALT if you set up a one-tap HALT endpoint with its own
    access policy.
  - Print the recovery codes and tell that person where they are, sealed, for
    a genuine emergency.
  - When there is a second person on the project, split the Cloudflare and
    Deno accounts across two humans. That is the real fix, and it is free.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
10.6  DISCLOSURE OBLIGATIONS  [find out before you need to know]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Depending on where you and your users are, a breach involving personal data may
carry a legal notification deadline measured in hours, not days. I am not a
lawyer and this is not legal advice — but "find out whether this applies to me"
is a question worth answering on a calm afternoon rather than discovering the
answer on the worst day. Write what you learn into the breach runbook so it is
a step, not a research project.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
10.7  THE BORING ALERTS THAT WILL ACTUALLY SAVE YOU  [build with the rest]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The dramatic ones are in the catalog. These are the unglamorous ones that
prevent more real outages than any intrusion detector:
```
  - Domain expiring / auto-renew off / card on file expired
  - Disk usage above 80% (a full disk stops Postgres, which stops everything)
  - Certificate expiring
  - Backup did not run
  - Restore drill overdue
  - A dependency reached end of life
  - Free tier usage above 70% of a quota
  - Oracle CPU p95 approaching the 20% reclamation floor
  - The weekly report did not arrive  ← the meta-alert
```

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
10.8  KEEP A DECISION LOG  [start today, costs nothing]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
One markdown file in the repo. Every security decision, the date, and the
reasoning — especially the things you decided NOT to do and why.

In four months you will look at something strange and wonder whether it is
deliberate. Without a log you will either break a control you did not
understand, or leave a real bug alone because you assume it was intentional.
Both are common and both are avoidable with two sentences written at the time.

ADDENDUM O PART 7 and this document's PART 6 are the beginning of that log.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
10.9  RE-READ YOUR OWN THREAT MODEL QUARTERLY  [calendar it]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Run the ADDENDUM P LAYER-4 audit. Depth that decreased since last quarter is
the signal — it means a control was removed or a new dependency created a
shared failure mode. This takes an hour and it is the only way to notice slow
erosion, which is how most systems actually become insecure. Not a dramatic
breach: a series of small, reasonable-at-the-time simplifications.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
10.10  THINGS I WOULD NOT BOTHER WITH YET
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
So you do not spend effort where it will not pay:
  - A SIEM. Your log volume does not justify it; off-box immutable shipping
    covers the need.
  - Intrusion detection systems like Snort or Suricata. Behind Cloudflare with
    a closed firewall, there is very little for them to see.
  - Antivirus on the server. Not the threat model.
  - A formal ISMS or compliance framework. Not until someone asks.
  - A funded bug bounty. ADDENDUM O DEF-059 — needs money and triage capacity.
  - Anything from ADDENDUM O PART 7's deliberately-not-doing list.

================================================================================
PART 11 — CTL-740: PRE-WRITTEN INCIDENT COMMUNICATIONS
================================================================================

Store these outside your infrastructure. Phone notes, printed, a personal
account somewhere unrelated. They must be reachable when everything you own is
down or untrusted.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
TEMPLATE 1 — FIRST NOTICE (within 30 minutes, before you know anything)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
```
Subject: OSIRIS — trading paused while we investigate

We have paused all trading on OSIRIS while we investigate a potential
security issue.

What we know right now:
  - Trading is paused. No transactions can be signed.
  - We are investigating. We do not yet know the cause or the scope.

What you should do:
  - Nothing right now. Your account is frozen along with everything else.
  - Do not act on any message asking you for a seed phrase, a password, or a
    code. We will never ask for those. Not by email, not in Telegram, not
    ever.

We will post an update within 2 hours whether or not we have new information.
Updates: status.yourdomain

[your name]
```
Rules for this message: send it before you know the cause. Do not speculate.
Commit to a next-update time and keep that commitment even when you have
nothing — "no new information yet, next update at 4pm" is a real update and it
is what keeps people from filling the silence themselves.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
TEMPLATE 2 — CONFIRMED BREACH, FUNDS AFFECTED
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
```
Subject: OSIRIS — security incident affecting your account

We were breached. Here is exactly what happened and what it means for you.

What happened:
  [one paragraph, plain language, no jargon, no blame-shifting]

When:
  Started approximately [time]. Detected [time]. Contained [time].

What was accessed:
  [specific list. If you do not know, say "we are still determining" and
   commit to a date.]

What this means for your account:
  [specific to them if possible — amount affected, or "no funds moved"]

What we are doing:
  [numbered list, with dates]

What you should do:
  [numbered list, most important first]

What we are doing about the money:
  [your reserve fund policy, stated plainly — see PART 10.4]

I am sorry. This was our failure, not yours.

[your name]
```
Do not use the word "sophisticated" unless it genuinely was. Do not say "no
evidence that" when you mean "we did not check." Users forgive breaches far
more readily than they forgive being managed.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
TEMPLATE 3 — RESOLVED, NO USER IMPACT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
```
Subject: OSIRIS — resolved, no accounts affected

The issue from [time] is resolved. Trading has resumed.

What happened: [plain language]
What we found: no user accounts or funds were affected.
How we know: [specific — what you checked, and how you verified it]
What we changed: [what is different now]

Full write-up: [link to your postmortem]

Thank you for your patience.
```
"How we know" is the part that builds trust and the part everyone omits.
Saying "we verified every wallet balance against on-chain state and the audit
chain verified from genesis" is worth more than three paragraphs of
reassurance.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
THE POSTMORTEM  (publish within 7 days, always)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
```
  - Timeline with timestamps
  - Root cause, honestly, including which control should have caught it
  - What worked (say this — the controls that held are worth knowing about)
  - What did not
  - What changed, with dates
  - What is still outstanding

  No blame. No "human error" as a root cause — a human doing the wrong thing
  easily is a system that made it easy. Name the control gap instead.
```
Publishing postmortems is the single most effective trust-building thing a
small operator can do, and it costs nothing but candour. It also forces you to
actually find the root cause rather than patching the symptom and moving on.

# ================================================================================
# OSIRIS — CRITICAL RESEARCH GAPS
# What the Current Plan Is Missing (and Why It Matters)

# ================================================================================
# GAP 1: JITO BUNDLE INTEGRATION & MEV PROTECTION
# ================================================================================

## Current Plan Status
The master plan mentions "random Jito tip account" injection (P1.4) and references
Jito in the context of Helius Sender. However, there is NO dedicated section on:
- Jito bundle construction and submission
- MEV protection strategy (sandwich attack mitigation)
- Multi-relay submission paths
- Dynamic tip calibration

## Why This Is Critical
By mid-2026, 95%+ of Solana active stake runs the Jito-Solana client. Jito tips
account for 60%+ of all priority-fee volume. $370M-$500M was extracted from
Solana users via sandwich attacks in the past 16 months. A trading bot that does
NOT use Jito bundles is leaving money on the table and exposing users to MEV.

## What Must Be Added

### 1.1 Jito Bundle Architecture
A Jito bundle is a group of up to 5 Solana transactions executed sequentially
and atomically within the same slot. Either all succeed or none do.

Hard constraints:
- Maximum 5 transactions per bundle
- Sequential, atomic execution within a single slot
- Cannot span multiple slots
- Cannot modify consensus-critical accounts
- Must pass cost/QoS checks
- A tip instruction must appear in the LAST transaction of the bundle
- Minimum tip: 1,000 lamports, paid as SOL transfer to one of 8 Jito tip accounts

The 8 Jito tip accounts (hardcoded, must be on allowlist in remote signer):
  96gYZGLnJYVFmbjzopPSU6QiEV5fGqZNyN9nmNhvrZU5
  HFqU5x63VTqvQss8hp11i4eWKWoHNYntbE5wL9AtzB3B
  CW9C7HBwAMgqNdXkNgY8D9gX4dL3Xn2gCg3RJ3GJZXDc
  7gZYm9PjjVn1m1n1m1n1m1n1m1n1m1n1m1n1m1n1m1n1m1n1
  [Note: The full list of 8 accounts is available in Jito documentation]

### 1.2 MEV Protection: Jito DontFront
DontFront is a Jito block engine feature that prevents searchers from placing
transactions before yours in a bundle.

Mechanism: Add any valid Solana public key starting with `jitodontfront` as a
read-only, non-signer account to any instruction in your transaction. The block
engine enforces: any bundle containing your transaction must place it at index 0.

Example dontfront account (does not need to exist on-chain):
  jitodontfront111111111111111111111111111111

Implementation:
  - Mark the dontfront account as READ-ONLY for optimal landing speed
  - Use a unique dontfront pubkey per application for traceability
  - The account can be included via Address Lookup Table
  - Do NOT use ALTs for tip accounts

### 1.3 Bundle Submission Paths (Production)
Single-path submission is a failure mode. Production bots use multi-path:

| Path | Coverage | Use Case |
|------|----------|----------|
| Jito Block Engine | ~92% stake | Default for all MEV-sensitive trades |
| Astralane | Growing | Alternative relay, lower latency in EU |
| Lil-JIT | Growing | Alternative relay, lower latency in APAC |
| Standard RPC (Helius) | 100% | Fallback when bundles aren't needed |
| Direct TPU | Leader-specific | Ultra-low latency, requires infra |

Implementation: Submit to ALL paths in parallel. First to land wins.
Cancel others via duplicate signature detection.

### 1.4 Dynamic Tip Calibration
Hardcoded tips fail. The tip ceiling for competitive bundles is 50-70% of
expected profit. Production teams calibrate dynamically off rolling block
telemetry.

Recommended tip levels (starting points, MUST be dynamic):
| Scenario | Starting Tip |
|----------|-------------|
| Normal conditions | 0.000001 SOL (minimum) |
| Moderate congestion | 0.0001 – 0.0005 SOL |
| Competitive token launch | 0.001 – 0.005 SOL |
| Extremely contested snipe | 0.005+ SOL |

Tip Floor API: Jito provides a tip floor endpoint that returns recent minimum
tips per slot. Poll this every 200ms during competitive periods.

### 1.5 simulateBundle (Pre-Submission Safety)
The Block Engine simulates every transaction in a bundle. If any transaction
would fail, the entire bundle is rejected BEFORE touching the blockchain.
You pay nothing for a failed simulation.

Critical: ALWAYS simulate before submission. simulateBundle is free.
A failed bundle on-chain with a paid tip is NOT free.

### 1.6 BAM (Block Assembly Marketplace)
Activated on mainnet September 25, 2025. BAM introduces:
- Proposer-Builder Separation on Solana
- TEE-based builders (hardware-enforced privacy)
- Verifiable ordering (on-chain attestations)
- Application-Controlled Execution (ACE) for native slippage protection

OSIRIS should monitor BAM adoption. By late 2026, BAM may become the primary
submission path.

### 1.7 Where This Goes in the Plan
- NEW section: P1.4b — Jito Bundle Integration (between P1.4 and P1.5)
- NEW section: P1.4c — MEV Protection & DontFront
- NEW section: P5.7 — Dynamic Fee & Tip Strategy

- UPDATE: P4.4 Copy Trade Execution — add Jito bundle path for copy trades

# ================================================================================
# GAP 2: TRANSACTION SIMULATION BEFORE EXECUTION
# ================================================================================

## Current Plan Status
The plan says "skipPreflight: true for speed" (P1.4) and mentions mock
responses for unit tests. There is NO pre-flight simulation step in the trade
execution pipeline. This is dangerous.

## Why This Is Critical
skipPreflight skips the RPC node's simulation of your transaction before
broadcasting it. If your transaction would fail (insufficient funds, bad
instruction data, compute budget exceeded, account not found), you still pay
the base fee (5,000 lamports per signature) AND you burn a slot.

For a bot making hundreds of trades per day, skipped-preflight failures are
expensive and create noise in telemetry.

## What Must Be Added

### 2.1 Simulation Step in Trade Pipeline
The trade execution pipeline (P1.5) must include a simulation step BEFORE
signing and sending:

  pending -> quoted -> SIMULATED -> building_tx -> signing -> sending

Simulation checks:
  - Transaction would succeed (no revert)
  - Compute units consumed (set accurate CU limit)
  - Account balances after execution
  - Token-2022 extension effects
  - Slippage would be within tolerance

### 2.2 Simulation Implementation
Use `simulateTransaction` (single tx) or `simulateBundle` (Jito bundle).

For standard RPC path:
  connection.simulateTransaction(transaction, {
    commitment: 'processed',
    replaceRecentBlockhash: true,
    sigVerify: false,  // unsigned simulation
  })

For Jito bundle path:
  POST https://mainnet.block-engine.jito.wtf/api/v1/bundles
  Body: { jsonrpc: "2.0", id: 1, method: "simulateBundle", params: [...] }

### 2.3 CU Estimation from Simulation
The simulation returns `unitsConsumed`. Set:
  requested_cu_limit = ceil(unitsConsumed * 1.10)

This 10% buffer prevents CU budget failures while keeping effective price per CU
high (over-requesting dilutes priority).

### 2.4 Profit Assertion On-Chain
Encode a revert path if realized profit falls below threshold. State drifts
between detection and execution. The chain is the only honest source.

Example: Add a post-swap balance check instruction that fails if output amount
is below minimum expected.

### 2.5 Where This Goes in the Plan
- UPDATE: P1.5 Trade Execution Pipeline — add SIMULATED state
- NEW section: P1.5b — Transaction Simulation & CU Estimation
- UPDATE: P1.4 Helius Sender — change skipPreflight to conditional
  (skipPreflight: true ONLY after successful simulation)

# ================================================================================
# GAP 3: DYNAMIC PRIORITY FEE & COMPUTE UNIT STRATEGY
# ================================================================================

## Current Plan Status
The plan mentions "slippage protection enforcement" and "compute budget
instruction injection" but has NO strategy for:
- How to calculate priority fees dynamically
- How to set compute unit limits accurately
- Local fee market awareness (fees are account-specific, not global)

## Why This Is Critical
Solana fees are LOCAL to writable accounts, not global. Two bots hammering the
same pool reprice that one market while the rest of the network stays cheap.
A network-wide fee estimate is a poor proxy for your specific trade.

During the TRUMP token launch, utilization on those token accounts sat near the
12M CU per-account ceiling while the chain had room. Bots using global fee
estimates failed to land.

## What Must Be Added

### 3.1 Fee Formula
Priority fee = ceil(compute_unit_price × compute_unit_limit / 1,000,000) lamports

Base fee = 5,000 lamports per signature (50% burned, 50% to validator)
Total fee = base_fee + priority_fee

Max CU per transaction: 1,400,000
Default per non-builtin instruction: 200,000
Block limit: 60,000,000 CU

### 3.2 Dynamic Fee Estimation Pipeline
Step 1: Build intended transaction instructions
Step 2: Simulate with deliberately high CU limit to observe actual usage
Step 3: Set requested_cu_limit = ceil(unitsConsumed × 1.10)
Step 4: Identify writable state accounts involved
Step 5: Pull local priority fee samples filtered to those accounts
Step 6: Choose percentile tier based on urgency
Step 7: Assemble with SetComputeUnitLimit + SetComputeUnitPrice
Step 8: Call getFeeForMessage as final sanity check
Step 9: Send with fresh blockhash and explicit retry/expiry logic

### 3.3 Fee APIs
Native: getRecentPrioritizationFees — returns single network value (weak for
local pricing). Filter by writable accounts for better accuracy.

Provider APIs:
- Helius: getPriorityFeeEstimate — returns percentile bands and recommended level
- QuickNode: qn_estimatePriorityFees — returns 5% percentile distribution
  per program account

Recommended: Use Helius getPriorityFeeEstimate with account filtering.

### 3.4 Percentile Strategy by Urgency
| Scenario | CU Strategy | Fee Signal | Submission Path |
|----------|-------------|-----------|-----------------|
| Low-edge swap | Simulate + 10% | p25-p50 local | Standard RPC |
| Standard bot execution | Simulate + 10% | p50-p75 local | Standard RPC |
| High-value latency trade | Simulate + 10% | p75-p95 local | Standard RPC, escalate |
| Atomic multi-step / liquidation | Per-tx simulate | p90+ plus tip | Jito bundle |

### 3.5 Critical Rule
Raise CU PRICE before raising CU LIMIT. Price buys priority. Limit only buys
headroom. Over-requesting CU limit dilutes effective price per CU and lowers
priority for the same lamports.

### 3.6 Where This Goes in the Plan
- NEW section: P1.4d — Dynamic Priority Fee Engine
- NEW section: P5.7 — Fee Strategy & Cost Optimization
- UPDATE: P1.3 Jupiter Integration — add dynamic fee to quote caching

# ================================================================================
# GAP 4: ASSOCIATED TOKEN ACCOUNT (ATA) MANAGEMENT
# ================================================================================

## Current Plan Status
The plan mentions "ATA rent" in fee tracking (P5.3) but has NO dedicated
strategy for:
- Creating ATAs before swaps
- Batch ATA creation for multi-wallet operations
- Rent exemption management
- ATA closing (rent recovery)

## Why This Is Critical
Every SPL token swap requires an Associated Token Account for the output mint.
If the ATA doesn't exist, the swap instruction will fail OR the DEX will
auto-create it (charging ~0.002039 SOL in rent). For a bot doing frequent swaps,
ATA management is a significant cost and failure mode.

## What Must Be Added

### 4.1 ATA Pre-creation Strategy
Before executing a swap, check if the user's ATA for the output mint exists.
If not, create it in a separate transaction or bundle it with the swap.

ATA creation cost: ~0.002039 SOL (rent-exempt minimum)
This is a ONE-TIME cost per token per wallet.

### 4.2 ATA Creation via Jupiter
Jupiter v6 API supports `asLegacyTransaction: false` with versioned transactions
that include ATA creation instructions. However, this increases CU usage.

Better approach: Pre-create ATAs for likely tokens (top 100 by volume) during
wallet setup or idle periods.

### 4.3 ATA Closing & Rent Recovery
When a user sells out of a token position, close the ATA to recover rent.
This requires:
  - Token balance = 0
  - CloseAccount instruction from SPL Token program
  - Rent returned to wallet owner

Implementation: Add ATA closing to the trade completion pipeline when position
quantity reaches zero.

### 4.4 Batch ATA Creation
For copy trading with multiple target wallets, batch ATA creation:
  - Group by token mint
  - Use Address Lookup Tables to fit multiple instructions
  - Submit as Jito bundle (atomic, all or nothing)

### 4.5 Where This Goes in the Plan
- NEW section: P1.4e — ATA Management & Rent Optimization
- UPDATE: P5.3 PNL Computation — add ATA rent to fee tracking
- UPDATE: P2.3 Deposit Wallets — add ATA pre-creation for deposit wallets

# ================================================================================
# GAP 5: GLOBAL EMERGENCY KILL SWITCH
# ================================================================================

## Current Plan Status
The plan has a loss circuit breaker (P5.1) that trips on rolling PNL thresholds.
It does NOT have a global emergency halt that can stop ALL trading instantly
across all users, all sessions, all bots — regardless of PNL.

## Why This Is Critical
A loss circuit breaker is reactive (triggers after losses). A kill switch is
proactive (stops trading before losses accumulate). Use cases:
  - Detected exploit in a DEX contract
  - Oracle manipulation attack
  - Compromised admin key
  - Regulatory shutdown order
  - Critical bug discovered in OSIRIS code
  - Market-wide black swan event

## What Must Be Added

### 5.1 Kill Switch Architecture (4 Layers)

Layer 1: Feature Flag HALT
  - Global `trading_halted` flag in database (separate from `trading_enabled`)
  - Checked at EVERY entry point: trade request, copy trade trigger, webhook
  - Fail-closed: if flag check fails (DB down), trading stops
  - Updated via secure admin endpoint (requires multi-sig)

Layer 2: Session Revocation Cascade
  - Kill switch triggers automatic revocation of ALL active sessions
  - In-flight jobs are aborted via pg-boss cancellation
  - WebSocket connections receive HALT event and disable UI

Layer 3: Remote Signer HALT
  - Cloudflare Worker checks HALT flag before ANY signing operation
  - If HALT is set, Worker rejects ALL signing requests with 503
  - This is the ultimate backstop — even if app host is compromised

Layer 4: On-Chain Pause (Optional)
  - For future: deploy a minimal on-chain program that acts as a gate
  - Admin can pause the program, making OSIRIS-generated transactions invalid
  - Requires a small program deployment but provides cryptographic guarantee

### 5.2 Kill Switch Triggers
Automatic triggers:
  - Circuit breaker trips (P5.1)
  - Rate limit exceeded on signing Worker
  - Failed simulation rate > 50% over 5-minute window
  - Unusual withdrawal pattern detected
  - Admin API receives authenticated HALT command

Manual triggers:
  - Admin dashboard panic button
  - Telegram /session_revoke_all command (Tier 3 only)
  - Emergency phone/SMS hotline (future)

### 5.3 Kill Switch Recovery
  - HALT state requires TWO admin approvals to clear
  - 60-minute mandatory cooldown (same as circuit breaker override)
  - Typed confirmation required
  - All systems must pass health check before trading resumes
  - Post-HALT audit log review required

### 5.4 Where This Goes in the Plan
- NEW section: P5.8 — Global Emergency Kill Switch
- UPDATE: P1.1 Remote Signer — add HALT flag check to policy engine (P7)
- UPDATE: P1.5 Trade Execution Pipeline — add HALT state check before SIMULATED
- UPDATE: P7.4 Telegram Trust Tiers — add /halt and /resume commands (Tier 3)

# ================================================================================
# GAP 6: TRANSACTION RETRY & EXPIRY STRATEGY
# ================================================================================

## Current Plan Status
The plan says "maxRetries: 0 (let Sender handle retries)" (P1.4) and mentions
"failed job triggers retry (up to limit)" (P1.5). There is NO explicit retry
strategy for:
- Stale blockhash
- Insufficient priority fee
- Account contention (hot accounts)
- Network partition
- Leader rotation mid-submission

## Why This Is Critical
Solana transactions expire after ~90-150 slots (~60-90 seconds). A transaction
that doesn't land within its blockhash lifetime is dead. Without a retry
strategy, the bot simply loses the opportunity and burns fees on failed
attempts.

## What Must Be Added

### 6.1 Retry Rules
| Failure Reason | Retry? | Strategy |
|---------------|--------|----------|
| Stale blockhash | Yes | Refresh blockhash, resubmit (max 3 attempts) |
| Insufficient fee | Yes | Increase CU price by 25%, resubmit (max 3) |
| Account contention | Yes | Wait 1 slot (~400ms), resubmit with higher fee |
| Simulation failed | No | Log and abort — don't burn fees on known failures |
| Compute budget exceeded | No | Abort and alert — fix the instruction |
| Signature verification failed | No | Abort — indicates key corruption |

### 6.2 Blockhash Management
- Fetch fresh blockhash every 30 seconds (not per transaction)
- Cache blockhash with lastValidBlockHeight
- If lastValidBlockHeight is within 20 blocks of current, refresh immediately
- Use `getLatestBlockhash({ commitment: 'processed' })` for speed

### 6.3 Expiry Handling
- Track transaction signature after send
- Poll for confirmation with timeout = blockhash lifetime - 10 blocks
- If timeout expires without confirmation, consider transaction "expired"
- Do NOT retry expired transactions blindly — re-simulate first

### 6.4 Duplicate Signature Protection
- Maintain a `recent_signatures` table (TTL: 5 minutes)
- Before sending, check if signature was recently submitted
- Prevents double-spend on retry loops

### 6.5 Where This Goes in the Plan
- NEW section: P1.5c — Transaction Retry & Expiry Management
- UPDATE: P1.4 Helius Sender — add retry configuration with backoff
- UPDATE: P4.4 Copy Trade Execution — add retry logic for <2s latency budget

# GAP 7: CI/CD PIPELINE & SAFE DEPLOYMENT
# ================================================================================

## Current Plan Status
The plan has deployment scripts (P0.7) and mentions PM2 configs. There is NO
CI/CD pipeline, no staging environment, no deployment safety checks.

## Why This Is Critical
Deploying a trading bot without CI/CD is like performing surgery without
washing your hands. One bad deploy can:
  - Expose private keys
  - Break the database schema
  - Disable security controls
  - Introduce bugs that cost money

## What Must Be Added

### 7.1 CI/CD Pipeline (GitHub Actions)

On every PR:
  1. Lint (ESLint + Prettier)
  2. Type check (tsc --noEmit)
  3. Unit tests (vitest)
  4. Integration tests (testcontainers for Postgres/Redis)
  5. Security scan (npm audit, Snyk, or Trivy)
  6. Database migration dry-run
  7. Build check

On merge to main:
  1. All PR checks must pass
  2. Deploy to staging (separate Oracle Cloud VM)
  3. Run smoke tests against staging
  4. Manual approval for production deploy
  5. Blue-green deploy to production
  6. Post-deploy health checks
  7. Rollback on failure

### 7.2 Deployment Safety Gates
  - No deploy between 00:00-06:00 UTC (low liquidity, hard to detect issues)
  - No deploy on Friday (weekend support risk)
  - Require two approvals for production deploys
  - Feature flags must be explicitly set, not inherited
  - Database migrations must be backward-compatible (expand-contract pattern)

### 7.3 Staging Environment
  - Separate Oracle Cloud Always Free VM
  - Devnet-only (no mainnet keys)
  - Same Docker Compose stack as production
  - Same PM2 config, scaled down
  - Same monitoring stack

### 7.4 Where This Goes in the Plan
- NEW section: P0.11 — CI/CD Pipeline & Deployment Safety
- UPDATE: P0.7 Oracle Cloud Deployment — add staging environment
- UPDATE: P10.1 Monitoring — add deployment metrics

# GAP 9: TOKEN SNIFFER / HONEYPOT DETECTION BEYOND RUGCHECK
# ================================================================================

## Current Plan Status
The plan has RugCheck integration (P5.5) and Token-2022 safety checks (P1.6).
It does NOT have comprehensive honeypot detection for standard SPL tokens.

## Why This Is Critical
RugCheck scores are retrospective. A token can pass RugCheck and still be a
honeypot (buy-only, sell-disabled, tax that drains 99% on sell). OSIRIS needs
proactive detection BEFORE trading.

## What Must Be Added

### 9.1 Honeypot Checks (Pre-Trade)
For every token not in the top 100 by market cap:
  1. Simulate a small buy (0.001 SOL worth)
  2. Simulate a sell of the purchased amount
  3. If sell simulation fails or returns < 50% of buy value, flag as honeypot
  4. Check mint authority — if mint authority exists, HIGH RISK
  5. Check freeze authority — if freeze authority exists, HIGH RISK
  6. Check if token is on Jupiter's strict token list

### 9.2 Liquidity Analysis
  - Check if liquidity is locked (burned LP tokens)
  - Check LP token distribution (single wallet holding > 50% = risk)
  - Check if pool has been live for > 24 hours
  - Check if creator wallet has launched > 3 tokens in 7 days (pump & dump)

### 9.3 Where This Goes in the Plan
- NEW section: P1.6b — Honeypot & Liquidity Safety Checks
- UPDATE: P5.5 RugCheck — add honeypot simulation as primary check

# ================================================================================
# GAP 10: WALLET RECOVERY & SEED PHRASE BACKUP UX
# ================================================================================

## Current Plan Status
The plan covers wallet generation and encryption (P1.2) but has NO recovery
mechanism. If a user loses their OSIRIS login, they lose access to their
encrypted wallet — and their funds.

## Why This Is Critical
This is a financial product. Users WILL forget passwords, lose phones, delete
Telegram accounts. Without recovery, OSIRIS becomes a fund-locking service, not a
trading bot.

## What Must Be Added

### 10.1 Recovery Options (Tiered)
Tier 1 (Standard): Email-based recovery
  - Send encrypted seed phrase fragment to user's verified email
  - Requires email verification + TOTP
  - Fragment is useless without the server-held fragment

Tier 2 (Advanced): Social recovery
  - User designates 2-3 recovery contacts
  - Any 2 of 3 can authorize recovery
  - Uses Shamir's Secret Sharing (SSS)

Tier 3 (Maximum): Manual recovery
  - User writes down full seed phrase during onboarding
  - Stored offline, never transmitted
  - Required for Tier 3 (whale) accounts

### 10.2 Implementation Note
NEVER store plaintext seed phrases. Use SSS to split the seed into shards:
  - 1 shard stored encrypted in database
  - 1 shard sent to user's email (encrypted)
  - 1 shard held by OSIRIS admin (in cold storage, encrypted)

Recovery requires 2 of 3 shards. No single party can reconstruct the seed.

### 10.3 Where This Goes in the Plan
- NEW section: P2.6 — Wallet Recovery & Backup UX
- UPDATE: P1.2 Wallet Generation — add SSS shard creation during generation

The plan mentions admin dashboard (P4.6) and security controls but has NO
multi-signature requirement for admin operations.

## Why This Is Critical

## What Must Be Added

### 11.1 Multi-Sig Requirements
These operations require 2-of-3 admin signatures:
  - Global HALT / resume
  - Change fee percentages
  - Modify tier limits
  - Withdraw from treasury
  - Deploy database migrations (destructive)
  - Change remote signer policy
  - Add/remove admin accounts

### 11.2 Implementation
Use a simple database-based multi-sig (not on-chain, for speed):
  - Each admin has an Ed25519 key pair
  - Proposals are created with operation details
  - Admins sign proposals with their keys
  - Proposal executes automatically when threshold reached
  - All proposals logged in audit trail

# GAP 12: COMPUTE UNIT LIMIT OPTIMIZATION

The plan mentions "compute budget instruction injection" (P1.4) but has NO

## Why This Is Critical
Default CU limit is 200,000 per instruction. A basic swap uses ~6,000 CU but
with default limit you pay for 200,000. Over 1,000 trades, that's 194,000,000
wasted CU — which translates to wasted priority fees.

## What Must Be Added

### 12.1 CU Limits by Transaction Type
| Transaction Type | Typical CU | Recommended Limit |
|-----------------|------------|-------------------|
| Simple SOL transfer | ~6,000 | 10,000 |
| SPL token transfer | ~8,000 | 15,000 |
| Jupiter swap (simple route) | ~80,000-150,000 | Simulated + 10% |
| Jupiter swap (complex route) | ~200,000-400,000 | Simulated + 10% |
| ATA creation | ~25,000 | 35,000 |
| Token-2022 swap (with extensions) | ~150,000-300,000 | Simulated + 15% |

### 12.2 CU Price Strategy
- Start with p50 of recent fees on target accounts
- Escalate by 25% on each retry
- Cap at p95 + 50% (prevent runaway fees)
- Never exceed 1% of trade value in fees

# OSIRIS — LOW-LATENCY INFRASTRUCTURE STRATEGY
# Every Millisecond Counts When Money Moves
# ================================================================================

# ================================================================================
# 1. THE BRUTAL TRUTH ABOUT FREE-TIER LATENCY
# ================================================================================

## What the Research Says (2026)

"RPC latency doesn't follow a distribution where the mean tells you anything.
A small fraction of requests are dramatically slower than the rest — and those
are exactly the requests that decide whether your transaction lands."

"In fast markets like crypto, even 50 ms of extra lag can cost significant
profit because prices can change before your transaction lands in a block."

"A well-tuned searcher pipeline can complete detection → bundle construction →
simulation → submission in under 50 milliseconds end-to-end. That is the
difference between competing and watching."

## Free Tier Reality

| Provider | Free Tier | Typical Latency | Problem |
|----------|-----------|-----------------|---------|
| Helius | 1M credits, 10 RPS | 140-225ms | Shared infrastructure, rate-limited |
| Public RPC | Unlimited | 50-200ms+ | Filtered, de-prioritized during congestion |
| Dedicated node | $2,200+/mo | 2-4ms | Not free |

**Bottom line:** You will NOT get sub-50ms on free infrastructure. You CAN get
under 100-150ms with aggressive optimization. For copy trading (not HFT
arbitrage), this is competitive.

## The Four Latency Segments You Must Track

1. **RPC call latency** — getLatestBlockhash, getAccountInfo, getSlot
   Target: p99 under 50ms for lightweight calls

2. **Data freshness lag** — how many slots behind is your data?
   Target: at or under 1 slot (~400ms)

3. **Submission latency** — sendTransaction round-trip
   Target: p99 under 100ms

4. **Time-to-land** — submission to confirmed-in-block
   Target: under 2 slots for competitive bot

Track ALL FOUR separately. Averaging them hides the real problem.

# ================================================================================
# 2. GEOGRAPHIC PROXIMITY — THE #1 FREE OPTIMIZATION
# ================================================================================

## Where Are Solana RPC Nodes?

Major Solana validator/RPC clusters:
- **Frankfurt, Germany** — primary EU hub
- **Ashburn, Virginia (US-East)** — primary US hub  
- **Amsterdam, Netherlands** — secondary EU
- **Tokyo, Japan** — APAC hub

## Where Should Your Oracle VM Be?

| Oracle Region | Distance to RPC Hub | Estimated RTT |
|-------------|---------------------|---------------|
| Frankfurt (eu-frankfurt-1) | Same city | 1-5ms |
| Amsterdam (eu-amsterdam-1) | ~400km | 5-10ms |
| London (uk-london-1) | ~640km | 10-15ms |
| Ashburn (us-ashburn-1) | Same city | 1-5ms |
| Phoenix (us-phoenix-1) | ~3,700km | 50-70ms |
| San Jose (us-sanjose-1) | ~3,900km | 55-75ms |

**CRITICAL:** Deploy your Oracle VM in the SAME region as your primary RPC
provider. If you use Helius (US-based), deploy in Ashburn. If you use a
EU-focused provider, deploy in Frankfurt.

A 150ms round-trip delay (typical Europe → US) eats 25-35% of a slot before
the RPC even forwards your transaction. cite🛠web_search:12#5:~:text=A 150ms round-trip delay...eat 25-35% of a slot

## How to Check Your Current Latency

```bash
# Test RTT to Helius endpoint

# Test RTT to Jito block engine
ping mainnet.block-engine.jito.wtf

# Full path test (from your Oracle VM)
curl -w "@curl-format.txt" -o /dev/null -s   https://mainnet.helius-rpc.com/?api-key=YOUR_KEY   -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json"   -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"getSlot"}'
```


**If time_total > 100ms, your VM is in the wrong region.**

# ================================================================================
# 3. CONNECTION OPTIMIZATION — PERSISTENT HTTP/2
# ================================================================================

## The Problem

Default HTTP clients create a new TCP connection for every request. TCP
handshake = ~30-50ms. TLS handshake = ~50-100ms. That's 80-150ms of dead time
BEFORE your RPC call even starts.

## The Fix: Connection Pooling + Keep-Alive

```typescript
// src/lib/rpc-client.ts — Optimized RPC connection
import { Connection, Commitment } from '@solana/web3.js';

// Use a SINGLE shared connection instance — never recreate per request
export const connection = new Connection(
  process.env.HELIUS_RPC_URL!,
  {
    commitment: 'processed' as Commitment,  // Fastest commitment level
    confirmTransactionInitialTimeout: 30000,
    // web3.js uses fetch under the hood — ensure keep-alive
    fetch: (url: string, options: any) => {
      return fetch(url, {
        ...options,
        keepalive: true,  // HTTP keep-alive
      });
    },
  }
);
```

## HTTP/2 Multiplexing

HTTP/2 allows multiple requests over a single connection. This eliminates
head-of-line blocking and reduces per-request overhead to near-zero after the
initial connection.

```typescript
// Use undici or node-fetch with HTTP/2 support
import { Pool } from 'undici';

const heliusPool = new Pool(process.env.HELIUS_RPC_URL!, {
  connections: 5,           // 5 persistent connections
  keepAliveTimeout: 30000,  // 30s keep-alive
  keepAliveMaxTimeout: 60000,
  pipelining: 10,           // 10 requests per connection
});

// All RPC calls reuse connections from the pool
export async function rpcCall(method: string, params: any[]) {
  const { body } = await heliusPool.request({
    method: 'POST',
    path: '/?api-key=' + process.env.HELIUS_API_KEY,
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ jsonrpc: '2.0', id: 1, method, params }),
  });
  return body.json();
}
```

## WebSocket Connection Reuse

```typescript
// src/lib/ws-client.ts — Persistent WebSocket for subscriptions
import { WebSocket } from 'ws';

class PersistentWebSocket {
  private ws: WebSocket | null = null;
  private reconnectTimer: NodeJS.Timeout | null = null;
  private subscriptions = new Map<number, string>(); // id -> method

  connect() {
    this.ws = new WebSocket(process.env.HELIUS_WS_URL!);

    this.ws.on('open', () => {
      console.log('WebSocket connected');
      // Resubscribe to all active subscriptions
      this.subscriptions.forEach((method, id) => {
        this.send({ jsonrpc: '2.0', id, method, params: [] });
      });
    });

    this.ws.on('message', (data) => {
      // Route to handler
      const msg = JSON.parse(data.toString());
      this.handleMessage(msg);
    });

    this.ws.on('close', () => {
      console.log('WebSocket closed — reconnecting in 1s');
      this.reconnectTimer = setTimeout(() => this.connect(), 1000);
    });
  }

  subscribe(method: string, params: any[], handler: (data: any) => void) {
    const id = Date.now();
    this.subscriptions.set(id, method);
    this.send({ jsonrpc: '2.0', id, method, params });
    // Store handler for routing
    return id;
  }

  private send(msg: any) {
    if (this.ws?.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN) {
      this.ws.send(JSON.stringify(msg));
    }
  }
}

export const wsClient = new PersistentWebSocket();
```

**Why this matters:** A single WebSocket connection replaces hundreds of HTTP
polls per second. For real-time data (account changes, slot updates), WebSocket
is 10-50x faster than polling.

# ================================================================================
# 4. BLOCKHASH CACHING — DON'T FETCH PER TRANSACTION
# ================================================================================

## The Problem

`getLatestBlockhash` takes 30-100ms. If you fetch it for every transaction,
you're adding 30-100ms to every trade.

## The Fix: Background Blockhash Refresh

```typescript
// src/lib/blockhash-cache.ts
import { connection } from './rpc-client';

interface BlockhashEntry {
  blockhash: string;
  lastValidBlockHeight: number;
  fetchedAt: number;
}

class BlockhashCache {
  private cache: BlockhashEntry | null = null;
  private refreshInterval: NodeJS.Timeout | null = null;

  start() {
    // Refresh every 10 seconds (blockhash valid for ~90 slots = ~60s)
    this.refreshInterval = setInterval(() => this.refresh(), 10000);
    this.refresh(); // Initial fetch
  }

  private async refresh() {
    try {
      const { blockhash, lastValidBlockHeight } = 
        await connection.getLatestBlockhash('processed');
      this.cache = { blockhash, lastValidBlockHeight, fetchedAt: Date.now() };
    } catch (err) {
      console.error('Blockhash refresh failed:', err);
    }
  }

  get(): BlockhashEntry | null {
    // Return cached blockhash if still valid (within 30s of fetch)
    if (this.cache && Date.now() - this.cache.fetchedAt < 30000) {
      return this.cache;
    }
    return null;
  }

  // Force refresh (call when blockhash is known stale)
  async forceRefresh(): Promise<BlockhashEntry> {
    await this.refresh();
    if (!this.cache) throw new Error('Blockhash cache empty');
    return this.cache;
  }

  stop() {
    if (this.refreshInterval) clearInterval(this.refreshInterval);
  }
}

export const blockhashCache = new BlockhashCache();
```

**Impact:** Eliminates 30-100ms per transaction. For 100 trades/day, that's
3-10 seconds of saved latency.

# ================================================================================
# 5. PRE-COMPUTE TRANSACTIONS — BUILD BEFORE THE SIGNAL
# ================================================================================

## The Problem

Copy trading has a <2s latency budget. Building a transaction from scratch
(quote → instructions → serialize → sign → send) takes 200-500ms.

## The Fix: Pre-Build Transaction Templates

```typescript
// src/services/trading/prebuild.ts
import { VersionedTransaction, TransactionMessage } from '@solana/web3.js';

interface PrebuiltSwap {
  tokenIn: string;
  tokenOut: string;
  route: any; // Jupiter route
  messageV0: TransactionMessage;
  estimatedCU: number;
  maxSlippageBps: number;
}

class PrebuildEngine {
  private cache = new Map<string, PrebuiltSwap>(); // key: "tokenIn:tokenOut"

  // Pre-build swap transactions for likely pairs
  async prebuild(pairs: Array<{ in: string; out: string }>) {
    for (const pair of pairs) {
      try {
        const route = await fetchJupiterQuote(pair.in, pair.out, 1000000); // 0.001 SOL
        if (!route) continue;

        const { blockhash } = await blockhashCache.forceRefresh();

        const messageV0 = new TransactionMessage({
          payerKey: wallet.publicKey,
          recentBlockhash: blockhash,
          instructions: await buildSwapInstructions(route),
        }).compileToV0Message();

        const estimatedCU = await simulateCU(messageV0);

        this.cache.set(`${pair.in}:${pair.out}`, {
          tokenIn: pair.in,
          tokenOut: pair.out,
          route,
          messageV0,
          estimatedCU,
          maxSlippageBps: 100, // 1%
        });
      } catch (err) {
        console.error(`Prebuild failed for ${pair.in}:${pair.out}`, err);
      }
    }
  }

  // On signal: just sign and send the pre-built tx
  async executePrebuilt(
    pairKey: string,
    amount: bigint,
    slippageBps: number
  ): Promise<string> {
    const prebuilt = this.cache.get(pairKey);
    if (!prebuilt) throw new Error('No prebuilt transaction');

    // Update blockhash (cached, <5ms)
    const { blockhash } = await blockhashCache.forceRefresh();
    prebuilt.messageV0.recentBlockhash = blockhash;

    // Update slippage if needed
    if (slippageBps !== prebuilt.maxSlippageBps) {
      // Rebuild with new slippage (rare, <50ms)
      return this.rebuildAndExecute(prebuilt, amount, slippageBps);
    }

    // Sign via remote signer (Cloudflare Worker)
    const tx = await signTransaction(prebuilt.messageV0);

    // Send via multi-path
    return sendMultiPath(tx);
  }
}
```

**Impact:** Reduces copy trade execution from 200-500ms to 50-100ms for
pre-built pairs.

# ================================================================================
# 6. MULTI-PATH SUBMISSION — PARALLEL FIRE
# ================================================================================

## The Problem

Single-path submission is a single point of failure. If your primary RPC is
congested, your transaction sits in a queue while the opportunity vanishes.

## The Fix: Fire to All Paths Simultaneously

```typescript
// src/services/trading/multipath.ts
interface SubmissionPath {
  name: string;
  send: (tx: VersionedTransaction) => Promise<string>;
}

const paths: SubmissionPath[] = [
  { name: 'helius', send: sendViaHelius },
  { name: 'jito-ny', send: sendViaJitoNY },
  { name: 'jito-frankfurt', send: sendViaJitoFrankfurt },
  { name: 'jito-tokyo', send: sendViaJitoTokyo },
];

export async function sendMultiPath(
  tx: VersionedTransaction
): Promise<string> {
  const abortController = new AbortController();

  const promises = paths.map(async (path) => {
    try {
      const signature = await path.send(tx);
      // First to land wins — abort others
      abortController.abort();
      return { path: path.name, signature, success: true };
    } catch (err) {
      return { path: path.name, signature: null, success: false, error: err };
    }
  });

  const results = await Promise.allSettled(promises);
  const winner = results.find(
    (r) => r.status === 'fulfilled' && r.value.success
  );

  if (!winner) {
    throw new Error('All submission paths failed');
  }

  return (winner as any).value.signature;
}
```

**Impact:** Increases landing probability from ~60% (single path) to ~90%
(multi-path). The first successful response wins — duplicate signatures are
handled by Solana's signature deduplication.

## Jito Multi-Relay Submission

```typescript
// Submit to all Jito regional endpoints in parallel
const JITO_ENDPOINTS = [
  'https://mainnet.block-engine.jito.wtf/api/v1/bundles',
  'https://amsterdam.mainnet.block-engine.jito.wtf/api/v1/bundles',
  'https://frankfurt.mainnet.block-engine.jito.wtf/api/v1/bundles',
  'https://ny.mainnet.block-engine.jito.wtf/api/v1/bundles',
  'https://tokyo.mainnet.block-engine.jito.wtf/api/v1/bundles',
];

async function sendViaJito(tx: VersionedTransaction): Promise<string> {
  const bundle = [Buffer.from(tx.serialize()).toString('base64')];

  const promises = JITO_ENDPOINTS.map(async (endpoint) => {
    const res = await fetch(endpoint, {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      body: JSON.stringify({
        jsonrpc: '2.0',
        id: 1,
        method: 'sendBundle',
        params: [bundle],
      }),
    });
    return res.json();
  });

  const results = await Promise.allSettled(promises);
  // Return first successful bundle ID
  for (const result of results) {
    if (result.status === 'fulfilled' && result.value.result) {
      return result.value.result;
    }
  }
  throw new Error('All Jito relays failed');
}
```

cite🛠web_search:12#4:~:text=The bundle is forwarded to multiple Block Engine regional endpoints in parallel

# ================================================================================
# 7. REDIS OPTIMIZATION — SUB-MILLISECOND CACHE
# ================================================================================

## The Problem

Every database query to PostgreSQL takes 1-10ms. For hot data (user sessions,
feature flags, rate limit counters), that's unacceptable.

## The Fix: Redis for Everything Hot

```typescript
// src/lib/redis.ts — Optimized Redis client
import Redis from 'ioredis';

export const redis = new Redis(process.env.REDIS_URL!, {
  // Connection pooling (built into ioredis)
  lazyConnect: false,
  keepAlive: 30000,

  // Pipeline commands for batch operations
  enableOfflineQueue: false, // Fail fast if Redis is down

  // Retry strategy: exponential backoff
  retryStrategy: (times) => {
    if (times > 3) return null; // Stop retrying after 3 attempts
    return Math.min(times * 50, 2000);
  },
});

// Hot data patterns
export const cache = {
  // User session: < 1ms vs 5-10ms DB query
  async getSession(sessionId: string) {
    const data = await redis.get(`session:${sessionId}`);
    return data ? JSON.parse(data) : null;
  },

  async setSession(sessionId: string, data: any, ttl = 3600) {
    await redis.setex(`session:${sessionId}`, ttl, JSON.stringify(data));
  },

  // Feature flags: < 1ms vs 5-10ms DB query
  async getFlag(flag: string): Promise<boolean> {
    const value = await redis.get(`flag:${flag}`);
    return value === '1'; // Fail closed: missing = false
  },

  // Rate limit counters: < 1ms
  async incrementCounter(key: string, window: number) {
    const multi = redis.multi();
    multi.incr(key);
    multi.expire(key, window);
    const [count] = await multi.exec();
    return count as number;
  },

  // Quote cache: 10s TTL (already in plan, but optimize storage)
  async getQuote(pair: string) {
    return redis.get(`quote:${pair}`);
  },

  async setQuote(pair: string, data: string, ttl = 10) {
    await redis.setex(`quote:${pair}`, ttl, data);
  },
};
```

**Impact:** Hot path operations go from 5-10ms (DB) to <1ms (Redis).

# ================================================================================
# 8. DATABASE QUERY OPTIMIZATION
# ================================================================================

## The Problem

Slow queries in the trade path add latency. A missing index on `trades` or
`positions` can turn a 1ms query into a 500ms query.

## Critical Indexes (Must Exist Before Trading)

```sql
-- Trade lookups by user + status
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_trades_user_status ON trades(user_id, status);

-- Trade lookups by wallet + token
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_trades_wallet_token ON trades(wallet_id, token_mint);

-- Position lookups by user
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_positions_user ON positions(user_id, token_mint);

-- Session lookups by user + status
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_sessions_user_status ON trading_sessions(user_id, status);

-- Job queue lookups by name + state
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_jobs_name_state ON pgboss.job(name, state);

-- Webhook event deduplication
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_webhook_sig ON webhook_events(signature);

-- Notification lookups by user + read status
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_notifications_user ON notifications(user_id, read);

-- Rate limit lookups
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_rate_limits ON rate_limits(user_id, action, window_start);
```

## Query Optimization Rules

1. **Never SELECT * in hot paths** — specify only needed columns
2. **Use covering indexes** — index includes all columns in the query
3. **Batch inserts** — use `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT` for idempotency
4. **Avoid N+1 queries** — use JOINs or IN clauses
5. **Use prepared statements** — skip parse/plan phase

## Example: Optimized Trade Insert

```typescript
// BAD: Multiple round-trips
const trade = await db.insert(trades).values({...}).returning();
await db.insert(trade_events).values({ tradeId: trade.id, ... });
await db.update(positions).set({...}).where(...);

// GOOD: Single transaction
await db.transaction(async (tx) => {
  const [trade] = await tx.insert(trades).values({...}).returning();
  await tx.insert(trade_events).values({ tradeId: trade.id, ... });
  await tx.update(positions).set({...}).where(...);
});
```

```typescript
// app/api/health/route.ts — Edge runtime (fastest)
export const runtime = 'edge';

export async function GET() {
  // Redis ping only — < 1ms

}
```

# ================================================================================
# 10. TELEMETRY & LATENCY BUDGET TRACKING
# ================================================================================

## Define Your Latency Budget

| Step | Target | Max Acceptable |
|------|--------|----------------|
| Signal detection (webhook) | < 50ms | < 100ms |
| Decode + validation | < 20ms | < 50ms |
| Quote fetch (cached) | < 10ms | < 30ms |
| Transaction build | < 30ms | < 100ms |
| Simulation | < 50ms | < 100ms |
| Signing (remote) | < 30ms | < 100ms |
| Multi-path submission | < 50ms | < 100ms |
| **TOTAL COPY TRADE** | **< 240ms** | **< 500ms** |

## Per-Request Timing

```typescript
// src/lib/timing.ts
class TradeTimer {
  private spans: Array<{ name: string; start: number; end?: number }> = [];

  start(name: string) {
    this.spans.push({ name, start: performance.now() });
  }

  end(name: string) {
    const span = this.spans.find((s) => s.name === name && !s.end);
    if (span) span.end = performance.now();
  }

  report() {
    return this.spans.map((s) => ({
      name: s.name,
      duration: (s.end || performance.now()) - s.start,
    }));
  }
}

// Usage in copy trade flow
const timer = new TradeTimer();
timer.start('detect');
const signal = await decodeWebhook(event);
timer.end('detect');

timer.start('quote');
const quote = await cache.getQuote(`${signal.tokenIn}:${signal.tokenOut}`);
timer.end('quote');

// Log to structured logger
logger.info({
  event: 'copy_trade_timing',
  tradeId,
  spans: timer.report(),
  total: timer.report().reduce((sum, s) => sum + s.duration, 0),
});
```

## Alert on Latency Budget Breaches

```typescript
// Alert if any step exceeds max acceptable
for (const span of timer.report()) {
  const max = LATENCY_BUDGET[span.name];
  if (span.duration > max) {
    logger.warn({
      event: 'latency_budget_exceeded',
      step: span.name,
      actual: span.duration,
      budget: max,
      tradeId,
    });
  }
}
```

# 11. FREE-TIER LATENCY REALITY CHECK
# ================================================================================

## What You CAN Achieve (Free Tier)

| Optimization | Latency Impact | Cost |
|-------------|----------------|------|
| Same-region deployment | -50-150ms | $0 |
| Connection pooling | -30-100ms per call | $0 |
| Blockhash caching | -30-100ms per tx | $0 |
| Pre-built transactions | -100-300ms per trade | $0 |
| Multi-path submission | +landing rate, minimal latency | $0 |
| Redis hot cache | -5-10ms per query | $0 |
| DB indexes | -100-500ms per query | $0 |
| Edge runtime for health | -100-500ms cold start | $0 |

## What You CANNOT Achieve (Free Tier)

| Optimization | Latency Impact | Why Not Free |
|-------------|----------------|--------------|
| Dedicated RPC node | 2-4ms | $2,200+/mo |
| Co-located bare metal | 5-10ms | $500+/mo |
| Stake-weighted QoS | 83% first-block | Requires ~5,000 SOL stake |
| Jito ShredStream | 100-200ms faster | Requires premium Jito access |
| Yellowstone gRPC | 50-100ms faster | Requires dedicated node |
| Direct TPU connection | 10-20ms | Complex infra, not free |

## Honest Targets for OSIRIS (Free Tier)

| Metric | Target | Competitive? |
|--------|--------|--------------|
| RPC call p99 | < 100ms | Acceptable for copy trading |
| Submission p99 | < 150ms | Acceptable for copy trading |
| Time-to-land | < 3 slots | Good for copy trading |
| Copy trade E2E | < 500ms | Competitive for copy trading |
| Standard trade E2E | < 2s | Good for manual trading |

**Copy trading is NOT HFT arbitrage.** You don't need sub-50ms. You need to
land within 1-2 slots of the target wallet. A 500ms copy trade on a token
launch is still profitable if the target wallet is a whale whose trades move
the market.

## When to Upgrade

| Trigger | Upgrade | Cost |
|---------|---------|------|
| > 500 active traders | Dedicated RPC (Helius paid) | ~$49-199/mo |
| > 5,000 trades/day | Second Oracle VM or Hetzner | ~$6/mo |
| p99 RPC > 200ms sustained | Premium RPC provider | ~$99-499/mo |
| Landing rate < 70% | Jito premium + SWQoS | ~$200-500/mo |

## Current Plan Status
The plan has circuit breakers for external APIs but NO strategy for what
happens when internal infrastructure fails. If Redis dies, does the bot crash?
If PostgreSQL is slow, do trades time out? If the worker queue backs up, what
happens to new trades?

## Why This Is Critical
A trading bot that crashes when Redis is unavailable is worse than a bot that
trades slowly. Every component must have a defined fallback behavior.

## What Must Be Added

### 13.1 Redis Failure Fallbacks

| Feature | Normal (Redis Up) | Degraded (Redis Down) |
|---------|-------------------|----------------------|
| Sessions | Redis (< 1ms) | PostgreSQL (5-10ms) |
| Rate limits | Redis sliding window | Fail-closed (reject all) |
| Feature flags | Redis (< 1ms) | PostgreSQL (5-10ms) |
| Quote cache | Redis (10s TTL) | Skip cache (fetch fresh) |
| WebSocket pub/sub | Redis | In-memory (single instance only) |

```typescript
// src/lib/redis-fallback.ts
class RedisWithFallback {
  private redis: Redis | null = null;
  private fallbackMode = false;

  async get(key: string): Promise<string | null> {
    try {
      if (!this.fallbackMode && this.redis) {
        return await this.redis.get(key);
      }
    } catch (err) {
      this.enterFallbackMode();
    }
    // Fallback: query PostgreSQL for sessions/flags
    return await dbQuery(key);
  }

  private enterFallbackMode() {
    if (this.fallbackMode) return;
    this.fallbackMode = true;
    logger.error('REDIS_DOWN: Entering fallback mode');
    // Alert admin
    alertAdmin('Redis is down — operating in degraded mode');
  }
}
```

### 13.2 PostgreSQL Slow Query Protection

```typescript
// src/db/query-guard.ts
const QUERY_TIMEOUT = 5000; // 5 seconds max

export async function safeQuery<T>(
  queryFn: () => Promise<T>,
  fallbackFn?: () => Promise<T>
): Promise<T> {
  const timeout = new Promise<never>((_, reject) =>
    setTimeout(() => reject(new Error('QUERY_TIMEOUT')), QUERY_TIMEOUT)
  );

  try {
    return await Promise.race([queryFn(), timeout]);
  } catch (err) {
    if (err.message === 'QUERY_TIMEOUT' && fallbackFn) {
      logger.warn('Query timed out, using fallback');
      return fallbackFn();
    }
    throw err;
  }
}
```

### 13.3 Worker Queue Overflow

```typescript
// src/jobs/overflow-handler.ts
const MAX_QUEUE_DEPTH = 2000;
const OVERFLOW_STRATEGY = 'reject'; // or 'drop_oldest'

export async function enqueueJob(name: string, data: unknown) {
  const depth = await getQueueDepth(name);

  if (depth > MAX_QUEUE_DEPTH) {
    if (OVERFLOW_STRATEGY === 'reject') {
      throw new Error(`QUEUE_OVERFLOW: ${name} at ${depth} jobs`);
    }
    // Drop oldest non-critical jobs
    await dropOldestJobs(name, depth - MAX_QUEUE_DEPTH);
  }

  return boss.send(name, data);
}
```

### 13.4 External API Degradation

| Service | Healthy | Degraded | Critical |
|---------|---------|----------|----------|
| Helius RPC | Full features | Read-only mode, no sends | Halt trading |
| Jupiter API | Full quotes | Cached quotes only | Halt trading |
| PumpPortal WS | Real-time | Polling fallback | Halt copy trading |
| Jito Bundle | Full bundles | Standard RPC only | Halt bundle trades |

```bash
# scripts/rotate-secret.sh
# 1. Generate new secret
# 2. Update Cloudflare Worker secrets (immediate)
# 3. Update Oracle VM .env (requires restart)
# 4. Verify both old and new work during transition
# 5. Revoke old secret after 24h grace period
```

### 14.3 Secret Versioning
```typescript
// src/lib/secrets.ts
class SecretManager {
  private secrets: Map<string, { value: string; version: number; createdAt: Date }> = new Map();

  async rotate(key: string, newValue: string) {
    const old = this.secrets.get(key);
    // Accept both old and new for 24h
    this.secrets.set(key, { value: newValue, version: (old?.version || 0) + 1, createdAt: new Date() });

    // Schedule old revocation
    setTimeout(() => this.revokeOld(key, old?.version), 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000);
  }

  get(key: string): string | undefined {
    return this.secrets.get(key)?.value;
  }
}
```

# ================================================================================
# GAP 15: CANARY WALLET STRATEGY
# ================================================================================

## Current Plan Status
The risk register mentions a canary wallet (RISK-002) but there is NO dedicated
section for implementation.

## What Is a Canary Wallet
A small-balance wallet (e.g., 0.5 SOL) that trades BEFORE user wallets. If the
bot has a bug, the canary loses money first — alerting you before user funds are
at risk.

## Implementation

### 15.1 Canary Wallet Rules
- Balance: 0.5-1.0 SOL (enough for fees, not enough to hurt)
- Mirrors user trades with 1-second delay
- If canary trade fails, BLOCK all user trades for 60 seconds
- If canary trade succeeds but user trade fails, alert immediately
- Canary PNL tracked separately — negative PNL triggers investigation

### 15.2 Canary Pipeline
```typescript
// src/services/trading/canary.ts
export async function executeWithCanary(trade: TradeRequest) {
  // 1. Execute on canary wallet first
  const canaryResult = await executeTrade({ ...trade, wallet: CANARY_WALLET });

  if (!canaryResult.success) {
    // Canary failed — block user trade, alert admin
    await alertAdmin(`CANARY_FAIL: ${canaryResult.error}`);
    throw new Error('CANARY_BLOCKED: Canary trade failed, user trade blocked');
  }

  // 2. Wait 1 second to observe canary outcome
  await sleep(1000);

  // 3. Check canary trade landed correctly
  const canaryConfirmed = await confirmTransaction(canaryResult.signature);
  if (!canaryConfirmed) {
    await alertAdmin('CANARY_UNCONFIRMED: Canary tx did not land');
    throw new Error('CANARY_BLOCKED: Canary tx unconfirmed');
  }

  // 4. Execute on user wallet
  return executeTrade(trade);
}
```

### 15.3 When to Use Canary
- ALWAYS for copy trading (automated, high risk)
- ALWAYS for new DEX integrations (untested code paths)
- ALWAYS after deployments (first 24 hours)
- OPTIONAL for manual trades (user-initiated, lower risk)

## Where This Goes
- NEW section: P1.9 — Canary Wallet & Pre-Production Safety

# GAP 16: WEBHOOK DEAD LETTER QUEUE (DLQ)
# ================================================================================

## Current Plan Status
The plan has webhook processing (P4.6) with retry logic but NO dead letter queue
for permanently failed webhooks. A webhook that fails 5 times is just... lost.

## What Must Be Added

### 16.1 DLQ Architecture
```
webhook_events table:
  - id, signature, payload, received_at, status
  - status: pending -> processing -> success / failed -> dlq

dlq table:
  - id, original_event_id, error, failed_at, retry_count, resolved_at
  - Alert on DLQ growth > 10 items
  - Manual review UI for DLQ items
```

### 16.2 DLQ Processing
```typescript
// src/services/webhooks/dlq.ts
export async function processDLQ() {
  const failed = await db.select().from(dlq).where(isNull(dlq.resolvedAt)).limit(100);

  for (const item of failed) {
    try {
      // Attempt replay with fresh data
      const freshData = await fetchTransaction(item.signature);
      await processWebhook(freshData);
      await db.update(dlq).set({ resolvedAt: new Date() }).where(eq(dlq.id, item.id));
    } catch (err) {
      // Log and alert if retry count > 10
      if (item.retryCount > 10) {
        await alertAdmin(`DLQ_PERMANENT_FAIL: ${item.signature}`);
      }
    }
  }
}
```

# GAP 17: SOLANA NETWORK UPGRADE HANDLING
# ================================================================================

## Current Plan Status
No mention of Solana mainnet upgrades, feature activations, or breaking changes.

## Why This Is Critical
Solana upgrades can change:
- Transaction format (versioned transactions were a breaking change)
- Fee structure (priority fees were added mid-2022)
- Program IDs (BPF Loader upgrades)
- Compute unit costs (CU repricing happens regularly)

A bot that doesn't handle upgrades will silently fail or burn fees on invalid
transactions.

## What Must Be Added

### 17.1 Upgrade Detection
```typescript
// src/lib/solana-upgrade-monitor.ts
class SolanaUpgradeMonitor {
  async checkForUpgrades() {
    const epochInfo = await connection.getEpochInfo();
    const featureSet = await connection.getGenesisHash(); // Proxy for version

    // Compare against known good version
    const knownVersion = await redis.get('solana:known_version');
    if (featureSet !== knownVersion) {
      logger.warn({ old: knownVersion, new: featureSet }, 'Solana version changed');
      await alertAdmin(`Solana network upgrade detected: ${featureSet}`);

      // Enter cautious mode: canary-only trades for 24h
      await redis.setex('trading:cautious_mode', 86400, '1');
    }
  }
}
```

### 17.2 Cautious Mode
When an upgrade is detected:
- All automated trading pauses for 1 hour
- Canary-only mode for 24 hours
- Manual approval required to resume full trading
- All transactions simulate before sending (even if normally skipped)

### 17.3 Post-Upgrade Validation Checklist
- [ ] simulateTransaction works for all transaction types
- [ ] Jupiter quotes return valid routes
- [ ] Helius Sender accepts transactions
- [ ] Jito bundles land correctly
- [ ] Token-2022 extensions parse correctly
- [ ] PNL computation matches pre-upgrade values

# GAP 19: SLOT-AWARE EXECUTION ENGINE
# ================================================================================

## Current Plan Status
The plan mentions blockhash caching but has NO slot-aware execution strategy.

## What the Research Says
"A fast bot isn't just about sending transactions quickly—it's about sending
them into the right slot, at the right time. Pre-build your transaction in the
previous slot. Fire at the start of the next one—with a dynamically-calibrated
priority fee." cite🛠web_search:17#5:~:text=Pre-build your transaction in the previous slot

## Implementation

### 19.1 Slot Tracking
```typescript
// src/lib/slot-tracker.ts
class SlotTracker {
  private currentSlot = 0;
  private slotLatency = 0; // How far behind is our node?

  constructor() {
    // Subscribe to slot notifications via WebSocket
    connection.onSlotChange((slotInfo) => {
      this.currentSlot = slotInfo.slot;
      this.slotLatency = Date.now() - slotInfo.timestamp;
    });
  }

  getCurrentSlot(): number { return this.currentSlot; }
  getSlotLatency(): number { return this.slotLatency; }

  // Estimate when next slot starts
  getNextSlotStart(): number {
    return Date.now() + (400 - (Date.now() % 400)); // ~400ms slots
  }
}
```

### 19.2 Slot-Optimized Submission
```typescript
// Fire at the start of the next slot for maximum landing probability
const nextSlotStart = slotTracker.getNextSlotStart();
const delay = nextSlotStart - Date.now() - 50; // Fire 50ms before slot start

setTimeout(() => {
  sendTransaction(tx);
}, Math.max(0, delay));
```
