# ================================================================================
# GAP 21: INCIDENT RESPONSE RUNBOOK
# ================================================================================

## Why This Is Critical
You have a kill switch, circuit breaker, and monitoring. But at 3am when the
kill switch trips and users are losing money, what EXACTLY do you do? Who gets
paged? What's the escalation path? Without a runbook, you'll waste critical
minutes figuring out who does what while an exploit drains funds. cite🛠web_search:21#9:~:text=Without a plan, you'll waste critical time figuring out who does what while an exploit drains funds

## What Must Be Added

### 21.1 Severity Levels
| Level | Name | Trigger | Response Time | Example |
|-------|------|---------|---------------|---------|
| SEV1 | Critical | User funds at risk, platform halted | 15 min | Kill switch tripped, suspected exploit |
| SEV2 | Major | Trading degraded, partial outage | 30 min | RPC provider down, >50% tx failures |
| SEV3 | Minor | Non-critical feature broken | 2 hours | PNL dashboard slow, notification delay |
| SEV4 | Low | Cosmetic, no user impact | Next business day | Log formatting issue |

### 21.2 Runbook: Kill Switch Tripped (SEV1)
```
TRIGGER: Alert "GLOBAL_HALT_ACTIVATED" fires

STEP 1: ACKNOWLEDGE (0-2 min)
  - Acknowledge in PagerDuty/Discord
  - Open incident channel: #inc-YYYYMMDD-halt
  - Post: "SEV1: Global halt active. Investigating."

STEP 2: ASSESS (2-5 min)
  - Check: Which trigger fired? (circuit breaker / admin / auto)
  - Check: Are user funds moving? (query recent transactions)
  - Check: Is this an attack or a bug?
  - Decision tree:
    - If attack suspected → Go to STEP 3A (Lockdown)
    - If bug suspected → Go to STEP 3B (Investigate)
    - If false positive → Go to STEP 3C (Resume)

STEP 3A: ATTACK LOCKDOWN (5-10 min)
  - Confirm HALT flag is set in DB
  - Confirm remote signer rejects all requests
  - Revoke ALL active sessions
  - Rotate API keys (Helius, Jupiter) immediately
  - Post status update to users
  - Escalate to security lead within 15 min
  - Begin forensic data collection (preserve logs)

STEP 3B: BUG INVESTIGATION (5-30 min)
  - Review recent deployments
  - Check error logs for pattern
  - Check canary wallet status
  - If root cause identified and safe → Go to STEP 4
  - If uncertain → Stay in HALT, escalate

STEP 3C: FALSE POSITIVE RESUME (5-10 min)
  - Verify no actual threat
  - Get 2-of-3 admin signatures for resume
  - 60-second cooldown + typed confirmation
  - Gradual resume: canary-only for 1 hour
  - Monitor for 4 hours before full resume

STEP 4: RESUME (after fix)
  - Deploy fix if bug
  - Run full test suite
  - Canary-only mode for 24 hours
  - Monitor all metrics
  - Post resolution update

STEP 5: POST-INCIDENT
  - Write timeline
  - Update runbook if steps were wrong
  - Schedule follow-up tasks
```

### 21.3 Communication Templates

**SEV1 Initial Update (every 15 min):**
```
🚨 SEV1 Incident Active
Status: Investigating
Impact: Trading halted, no funds at risk
What we know: [brief]
What we don't know: [brief]
What we're doing: [brief]
Next update: 15 minutes
```

**SEV1 Resolution:**
```
✅ SEV1 Resolved
Root cause: [brief]
Impact: [duration, affected users]
Action taken: [fix]
Prevention: [what we're doing to prevent recurrence]
```

### 21.4 Escalation Matrix
| Time Unresolved | Action |
|-----------------|--------|
| 15 min (SEV1) | Escalate to security lead |
| 30 min (SEV1) | Escalate to founder/CEO |
| 1 hour (SEV1) | External security firm on standby |
| 2 hours (SEV2) | Escalate to engineering lead |

## Where This Goes
- NEW section: P10.7 — Incident Response Runbook & Playbook

# GAP 23: DATABASE BACKUP & DISASTER RECOVERY
# ================================================================================

## Current Plan Status
Mentioned in P10.3 but has no detail. Backups should be operational from Phase 0.

## What Must Be Added

### 23.1 Backup Strategy
```bash
# scripts/backup.sh — Run daily via cron at 2 AM UTC
#!/bin/bash
set -e

DATE=$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)
BACKUP_DIR="/backups"
DB_NAME="osiris"
DB_USER="osiris"

# 1. PostgreSQL dump
docker exec osiris-db pg_dump -U $DB_USER $DB_NAME | gzip > "$BACKUP_DIR/osiris_$DATE.sql.gz"

# 2. Redis RDB snapshot
docker exec osiris-redis redis-cli SAVE
docker cp osiris-redis:/data/dump.rdb "$BACKUP_DIR/redis_$DATE.rdb"

# 3. Upload to Cloudflare R2 (encrypted)
aws s3 cp "$BACKUP_DIR/osiris_$DATE.sql.gz" s3://osiris-backups/   --endpoint-url https://<account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com

# 4. Keep only last 14 days locally, last 90 days in R2
find $BACKUP_DIR -name "osiris_*.sql.gz" -mtime +14 -delete
aws s3 ls s3://osiris-backups/ --endpoint-url https://<account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com |   awk '{print $4}' | sort | head -n -90 |   xargs -I {} aws s3 rm s3://osiris-backups/{} --endpoint-url https://<account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com

# 5. Verify backup integrity
if ! gunzip -t "$BACKUP_DIR/osiris_$DATE.sql.gz"; then
  alertAdmin "BACKUP_CORRUPT: $DATE"
  exit 1
fi

echo "Backup completed: $DATE"
```

### 23.2 Restore Testing (Monthly)
```bash
# scripts/restore-test.sh — Run monthly
#!/bin/bash
# 1. Spin up temporary PostgreSQL container
# 2. Download latest backup from R2
# 3. Restore to temporary DB
# 4. Run health checks (can query users, trades, sessions)
# 5. Verify row counts match production (within 1%)
# 6. Destroy temporary container
# 7. Log result
```

### 23.3 Disaster Recovery RTO/RPO
| Metric | Target | Definition |
|--------|--------|------------|
| RTO (Recovery Time Objective) | < 4 hours | Time to restore service after total loss |
| RPO (Recovery Point Objective) | < 24 hours | Max data loss (last backup) |
| Backup Frequency | Daily | Automated at 2 AM UTC |
| Retention | 90 days | Off-site (R2) |
| Encryption | AES-256 | At rest and in transit |

```typescript
// src/lib/cost-monitor.ts
class CostMonitor {
  async checkHeliusUsage() {
    // Helius doesn't have a direct API for credit usage
    // Estimate from request count
    const dailyRequests = await redis.get('metrics:helius:daily');
    const estimatedMonthly = Number(dailyRequests) * 30;
    const limit = 1_000_000; // Free tier

    const usagePercent = (estimatedMonthly / limit) * 100;

    if (usagePercent > 80) {
      await alertAdmin(`Helius usage at ${usagePercent.toFixed(1)}% — upgrade soon`);
    }
    if (usagePercent > 95) {
      await alertAdmin(`Helius usage at ${usagePercent.toFixed(1)}% — CRITICAL`);
      // Enter conservative mode: reduce polling frequency
      await redis.setex('mode:conservative', 86400, '1');
    }
  }
}
```

# ================================================================================
# GAP 26: GRACEFUL SHUTDOWN HANDLING
# ================================================================================

## Why This Matters
When Docker sends SIGTERM (container stop, deploy, restart), Node.js exits
immediately by default. In-flight trades, database writes, and job processing
are aborted mid-flight. This causes data inconsistency, stuck jobs, and lost
user funds.

## Implementation

### FILE: src/lib/shutdown.ts
```typescript
import { sql } from '@/db';
import { redis } from '@/lib/redis';
import { boss } from '@/jobs/manager';
import logger from '@/lib/logger';

let isShuttingDown = false;

export function setupGracefulShutdown() {
  const shutdown = async (signal: string) => {
    if (isShuttingDown) return;
    isShuttingDown = true;

    logger.info({ signal }, 'Graceful shutdown initiated');

    // 1. Stop accepting new HTTP requests
    // (Next.js handles this when process exits)

    // 2. Stop accepting new jobs
    await boss.stop({ graceful: true, timeout: 10000 });
    logger.info('Job queue stopped');

    // 3. Wait for in-flight jobs to complete (max 15s)
    const start = Date.now();
    while (Date.now() - start < 15000) {
      const active = await boss.getQueueSize();
      if (active === 0) break;
      await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 500));
    }

    // 4. Close database connections
    await sql.end({ timeout: 5 });
    logger.info('Database connections closed');

    // 5. Close Redis connections
    await redis.quit();
    logger.info('Redis connections closed');

    // 6. Flush logs
    logger.end();

    // 7. Exit
    process.exit(0);
  };

  process.on('SIGTERM', () => shutdown('SIGTERM'));
  process.on('SIGINT', () => shutdown('SIGINT'));
}
```

### FILE: src/worker.ts (update)
```typescript

```

## Docker Compose Update
```yaml

    # ... existing config ...
    stop_grace_period: 30s
    stop_signal: SIGTERM

  worker:
    # ... existing config ...
    stop_grace_period: 30s
    stop_signal: SIGTERM
```

# GAP 27: DETAILED HEALTH CHECK ENDPOINT
# ================================================================================

## Current Plan Status
P0.6 says "GET /api/health returns 200 with DB + Redis status" but has no
detail on what "status" means or what happens when a dependency is down.

## Implementation

### FILE: app/api/health/route.ts
```typescript
import { NextResponse } from 'next/server';
import { sql } from '@/db';
import { redis } from '@/lib/redis';
import { boss } from '@/jobs/manager';

interface HealthCheck {
  status: 'healthy' | 'degraded' | 'unhealthy';
  timestamp: string;
  version: string;
  checks: {
    database: { status: 'up' | 'down'; latencyMs: number };
    redis: { status: 'up' | 'down'; latencyMs: number };
    jobQueue: { status: 'up' | 'down'; pendingJobs: number };
    rpc: { status: 'up' | 'down'; latencyMs: number; slot: number };
    disk: { status: 'up' | 'down'; usagePercent: number };
    memory: { status: 'up' | 'down'; usagePercent: number };
  };
}

export const runtime = 'edge';

export async function GET() {
  const checks: HealthCheck['checks'] = {
    database: { status: 'down', latencyMs: 0 },
    redis: { status: 'down', latencyMs: 0 },
    jobQueue: { status: 'down', pendingJobs: 0 },
    rpc: { status: 'down', latencyMs: 0, slot: 0 },
    disk: { status: 'down', usagePercent: 0 },
    memory: { status: 'down', usagePercent: 0 },
  };

  // Database check
  const dbStart = Date.now();
  try {
    await sql`SELECT 1`;
    checks.database = { status: 'up', latencyMs: Date.now() - dbStart };
  } catch {
    checks.database = { status: 'down', latencyMs: Date.now() - dbStart };
  }

  // Redis check
  const redisStart = Date.now();
  try {
    await redis.ping();
    checks.redis = { status: 'up', latencyMs: Date.now() - redisStart };
  } catch {
    checks.redis = { status: 'down', latencyMs: Date.now() - redisStart };
  }

  // Job queue check
  try {
    const pending = await boss.getQueueSize();
    checks.jobQueue = { status: 'up', pendingJobs: pending };
  } catch {
    checks.jobQueue = { status: 'down', pendingJobs: 0 };
  }

  // RPC check
  const rpcStart = Date.now();
  try {
    const slot = await connection.getSlot();
    checks.rpc = { status: 'up', latencyMs: Date.now() - rpcStart, slot };
  } catch {
    checks.rpc = { status: 'down', latencyMs: Date.now() - rpcStart, slot: 0 };
  }

  // Disk check
  try {
    const { execSync } = require('child_process');
    const output = execSync('df / | awk "NR==2 {print \$5}"').toString().trim();
    const usage = parseInt(output.replace('%', ''));
    checks.disk = { status: usage > 90 ? 'down' : 'up', usagePercent: usage };
  } catch {
    checks.disk = { status: 'down', usagePercent: 0 };
  }

  // Memory check
  try {
    const total = require('os').totalmem();
    const free = require('os').freemem();
    const usage = Math.round(((total - free) / total) * 100);
    checks.memory = { status: usage > 90 ? 'down' : 'up', usagePercent: usage };
  } catch {
    checks.memory = { status: 'down', usagePercent: 0 };
  }

  // Determine overall status
  const downCount = Object.values(checks).filter((c) => c.status === 'down').length;
  const status: HealthCheck['status'] =
    downCount === 0 ? 'healthy' : downCount <= 2 ? 'degraded' : 'unhealthy';

  const response: HealthCheck = {
    status,
    timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
    version: process.env.npm_package_version || 'unknown',
    checks,
  };

  return NextResponse.json(response, {
    status: status === 'healthy' ? 200 : status === 'degraded' ? 200 : 503,
  });
}
```

# GAP 28: LOG ROTATION & RETENTION
# ================================================================================

## Why This Matters
Winston logs grow indefinitely. On a 200GB disk, unrotated logs can fill the
disk in weeks, causing the VM to crash.

## Implementation

### FILE: scripts/logrotate-osiris
```bash
# /etc/logrotate.d/osiris
/var/log/osiris/*.log {
  daily
  rotate 14
  compress
  delaycompress
  missingok
  notifempty
  create 0644 osiris osiris
  postrotate
    # Signal PM2 to reopen log files
    pm2 reloadLogs
  endscript
}
```

### FILE: src/lib/logger.ts (update)
```typescript
import winston from 'winston';
import path from 'path';

const logDir = process.env.LOG_DIR || '/var/log/osiris';

export const logger = winston.createLogger({
  level: process.env.LOG_LEVEL || 'info',
  format: winston.format.combine(
    winston.format.timestamp(),
    winston.format.errors({ stack: true }),
    winston.format.json()
  ),
  defaultMeta: {
    service: 'osiris',
    version: process.env.npm_package_version,
  },
  transports: [
    // Console for development
    new winston.transports.Console({
      format: winston.format.combine(
        winston.format.colorize(),
        winston.format.simple()
      ),
    }),
    // File for production (rotated by logrotate)
    new winston.transports.File({
      filename: path.join(logDir, 'app.log'),
      maxsize: 10 * 1024 * 1024, // 10MB internal rotation as backup
      maxFiles: 5,
    }),
    new winston.transports.File({
      filename: path.join(logDir, 'error.log'),
      level: 'error',
      maxsize: 10 * 1024 * 1024,
      maxFiles: 5,
    }),
  ],
  // Reject logs with secrets
  rejectionHandlers: [
    new winston.transports.File({ filename: path.join(logDir, 'rejections.log') }),
  ],
});

// Prevent logging secrets
const SECRET_PATTERNS = [
  /api[_-]?key/i,
  /password/i,
  /secret/i,
  /private[_-]?key/i,
  /token/i,
];

const originalLog = logger.log.bind(logger);
logger.log = (level: string, message: any, ...args: any[]) => {
  const msgStr = typeof message === 'string' ? message : JSON.stringify(message);
  for (const pattern of SECRET_PATTERNS) {
    if (pattern.test(msgStr)) {
      logger.warn('Attempted to log sensitive data — blocked');
      return;
    }
  }
  return originalLog(level, message, ...args);
};

export default logger;
```

- UPDATE: P0.8 — Security Controls — add log rotation to logger deliverables
- NEW file: scripts/logrotate-osiris

```typescript
import { z } from 'zod';

const envSchema = z.object({
  NODE_ENV: z.enum(['development', 'staging', 'production']).default('development'),
  DATABASE_URL: z.string().min(1),
  REDIS_URL: z.string().min(1),
  HELIUS_RPC_URL: z.string().url(),
  HELIUS_API_KEY: z.string().min(1),
  JUPITER_API_KEY: z.string().min(1),
  BETTER_AUTH_SECRET: z.string().min(32),
  TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN: z.string().min(1),
  SIGNER_WORKER_URL: z.string().url(),
});

const parsed = envSchema.safeParse(process.env);

if (!parsed.success) {
  console.error('Invalid environment variables:', parsed.error.format());
  process.exit(1);
}

export const config = {
  ...parsed.data,

  // Environment-specific defaults
  isDev: parsed.data.NODE_ENV === 'development',
  isStaging: parsed.data.NODE_ENV === 'staging',
  isProd: parsed.data.NODE_ENV === 'production',

  // Derived values
  logLevel: parsed.data.NODE_ENV === 'production' ? 'info' : 'debug',

  // Feature flags (environment-based)
  tradingEnabled: parsed.data.NODE_ENV === 'production' ? false : true,

  // Rate limits
  rateLimits: {
    auth: { max: 5, window: 60 },      // 5 attempts per minute
    trade: { max: 10, window: 60 },    // 10 trades per minute
    copy: { max: 5, window: 60 },      // 5 copy trades per minute
    webhook: { max: 100, window: 60 }, // 100 webhooks per minute
  },

  // Timeouts
  timeouts: {
    rpc: parsed.data.NODE_ENV === 'production' ? 10000 : 30000,
    db: 5000,
    redis: 2000,
    job: 30000,
  },

  // Retry config
  retries: {
    rpc: 3,
    db: 3,
    trade: 3,
  },
} as const;
```

## Why This Matters
When you need to change an API endpoint, you can't break existing clients
(Telegram bot, web dashboard, mobile apps). Versioning prevents this.

## Implementation

```typescript
  //   trade: tradeRouterV2,
```

### FILE: app/api/v1/[trpc]/route.ts
```typescript

import { appRouter } from '@/server/routers/_app';

const handler = (req: Request) =>
  fetchRequestHandler({
    endpoint: '/api/v1/trpc',
    req,
    router: appRouter,
    createContext: () => ({}),
  });

export { handler as GET, handler as POST };
```

### Versioning Rules
1. **URL path versioning**: `/api/v1/...`, `/api/v2/...`
2. **Backward compatibility**: v1 endpoints NEVER change behavior
3. **Deprecation**: Mark old versions with `Sunset` header 90 days before removal
4. **Client support**: Telegram bot and web dashboard pin to a version

# ================================================================================
# GAP 31: DATABASE MIGRATION ROLLBACK PROCEDURE
# ================================================================================

## Why This Matters
A bad migration can corrupt data. You need a tested rollback path for every
migration before applying it to production.

## Implementation

### FILE: scripts/migrate-with-rollback.sh
```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -e

ENV=${1:-development}
BACKUP_FILE="/backups/pre-migration-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).sql"

echo "Creating pre-migration backup..."
docker exec osiris-db pg_dump -U osiris osiris > "$BACKUP_FILE"
echo "Backup created: $BACKUP_FILE"

echo "Running migration..."
if ! pnpm db:migrate; then
  echo "Migration failed! Rolling back..."
  docker exec -i osiris-db psql -U osiris osiris < "$BACKUP_FILE"
  echo "Rollback complete."
  exit 1
fi

echo "Migration successful."
echo "To rollback: docker exec -i osiris-db psql -U osiris osiris < $BACKUP_FILE"
```

### FILE: src/db/migrations/README.md
```markdown
# Migration Rules

1. Every migration MUST have a rollback in the same file
2. Rollbacks are tested on staging before production
3. Migrations run during low-traffic windows (00:00-06:00 UTC)
4. Backups are created before every production migration
5. Destructive migrations (column drops) use expand-contract pattern:
   - Migration 1: Add new column, start writing to both
   - Migration 2: Backfill old column to new
   - Migration 3: Switch reads to new column
   - Migration 4: Drop old column
```

- UPDATE: P0.2 — Database Layer — add rollback procedure

# ================================================================================
# GAP 33: TOKEN PRICE FEED STRATEGY
# ================================================================================

## Why This Matters
PNL computation, slippage protection, and copy trading all need accurate
token prices. The plan mentions Birdeye/DexScreener but has no implementation.

## Implementation

### FILE: src/services/prices/feed.ts
```typescript
import { z } from 'zod';

const PriceSchema = z.object({
  mint: z.string(),
  priceSol: z.number(),
  priceUsd: z.number(),
  timestamp: z.number(),
  source: z.enum(['jupiter', 'birdeye', 'dexscreener']),
});

type Price = z.infer<typeof PriceSchema>;

class PriceFeed {
  private cache = new Map<string, Price>();
  private readonly CACHE_TTL = 30000; // 30 seconds

  async getPrice(mint: string): Promise<Price | null> {
    // 1. Check cache
    const cached = this.cache.get(mint);
    if (cached && Date.now() - cached.timestamp < this.CACHE_TTL) {
      return cached;
    }

    // 2. Fetch from Jupiter Price API (free, no API key needed)
    try {
      const price = await this.fetchFromJupiter(mint);
      this.cache.set(mint, price);
      return price;
    } catch {
      // 3. Fallback to Birdeye
      try {
        const price = await this.fetchFromBirdeye(mint);
        this.cache.set(mint, price);
        return price;
      } catch {
        // 4. Fallback to DexScreener
        return this.fetchFromDexScreener(mint);
      }
    }
  }

  private async fetchFromJupiter(mint: string): Promise<Price> {
    const res = await fetch(`https://price.jup.ag/v6/price?ids=${mint}`);
    const data = await res.json();

    return PriceSchema.parse({
      mint,
      priceSol: data.data[mint]?.price || 0,
      priceUsd: data.data[mint]?.price || 0,
      timestamp: Date.now(),
      source: 'jupiter',
    });
  }

  private async fetchFromBirdeye(mint: string): Promise<Price> {
    const res = await fetch(`https://public-api.birdeye.so/public/price?address=${mint}`, {
      headers: { 'X-API-KEY': process.env.BIRDEYE_API_KEY || '' },
    });
    const data = await res.json();

    return PriceSchema.parse({
      mint,
      priceSol: data.data?.value || 0,
      priceUsd: data.data?.value || 0,
      timestamp: Date.now(),
      source: 'birdeye',
    });
  }

  private async fetchFromDexScreener(mint: string): Promise<Price | null> {
    const res = await fetch(`https://api.dexscreener.com/latest/dex/tokens/${mint}`);
    const data = await res.json();
    const pair = data.pairs?.[0];

    if (!pair) return null;

    return PriceSchema.parse({
      mint,
      priceSol: parseFloat(pair.priceNative) || 0,
      priceUsd: parseFloat(pair.priceUsd) || 0,
      timestamp: Date.now(),
      source: 'dexscreener',
    });
  }
}

export const priceFeed = new PriceFeed();
```

- NEW section: P5.11 — Token Price Feed Strategy
- NEW file: src/services/prices/feed.ts
- UPDATE: P5.3 — PNL Computation — use priceFeed for unrealized PNL

# ================================================================================
# GAP 34: SESSION TIMEOUT AND CLEANUP
# ================================================================================

## Why This Matters
Active trading sessions that never expire are a security risk. A user who
forgets to revoke a session leaves their wallet exposed indefinitely.

## Implementation

### FILE: src/services/trading/session-cleanup.ts
```typescript
import { sql } from '@/db';
import { redis } from '@/lib/redis';
import logger from '@/lib/logger';

const SESSION_MAX_AGE = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000; // 24 hours
const CLEANUP_INTERVAL = 60 * 60 * 1000; // 1 hour

export async function cleanupExpiredSessions() {
  const now = new Date();

  // 1. Find expired sessions
  const expired = await sql`
    SELECT id, user_id FROM trading_sessions
    WHERE status = 'active'
    AND (expires_at < ${now} OR created_at < ${new Date(now.getTime() - SESSION_MAX_AGE)})
  `;

  for (const session of expired) {
    // 2. Revoke session
    await sql`
      UPDATE trading_sessions
      SET status = 'expired', revoked_at = ${now}
      WHERE id = ${session.id}
    `;

    // 3. Cancel in-flight jobs
    await sql`
      UPDATE pgboss.job
      SET state = 'cancelled'
      WHERE name LIKE 'trade:%'
      AND data->>'sessionId' = ${session.id}
      AND state IN ('created', 'retry')
    `;

    // 4. Notify user
    await redis.publish('notifications', JSON.stringify({
      type: 'session_expired',
      userId: session.user_id,
      sessionId: session.id,
    }));

    logger.info({ sessionId: session.id }, 'Expired session cleaned up');
  }
}

// Run cleanup every hour
export function startSessionCleanup() {
  setInterval(cleanupExpiredSessions, CLEANUP_INTERVAL);
  cleanupExpiredSessions(); // Initial run
}
```

- NEW section: P1.7 — Trading Session Management (update)
- NEW file: src/services/trading/session-cleanup.ts

# ================================================================================
# GAP 35: WEBHOOK SECURITY BEYOND SIGNATURE VERIFICATION
# ================================================================================

## Why This Matters
Helius webhook signature verification (P4.1) is necessary but not sufficient.
You also need: IP allowlisting, replay attack prevention, payload size limits,
and timeout handling.

## Implementation

### FILE: app/api/webhooks/helius/route.ts (update)
```typescript
import { NextResponse } from 'next/server';
import { createHmac } from 'crypto';

const HELIUS_IPS = ['34.102.136.180', '34.102.137.0/24']; // Helius egress IPs
const MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE = 1024 * 1024; // 1MB
const WEBHOOK_TIMEOUT = 30000; // 30 seconds

export async function POST(req: Request) {
  // 1. IP allowlist check
  const clientIp = req.headers.get('x-forwarded-for') || 'unknown';
  if (!isAllowedIp(clientIp)) {
    return NextResponse.json({ error: 'UNAUTHORIZED_IP' }, { status: 403 });
  }

  // 2. Payload size check
  const contentLength = parseInt(req.headers.get('content-length') || '0');
  if (contentLength > MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE) {
    return NextResponse.json({ error: 'PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE' }, { status: 413 });
  }

  // 3. Signature verification (existing)
  const signature = req.headers.get('x-helius-signature');
  const body = await req.text();

  if (!verifyHeliusSignature(signature, body)) {
    return NextResponse.json({ error: 'INVALID_SIGNATURE' }, { status: 401 });
  }

  // 4. Replay attack prevention (nonce/timestamp)
  const payload = JSON.parse(body);
  if (await isDuplicateWebhook(payload.signature)) {
    return NextResponse.json({ error: 'DUPLICATE_WEBHOOK' }, { status: 200 });
  }

  // 5. Timeout handling
  const timeoutPromise = new Promise((_, reject) =>
    setTimeout(() => reject(new Error('TIMEOUT')), WEBHOOK_TIMEOUT)
  );

  try {
    await Promise.race([
      processWebhookEvent(payload),
      timeoutPromise,
    ]);
    return NextResponse.json({ success: true });
  } catch (err) {
    logger.error({ error: err, signature: payload.signature }, 'Webhook processing failed');
    return NextResponse.json({ error: 'PROCESSING_FAILED' }, { status: 500 });
  }
}

function isAllowedIp(ip: string): boolean {
  // Implement IP allowlist matching
  return HELIUS_IPS.some((allowed) => ip.startsWith(allowed.replace('/24', '')));
}

async function isDuplicateWebhook(signature: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const exists = await redis.get(`webhook:${signature}`);
  if (exists) return true;
  await redis.setex(`webhook:${signature}`, 3600, '1');
  return false;
}
```

- UPDATE: P4.1 — Helius Webhook Setup — add IP allowlist, replay protection, size limits
